ess.Ess.Support.reinforce: Spawns opts.units on a 3-wide, 4-unit-spaced grid around (x,y,z). opts.deliver selects the mode: "copter" spawns every unit at once via MrxCopterDrop.Create (template guarded by Ess.Safe.template to prevent a blank-template hard crash past pcall); "paradrop" flies a transport flyby then spawns each unit 1.5+0.2*i seconds later via the same direct spawn as below (no literal parachute object); anything else/omitted spawns all units immediately via Ess.Object.spawn. opts.faction (default "VZ") maps to a 2-letter code used only by the copter path.
ess.Ess.Support.shell: Spawns one falling shell via Airstrike.SpawnOrdnance, dropped from opts.dropHeight (default 220) above (x,y,z) with straight-down velocity, impact-fused. Optional opts: ammo (default "Gunship Shell"), owner (faction name for damage/kill attribution). This is the primitive artillery repeatedly calls; the other Support functions compose different natives directly instead.

Ess.Table.compact.doc: Rebuilds a numeric array densely, mutating t in place (and returning it). Fixes the real bug where t[#t] = nil leaves a nil hole that desyncs #/ipairs/table.insert; non-numeric keys are left untouched.
Ess.Table.compact.gotcha: Rebuilds a numeric array densely because a nil hole desyncs `#t` from ipairs -- ipairs stops at the first gap while # may report a larger length, so data silently disappears instead of erroring.

Ess.Table.contains.doc: Scans a whole table for a value equal to `val`. Uses pairs, so values stored under string keys are searched too.

Ess.Table.copy.doc: Duplicates a table one level deep, copying every key from the source (pairs, so map keys come along too).
Ess.Table.copy.ret: A new table with the same keys and values.
Ess.Table.copy.gotcha: Shallow. Nested tables are shared with the original, not cloned, so mutating a sub-table changes both copies.

Ess.Table.count.doc: Counts every entry in a table, including the string keys that `#t` cannot see. Reach for it whenever a table is used as a set or a map rather than a list.

Ess.Table.filter.doc: Builds a new array holding only the array elements for which fn(value, index) returns truthy.
Ess.Table.filter.ret: A new, densely packed array - dropped elements leave no holes, so #result is always accurate.

Ess.Table.find.doc: Returns the first array element for which fn(value, index) is truthy, together with where it was found. Use it when you want the matching item itself rather than a yes/no.
Ess.Table.find.ret: value, index - or nil when nothing matches.

Ess.Table.indexOf.doc: Finds where a value sits in the array part of a table.
Ess.Table.indexOf.ret: The 1-based index of the first match, or nil when the value is not there.
Ess.Table.indexOf.gotcha: Walks only the array part (ipairs), so a value stored under a string key is never found. Use Ess.Table.contains for a whole-table search.

Ess.Table.isEmpty.doc: Reports whether a table holds nothing at all, array part or map part. Cheaper than counting because it only asks for the first key.

ess.Ess.Table.keys: Every key in t, array or not, order unspecified.

Ess.Table.map.doc: Builds a new array by running fn(value, index) over each element of the array part and keeping the result. The source table is left untouched.
Ess.Table.map.ret: A new array with one entry per array element of the source.

Ess.Table.merge.doc: Copies src's keys onto dst, with src winning on any collision. The usual way to layer caller-supplied options over a table of defaults.
Ess.Table.merge.ret: dst itself, so the call can be chained.
Ess.Table.merge.gotcha: Mutates dst in place - the only non-pure helper in this group - and copies only one level deep. A nil src is treated as an empty table rather than an error.

Ess.Table.reduce.doc: Folds the array part down to a single value: the accumulator starts at init and becomes fn(acc, value, index) for each element. Use it to sum, find a maximum, or build a string from a list.
Ess.Table.reduce.ret: The final accumulator - or init unchanged when the array part is empty.

Ess.Table.reverse.doc: Builds a new array with the order of the array part flipped end for end. The source is left alone.
Ess.Table.reverse.ret: A new array of the same length, reversed.

Ess.Table.slice.doc: Extracts elements i through j of the array part, 1-based and inclusive, into a new array. i defaults to 1 and j to #t, and both are clamped to the real bounds.
Ess.Table.slice.ret: A new array of the selected elements (empty if the range collapses).

Ess.Table.values.doc: Collects every value in a table into a new array, walking the whole table with pairs so map-style string keys are included, not just the array part.
Ess.Table.values.ret: A new array holding the values.
Ess.Table.values.gotcha: pairs has no defined order, so the result's ordering is arbitrary even when the source looked like a list.

Ess.TextConsole.close.doc: Closes the text console, stops its polling loop, hides the widget and gives the player their controls back if they were locked.
Ess.TextConsole.close.gotcha: Returns immediately when the console is not open, so calling it defensively is free.

Ess.TextConsole.open.doc: Opens the plain text-entry console - a prompt line the player types into, needing no .gfx asset. opts takes text (initial buffer), prompt (default "> "), max (default 200), lockPlayer (default true) and the onSubmit / onCancel / onChange callbacks. Buffered key events are drained first so the key that opened it does not leak into the buffer.
Ess.TextConsole.open.gotcha: Enter fires onSubmit and clears the buffer but leaves the console OPEN; only Escape or Ess.TextConsole.close actually closes it. With lockPlayer left at its default the player cannot move until then.

Ess.Time.clock.doc: Returns a clock object with a :delta() method, an auto-advancing per-frame timer. maxDelta defaults to 0.25 seconds.
Ess.Time.clock.gotcha: Auto-advancing: :delta() returns the time since its OWN last :delta() call and clamps it (default 0.25s), so a long pause or hitch can't blow up per-tick math. Don't mix it with the explicit stamp/elapsed flavour -- elapsed() never advances on its own, which is what makes a cooldown check idempotent.

ess.Ess.Time.cooldown: Returns a ready() function that is true (and re-marks) at most once per seconds window, false otherwise without re-marking so a retry doesn't push the window back. The first call is always ready.
ess.Ess.Time.elapsed: Returns seconds since the stamp was marked (Sys.TimeStampGetElapsed), or 0. since() is a plain alias for the same function.
ess.Ess.Time.format: Formats a raw seconds value (e.g. from elapsed()) into a HUD-ready display string via Junk.FormatTime.
ess.Ess.Time.mark: Re-marks an existing stamp handle in place (Sys.TimeStampMark). Every confirmed call site re-marks a stamp previously produced by stamp()/mainStamp() rather than creating a new one each time.
ess.Ess.Time.restoreScale: Convenience for scale(1) — undoes slow-motion under a clearer name.
ess.Ess.Time.scale: Sets the world time scale via Sys.SetTimeScale(n) — confirmed idiom for slow-motion, e.g. Ess.Time.scale(0.2) for a 5x slowdown.

Ess.Time.stamp.doc: Creates a real-world time stamp via Sys.RealTimeStamp (pcall-guarded). Keeps advancing through world-pause and slow-motion, unlike mainStamp().
Ess.Time.stamp.gotcha: The REAL-WORLD clock -- it survives world-pause (menus/PDA), unlike Event.TimerRelative's own delta. Use Ess.Time.mainStamp for a gameplay cooldown that should freeze with the game.

Ess.Track.new.doc: Creates a new tracker object; each :xxx() method on it both registers a teardown for that thing and returns the value you gave it, so you can wrap a spawn/creation call inline without an extra local variable.
Ess.Track.new.gotcha: Every Add.../Remove... pair on this engine is leak-prone: the handle is only accepted by its own matching Remove call, and there is NO clear-all native for ANY of them (Event, Marker, radar/PDA blips, quality refs, disposers, context actions). Register handles here at creation time, not at teardown time.

ess.Ess.Triggers.arm: Passthrough to Ess.Raw.Triggers.arm; stays a bare top-level call because it's stateless and never names or shares state.

Ess.Triggers.scope.doc: Returns an isolated named-trigger/gate namespace with its own private known/fired id tables, so two independent scopes can't collide even if they reuse the same ids. Ess.Contract gives each running contract instance its own scope.
Ess.Triggers.scope.gotcha: Named trigger ids and gate inputs cross-reference BY NAME, so a single shared registry lets two unrelated systems both using an id like "start" silently satisfy each other's gates. Take your own scope per independent group of triggers -- the collision is then impossible by construction.

Ess.UI.Bar.doc: Builds a labelled progress bar - health, a capture timer, a download meter. opts takes x/y/w/h, label and value.
Ess.UI.Bar.ret: The bar object: :set(v), :label(s), plus the shared :show/:hide/:focus/:blur/:destroy.
Ess.UI.Bar.gotcha: :set takes a FRACTION from 0 to 1, not a percentage, and clamps - passing 50 pins the bar at full.

Ess.UI.Board.doc: Builds the two-pane browse board: a scrolling item list on the left and a detail pane on the right, fed by :detail{ category, rewards, objectives, progress, progressText }. Built for contract browsing but reusable for any list-plus-details screen. opts takes x/y/w/h, title, hint, items, detail, empty, focus and the onSelect / onChoose / onBack callbacks.
Ess.UI.Board.ret: The board object: :items(t), :selected() -> item, index, :select(i), :detail(d), :title(s), :hint(s), plus the shared :show/:hide/:focus/:blur/:destroy.
Ess.UI.Board.gotcha: Unlike Ess.UI.List, the selection does NOT wrap at the ends, and both :items() and :select() fire onSelect immediately as a side effect.

Ess.UI.Chat.doc: Builds the chat/log widget: a scrolling message area showing the last five wrapped lines, plus an optional typed input line. opts takes x/y/w/h, title, max (backlog, default 60), autoHide (seconds) and onSubmit.
Ess.UI.Chat.ret: The chat object: :push(text), :prompt(onSubmit), :clear(), :title(s), plus the shared :show/:hide/:focus/:blur/:destroy.
Ess.UI.Chat.gotcha: opts.autoHide only starts counting after a :push, so an idle box with no messages never fades. The widget resizes itself to the number of visible lines, capped at five however large the backlog is.

Ess.UI.Confirm.doc: Shows the modal yes/no prompt and calls opts.onResult(true or false) with the answer. opts takes title, text, yes, no and onResult; focus is restored to whatever held it when the prompt resolves.
Ess.UI.Confirm.gotcha: One shared instance serves the whole framework - opening a second Confirm overwrites the first's callback, which is then never called. The highlight starts on NO, and Escape resolves as false.

Ess.UI.Input.doc: Shows the modal single-line text prompt: Enter fires opts.onSubmit(text), Escape fires opts.onCancel, and focus returns to whatever held it before. opts takes prompt, text (initial value), max (default 120), onSubmit and onCancel.
Ess.UI.Input.gotcha: One shared instance for the whole framework, so a second Input replaces the first's callbacks. Only characters Ess.Input.VkToChar can map are accepted, which means a US keyboard layout.

Ess.UI.List.doc: Builds the scrolling, keyboard-driven selection list widget. opts takes x/y/w/h, title, crumb, hint, items, empty (the text shown for an empty list), focus, and the onChoose / onBack / onSelect callbacks. Each item is a table with a `label`, or a `header` for a non-selectable section caption.
Ess.UI.List.ret: The list object: :items(t), :selected() -> item, index, :select(i), :title/:crumb/:hint, plus the shared :show/:hide/:focus/:blur/:destroy.
Ess.UI.List.gotcha: Shows 10 rows at a time and WRAPS at both ends - pressing down on the last row jumps to the first. Header entries are skipped by every move and can never become the selection.

ess.Ess.UI.Menu: Declarative drill-down menu constructor (ForgeMenu-style). Options: title, id (defaults to title), key (toggle key, display only), x/y (default 40, 60), onClose.

Ess.UI.Panel.doc: Builds a simple text panel of up to eight lines - the readout widget for a stats display or a dev overlay. opts takes x/y/w/h, title and lines.
Ess.UI.Panel.ret: The panel object: :title(s), :line(i, s), :fit(n), :clear(), plus the shared :show/:hide/:focus/:blur/:destroy.
Ess.UI.Panel.gotcha: Lines are indexed 0..7, not 1..8. Writing a non-blank line auto-grows the panel to fit, but it never shrinks on its own - call :fit or :clear to pull it back in.

Ess.UI.Toast.doc: Pops a short, self-expiring notification in the corner of the screen. Text is word-wrapped to two lines, and the toast claims a free slot or, if all are busy, the one expiring soonest. opts takes ttl (seconds, default Ess.UI.TOAST_TTL).
Ess.UI.Toast.ret: The toast object, which offers :dismiss() to clear it early.
Ess.UI.Toast.gotcha: Only Ess.UI.TOAST_SLOTS (3 by default) toasts exist, so a burst of messages overwrites itself. Anything past the second wrapped line is dropped without a hint.

ess.Ess.Vec.dir: Unit direction from A to B (normalize(sub(B, A))).
ess.Ess.Vec.lerp: Interpolates between two positions. Powers Ess.Easy.Camera's follow-damping (via per-tick easing rather than snapping), confirmed working live in that consumer even though Ess.Vec itself is only offline-verified.
ess.Ess.Vec.normalize: Unit vector of (x,y,z); a zero-length input returns 0,0,0 rather than NaN.

Ess.Vec.sub.doc: Component-wise subtraction of the second point from the first, giving the vector that points from point 2 to point 1.
Ess.Vec.sub.ret: Three values: the difference x, y, z.
Ess.Vec.sub.gotcha: Same multi-return caveat as the rest of Ess.Vec - it only expands in full as the last argument of a call.

ess.Ess.Vec.toward: The point dist units from A toward B.

Ess.Vehicle.enterBestSeat.doc: pcall-wrapped MrxUtil.EnterBestAvailableSeat — confirmed driver/gunner/passenger/cargo seat priority order.
Ess.Vehicle.enterBestSeat.gotcha: Flagged caution (unconfirmed causally but repeatable enough to record): immediately after a Pg.Spawn + enterBestSeat from INSIDE an interior cell, the very next bridge chunk -- even a bare `return 1+1` -- stalled the Lua tick for 30+ seconds with the process still alive, recoverable only by killing the game. Avoid spawning and entering a vehicle from inside an interior.

Ess.Vehicle.enterSeatExcluding.doc: Puts a character into the best free seat of a vehicle while refusing the seat types you list. Tries driver, gunner, passenger, cargo in that order ("d", "g", "p", "c") and takes the first one it can actually board - the way to load passengers without letting them steal the wheel.
Ess.Vehicle.enterSeatExcluding.ret: true plus the seat-type letter that was taken, or false, nil when every allowed seat failed.

ess.Ess.Vehicle.exit: Confirmed signature+usage from DestroyerTool.lua: calls Vehicle.Exit(uVehicle, uCharacter, true).
ess.Ess.Vehicle.flyTo: Sends an AI helicopter to a world point via Ai.Deliver(driver, x, y, z, dropHeight, careless) — not Ai.Goal "MoveToPos", which does not fly a heli. Since a freshly-spawned heli has no driver for a moment, this polls Ess.Vehicle.driver until one exists before issuing the order. opts.height (default 0.5), opts.careless, opts.onReady(driver) fire once the order is issued; returns cancel() to stop the driver-wait early.
ess.Ess.Vehicle.followGhost: Spawns a template and returns a ghost object (ghost.guid, ghost:update(nx,ny,nz), ghost:remove()). Object.SetPosition silently fails to move a spawned human, so update() tries SetPosition then re-reads the real position; if still off by more than ~3 units it despawns/respawns the template instead, updating ghost.guid so callers always read the current handle.

Ess.Vehicle.riders.doc: Everyone currently aboard a vehicle, driver and passengers alike.
Ess.Vehicle.riders.ret: An array of character guids - empty when there is nobody, never nil.
Ess.Vehicle.riders.gotcha: An empty table also means "the read failed", so a zero length does not prove the vehicle is really empty.

ess.Ess.Vehicle.seatOf: Returns which seat a character currently occupies, if any. Together with driver/riders this collapses a 7-getter native overlap down to the 3 shapes actually needed day to day.

Ess.Followers.recruit.gotcha: Ess.AIOrders' own follow behaviour never reverts the Ai feeling / LivingWorld / Vip state it sets when following ends -- that's the gap this closes. Use dismiss() rather than just dropping the guid, or that state stays applied.

Ess.Pursuit.capLevel.gotcha: A SESSION-LENGTH COMMITMENT, not a tunable: Pg.SetMaxPursuitLevel is a one-way ratchet down and nothing raises the ceiling back up -- only a save-load or restart resets it. This logs a loud warning on every call for that reason.

Ess.Pursuit.restrictAll.gotcha: Gates ORGANIC AI escalation only -- it does not clear an active pursuit and does not block a scripted .start(), despite the name. Ess.Pursuit.clear() is the only off switch for a live chase.

Ess.Pursuit.start.gotcha: Starting a pursuit spawns NOTHING to chase you -- PlayerState stays "Stopped" until faction units actually engage on their own. A real countdown is seeded (~400s at level 3), so the state reads active even while nothing is happening.

Ess.Safe.reject.gotcha: Records the OTHER kind of silence: a GUARD REJECTION, where Ess inspected the arguments and returned early WITHOUT ever calling the engine -- no throw for a pcall to catch, no log line, no effect. This is the common failure channel in practice, so a diagnostic built only on caught errors is quiet exactly when you need it; set Ess.DEBUG = true to surface both.

Ess.lastError.gotcha: Only reports the most recent SWALLOWED failure -- and on this engine most bad calls never throw at all (14 deliberately-malformed native calls across nine namespaces produced ZERO Lua errors), so a nil here does not mean nothing went wrong. Check Ess.Safe.stats() and guard rejections too.

Ess.stop.gotcha: Exists because Ess grew 27 teardown verbs across five structurally different disposal idioms (returned closure, opaque handle table, caller-supplied id string, object with :cancel, tracker with :closeAll). If you're holding a handle and just want it gone, use this rather than guessing which namespace spells teardown which way.

Ess.Math.lerp.doc: Blends between a and b by t: 0 gives a, 1 gives b, 0.5 the midpoint. The workhorse for easing a value over time - a fade amount, a camera FOV, a bar fill.
Ess.Math.lerp.gotcha: t is not clamped, so a value outside 0..1 extrapolates past the endpoints instead of stopping there.

Ess.Math.sign.doc: Reduces a number to just its direction, discarding magnitude. Handy for turning a difference into a step direction.
Ess.Math.sign.ret: 1 when positive, -1 when negative, 0 when exactly zero.

Ess.Vec.length.doc: Magnitude of a 3D vector given as three loose components - how long a direction/velocity/offset is.
Ess.Vec.length.ret: The length as a single number.

Ess.Vec.scale.doc: Multiplies each component of a vector by s. The usual way to turn a unit direction into a shove of a given strength before feeding it to Ess.Object.impulse.
Ess.Vec.scale.ret: Three values: the scaled x, y, z.
Ess.Vec.scale.gotcha: Returns three separate values, so it expands fully only as the LAST argument of a call. Nesting it inside another Vec call passes just x - capture into locals first.

Ess.Vec.dot.doc: Dot product of two 3D vectors. With unit directions, the sign answers "are these two roughly pointing the same way" - positive means yes, negative means opposed, zero means perpendicular.

Ess.Player.viewYaw.doc: The bearing the player is LOOKING along, worked out from whatever the reticle is aimed at - as opposed to the chest/body yaw that Ess.Player.pose returns as its 4th value. Stand still and swing the mouse and these two diverge, so this is the one that matches what the player perceives as "in front of me".
Ess.Player.viewYaw.ret: yaw in degrees plus a boolean that is true when the bearing came from a real reticle hit; nil, false when the player has no character.
Ess.Player.viewYaw.gotcha: Aiming at open sky, or at something closer than 3 units, silently falls back to the body yaw and returns false as the second value. You always get a usable yaw, so branch on that flag if the difference matters to you.

Ess.Object.setHealth.doc: Sets an object's health outright, without any damage event. Use it to top a unit back up or to soften something before a scripted kill.
Ess.Object.setHealth.gotcha: Silent on failure - an invalid guid is a no-op with no return value to check.

Ess.Object.enablePhysics.doc: Turns the engine's physics simulation back on for one object, so it falls, collides and reacts to impulses again.
Ess.Object.enablePhysics.gotcha: Silent on failure, and nothing is returned.

Ess.Object.disablePhysics.doc: Freezes one object out of the physics simulation - useful for pinning a prop in place for a cutscene or stopping a spawned vehicle from rolling away.
Ess.Object.disablePhysics.gotcha: Silent on failure, and nothing is returned.

Ess.Object.speed.doc: How fast an object is currently moving, as a single scalar. One native call plus a square root.
Ess.Object.speed.ret: The speed, or nil when the velocity could not be read (dead or invalid guid).
Ess.Object.speed.gotcha: For a plain threshold test ("is it moving faster than X") use Ess.Object.speedSq against X*X instead - it skips the square root.

Ess.Vehicle.driver.doc: The character currently in the driver's seat of a vehicle. AI orders must target the driver, not the hull, so this is how you get a usable actor guid out of a vehicle.
Ess.Vehicle.driver.ret: The driver's guid, or nil when the seat is empty or the read failed.

Ess.Human.disableWeapons.doc: Stops a character using weapons at all - what you want for a scripted escort, a surrendering unit, or a character walking through a cutscene.
Ess.Human.disableWeapons.gotcha: Silent on failure and returns nothing. Pair every call with Ess.Human.enableWeapons or the character stays disarmed for the rest of the session.

Ess.Human.enableWeapons.doc: Gives a character its weapons back after Ess.Human.disableWeapons.
Ess.Human.enableWeapons.gotcha: Silent on failure and returns nothing.

Ess.TextConsole.isOpen.doc: Whether the text console is currently accepting input. Use it to avoid stacking a second prompt on top of a live one.

Ess.SaveVar.get.doc: Reads a value previously written through this namespace, falling back to `default` when the key has never been set.
Ess.SaveVar.get.ret: The stored value, or `default` when nothing is stored.

Ess.SaveVar.set.doc: Writes a value under this namespace's prefix. The store persists across full game restarts (it lives in lua_loader_data.ini), unlike Ess.State which only survives a script re-run.
Ess.SaveVar.set.gotcha: The underlying store only holds numbers, strings and booleans - a table will not survive the round trip.

Ess.SaveVar.setFlag.doc: Stores a key as a real boolean, coercing anything truthy to true. The write half of the persistent unlock-flag idiom, with :flag(key) as the read.

Ess.Keys.isBound.doc: Whether a key already has a handler bound to it. Accepts either a friendly name ("f5", "escape", "a") or a raw virtual-key number.
Ess.Keys.isBound.gotcha: A key name the parser does not recognise also returns false, which is indistinguishable from a real key that simply has nothing bound.

Ess.Raw.Mark.removeRadar.doc: Removes a radar objective marker using the NAME that Ess.Raw.Mark.radar returned - the radar API removes by name, not by handle. A nil name is a silent no-op.
Ess.Raw.Mark.removeRadar.gotcha: Returns nothing, and a name that was never registered fails silently inside the pcall.

Ess.Raw.Mark.removePda.doc: Removes a PDA map blip using the NAME that Ess.Raw.Mark.pda returned - like the radar surface, the PDA removes by name. A nil name is a silent no-op.
Ess.Raw.Mark.removePda.gotcha: Returns nothing and swallows any failure.

Ess.Raw.Mark.removeWorld.doc: Removes a floating in-world icon using the handle Ess.Raw.Mark.world returned.
Ess.Raw.Mark.removeWorld.gotcha: This one takes a HANDLE, unlike its radar and PDA siblings which take a name string. Passing the wrong kind is a silent no-op.

Ess.UI.comma.doc: Formats a number with thousands separators - 1234567 becomes "1,234,567" - for cash, score and ammo readouts.
Ess.UI.comma.gotcha: Floors to an integer first, so any fractional part is dropped rather than rounded, and a non-number argument silently becomes 0.

Ess.UI.fmt_time.doc: Formats a count of seconds as M:SS for a countdown or elapsed-time readout.
Ess.UI.fmt_time.gotcha: Minutes never roll over into hours and are never zero-padded, so 3700 seconds reads "61:40".

Ess.UI.navName.doc: Maps a virtual-key code to the semantic navigation direction it means, reading the remappable Ess.UI.KEYS table. Every Ess.UI widget's key handler starts with this call, which is why rebinding Ess.UI.KEYS.up retargets the whole kit at once.
Ess.UI.navName.ret: One of "up", "down", "left", "right", "enter", "esc" - or nil for any other key.

Ess.UI.Focus.doc: Gives one widget exclusive keyboard focus. Also swallows any buffered key events (so the keypress that triggered the change does not leak into the newly focused widget) and wakes the UI heartbeat.
Ess.UI.Focus.gotcha: Exactly one widget hears keys at a time - focusing a new one silently takes focus away from whatever had it, with no notification to the old holder.

Ess.UI.Focused.doc: The widget currently holding keyboard focus.
Ess.UI.Focused.ret: The focused widget object, or nil when nothing has focus.

Ess.UI._register.doc: Internal: adds a widget to the engine's live list so the shared heartbeat services it - warmup repaints after the async movie load, size easing, and auto-hide countdowns. Every Ess.UI constructor calls it; it is idempotent, so a repeat registration is ignored.

Ess.UI._ensureTick.doc: Internal: arms the single shared Ess.UI heartbeat if it is not already running. Deliberately guarded by isRunning rather than calling Ess.Loop.start unconditionally, because start() reschedules a live loop and would keep pushing the next tick back on every :show().
Ess.UI._ensureTick.gotcha: The tick returns needsTick(), so the heartbeat STOPS ITSELF as soon as nothing needs servicing. Anything that creates new work (a new toast, a size change, a focus grab) has to call this again to wake it back up.

Ess.Easy.Camera.shake.doc: One-call screen shake for an explosion or heavy impact: the confirmed one-shot "ShakeCameraMedium" preset, sourced on the player's own character, amplitude 6 for 5 seconds.
Ess.Easy.Camera.shake.gotcha: Does nothing at all if the player has no camera or character yet - no log, no return value.

Ess.Easy.Camera.fadeIn.doc: Clears a full-screen fade back to a fully visible picture, by setting the fade amount to 0. The partner to fading out to black before a cutscene.
Ess.Easy.Camera.fadeIn.gotcha: Instant - the underlying native takes no duration argument, so there is no cross-fade here. To ease it, step the value yourself over several frames.

Ess.RNG.pick.doc: Picks one entry from a list using this generator's own deterministic stream, honouring per-entry weights read from `weightKey` (default "w"). Entries that are not tables count as weight 1, so a plain list of guids or strings is picked from uniformly. Called as a method on an RNG instance.
Ess.RNG.pick.gotcha: A list whose weights total zero or less quietly returns the FIRST entry instead of failing or picking randomly - an all-zero weight table is not an error.

Ess.Raw.AIOrders.pri.doc: Normalises a friendly priority word into the engine's own string constant: "hi"/"high" become "HiPri", "med"/"medium" become "MedPri", "lo"/"low" become "LoPri". Case-insensitive.
Ess.Raw.AIOrders.pri.gotcha: Anything unrecognised - including nil and a typo - falls back to "HiPri", so a misspelled priority silently becomes the highest one rather than erroring.

Ess.Relations.setPerceivability.doc: Sets how readily AI notices an object - the dial for making a unit harder or easier to spot.
Ess.Relations.setPerceivability.ret: true when the native call went through, false when it threw.

Ess.Raw.Relations.set.doc: Sets faction ga's raw numeric stance toward faction gb, taking faction guids rather than names.
Ess.Raw.Relations.set.ret: true when the native call went through, false when it threw.
Ess.Raw.Relations.set.gotcha: One-directional. A mutual stance needs both (ga,gb) and (gb,ga) set, which is what Ess.Relations.apply does for you - setting only one side leaves the other faction still friendly.

Ess.Sandbox.isActive.doc: Whether a sandbox is currently open under that id. Worth checking before Ess.Sandbox.begin, which refuses a duplicate id.

Ess.Raw.Sandbox.register.doc: Registers a custom sandbox provider under a name so Ess.Sandbox.begin can list it. A provider is a table with apply(id, opts) and restore(id) - write one for any state not covered by the built-in layers/economy/supports/relations set.
Ess.Raw.Sandbox.register.gotcha: Registering an existing name replaces the old provider outright, with no warning and no return value.

Ess.Raw.Sandbox.ungateSaves.doc: Releases the Raw tier's own save-gate holder so the game can write savegames again. The partner to Ess.Raw.Sandbox.gateSaves, for a provider author gating saves by hand without the full Sandbox lifecycle.
Ess.Raw.Sandbox.ungateSaves.gotcha: Uses one fixed holder key shared by every Raw-tier caller, so two hand-rolled gates will release each other. Saves stay blocked while ANY other holder (a live Ess.Sandbox or Ess.Layers mode) is still gating.

Ess.Cinematic.active.doc: The live cinematic sequence object, for code that needs to inspect or annotate the running cutscene. Use Ess.Cinematic.isPlaying when a plain yes/no is all you want.
Ess.Cinematic.active.ret: The sequence object, or nil when nothing is playing.

Ess.Followers._emit.doc: Internal: fires every listener registered for an event name through Ess.Followers.on, passing the extra arguments straight through. Each handler runs in its own pcall, so one throwing listener cannot stop the rest.
Ess.Followers._emit.gotcha: An event nobody has subscribed to is a silent no-op returning nil. The rejection message it logs under Ess.DEBUG talks about a marker not being placed, which has nothing to do with the actual cause - do not chase that text.

Ess.Followers.markersEnabled.doc: Whether the map markers over followers' heads are currently switched on. Defaults to true for a fresh load.

Ess.Followers.count.doc: How many followers are on the roster right now.
Ess.Followers.count.gotcha: Counts by calling Ess.Followers.list(), which PRUNES dead entries from the roster as a side effect - cheap, but not a pure read.

Ess.Followers.isFollower.doc: Whether a guid is currently on the follower roster. This is the membership test Ess.Squad.createTeam uses to decide which guids it will accept into a team.

Ess.Easy.Followers.orderAttack.doc: Orders every follower on the roster to attack one target guid.
Ess.Easy.Followers.orderAttack.ret: Whatever Ess.Followers.order returns for the "attack" behavior.
Ess.Easy.Followers.orderAttack.gotcha: Addresses the WHOLE roster - to move only some of them, name a team with Ess.Squad and use Ess.Easy.Squad.orderTeamAttack instead.

Ess.Easy.Followers.orderPatrol.doc: Orders every follower to patrol a route given as a list of {x,y,z} points.
Ess.Easy.Followers.orderPatrol.ret: Whatever Ess.Followers.order returns for the "patrol" behavior.

Ess.Easy.Followers.orderGuard.doc: Orders every follower to hold and defend a position, mapping onto the underlying "defend" behavior.
Ess.Easy.Followers.orderGuard.ret: Whatever Ess.Followers.order returns for the "defend" behavior.

Ess.Easy.Followers.hideMarkers.doc: Turns off the map markers floating over followers' heads - for a cutscene, a screenshot, or simply a quieter HUD. Ess.Followers.setMarkersEnabled(true) puts them back.
Ess.Easy.Followers.hideMarkers.gotcha: Returns nothing, and the setting is global to the whole roster rather than per follower.

Ess.Squad.roleOf.doc: The role string a unit was tagged with by Ess.Squad.assignRole. Ess.Squad.Tactics.mountUp reads this to board anyone marked "driver" first, before a passenger call can claim the wheel.
Ess.Squad.roleOf.ret: The role string, or nil when the unit has no role.

Ess.Easy.Squad.createTeam.doc: Names a group of existing followers as a team so later orders can address them by name instead of by guid list.
Ess.Easy.Squad.createTeam.ret: true, or false when the team name is missing or reserved.
Ess.Easy.Squad.createTeam.gotcha: Only guids that are ALREADY Ess.Followers followers are taken - anything else is dropped silently, so a team can come back smaller than the list you passed.

Ess.Easy.Squad.assignRole.doc: Tags one unit with a free-form role string such as "driver" or "gunner". The tactics layer reads "driver" specifically when boarding a vehicle.
Ess.Easy.Squad.assignRole.ret: true, or false when guid is nil.
Ess.Easy.Squad.assignRole.gotcha: The role is free-form and never validated - only "driver" has any built-in meaning, so a typo is accepted and simply does nothing.

Ess.Easy.Squad.orderTeamAttack.doc: Orders one named team to attack a target guid, leaving every other team and follower alone.
Ess.Easy.Squad.orderTeamAttack.ret: false when the team is unknown or has no live members; otherwise the result of issuing the "attack" behavior.

Ess.Easy.Squad.orderTeamPatrol.doc: Orders one named team to patrol a route of {x,y,z} points.
Ess.Easy.Squad.orderTeamPatrol.ret: false when the team is unknown or has no live members; otherwise the result of issuing the "patrol" behavior.

Ess.Easy.Squad.orderTeamGuard.doc: Orders one named team to hold and defend a position, mapping onto the underlying "defend" behavior.
Ess.Easy.Squad.orderTeamGuard.ret: false when the team is unknown or has no live members; otherwise the result of issuing the "defend" behavior.

Ess.Easy.Squad.cancelQueue.doc: Cancels a team's queued multi-step order: marks the queue cancelled, stops the step loop, runs its onCancel and puts everyone back on plain follow.
Ess.Easy.Squad.cancelQueue.ret: true when a queue was cancelled, false when that team had none.

Ess.Easy.Squad.mountUp.doc: Boards a team into a vehicle. Anyone tagged with the "driver" role boards first so a passenger call cannot claim the wheel, and everyone else follows as a passenger.
Ess.Easy.Squad.mountUp.ret: false immediately when the vehicle guid is missing or the team resolves to nobody.
Ess.Easy.Squad.mountUp.gotcha: The team argument also accepts a raw guid list, not just a team name - both go through the same resolver.

Ess.Easy.Squad.dismountAndSecure.doc: Gets a team out of whatever vehicles they are riding and has them secure a position within a radius - the standard "pull up, pile out, hold the ground" move.
Ess.Easy.Squad.dismountAndSecure.ret: false when the team resolves to nobody or atPos is missing.
Ess.Easy.Squad.dismountAndSecure.gotcha: The team argument also accepts a raw guid list. Vehicle drivers are exited explicitly, so the vehicle is left empty behind them.

Ess.Easy.Squad.clearFormation.doc: Drops the formation slots holding a team in shape, freeing each unit to move on its own again.
Ess.Easy.Squad.clearFormation.ret: true, or false when the team resolves to nobody.

Ess.Net.setv.doc: Writes a value into a synced namespace, bumps its version number and immediately broadcasts it to the peer. Conflicts resolve last-writer-wins by version.
Ess.Net.setv.gotcha: Every single write sends a packet, so do not call it on a per-frame tick - use Ess.Net.Track for a value that changes constantly. Keys written by both machines converge unpredictably; keep each key single-writer or host-authoritative.

Ess.Net.getv.doc: Reads the current synced value for a key in a namespace, whether it was set locally or arrived from the peer.
Ess.Net.getv.ret: The value, or nil when that namespace/key has never been set.

Ess.Contract._newTask.doc: Internal: creates a fresh task record for one objective - the bag that collects the engine events, spawned guids and marker handles that objective creates, so cleanup can later delete exactly those and nothing else.
Ess.Contract._newTask.ret: A task table with :event(h) and :guid(u) collector methods.

Ess.Contract._CleanupAll.doc: Internal: tears down every task on a contract instance - deletes their engine events, clears their markers and removes every object they spawned - then empties the task list.
Ess.Contract._CleanupAll.gotcha: Spawned objects are REMOVED outright, so anything the player is meant to keep must never be registered on a task's guid list.

Ess.Contract._finish.doc: Internal: ends the live contract, win or lose. Clears the HUD objective and chatter lines, stops any mission music, snapshots the final per-objective state into Ess.Contract.finished for the board's Status(), then on a win pays the reward, logs, shows the fanfare and calls def.onComplete (or logs and calls def.onFail on a loss). Finally it restores faction stances, cleans up every task and closes the sandbox if the contract opened one.
Ess.Contract._finish.gotcha: Returns immediately when the instance is not active, so a double finish is harmless. The snapshot it writes into .finished PERSISTS until the next Accept, which is why Status() keeps reporting a result after the mission is over.

Ess.Contract.Destroy.doc: Builds a "destroy these" objective for a contract's `objectives` list. t takes spawns (units to spawn and then kill), objects (guids that already exist), where, and quota (how many count as enough); like every builder it also passes through t.optional, t.bonus and t.msg.
Ess.Contract.Destroy.gotcha: Builders only assemble a table - nothing spawns, marks or runs until the definition is registered and Ess.Contract.Accept starts it.

Ess.Contract.Reach.doc: Builds a "get to this place" objective. t.at is the destination as {x,y,z} or {x=,y=,z=}, and t.radius is how close counts, defaulting to 15.
Ess.Contract.Reach.ret: An objective definition table for a contract's `objectives` list.

Ess.Contract.Defend.doc: Builds a "keep this alive for t.time seconds" objective, with t.target naming what must survive.
Ess.Contract.Defend.ret: An objective definition table for a contract's `objectives` list.

Ess.Contract.Collect.doc: Builds a "pick these up" objective. t.items lists what to collect, t.quota how many are needed, and t.radius the pickup range.
Ess.Contract.Collect.ret: An objective definition table for a contract's `objectives` list.

Ess.Contract.Escort.doc: Builds an "escort this unit to a place" objective. t.spawn is the unit to escort and t.to plus t.radius (default 15) is the destination zone.
Ess.Contract.Escort.ret: An objective definition table for a contract's `objectives` list.

Ess.Contract.Enter.doc: Builds a "get into this vehicle" objective. Name an existing guid with t.target or have the contract spawn one with t.spawn, and optionally pin a specific t.seat.
Ess.Contract.Enter.ret: An objective definition table for a contract's `objectives` list.

Ess.Contract.Hold.doc: Builds a "stay in this area for t.time seconds" objective, with t.at plus t.radius (default 15) describing the zone - the hold-the-point goal.
Ess.Contract.Hold.ret: An objective definition table for a contract's `objectives` list.

Ess.Contract.Group.doc: Builds a compound objective that wraps a list of other objectives (t.objectives) behind a single HUD line, combined according to t.mode - the way to express "do all of these" or "do any of these" as one step.
Ess.Contract.Group.ret: An objective definition table for a contract's `objectives` list.

Ess.Contract.Interact.doc: Builds a "use this thing" objective. t.target or t.spawn identifies the object, t.at gives an optional world position, t.radius (default 4) is how close the player must be, and t.time is how long the interaction must be held.
Ess.Contract.Interact.ret: An objective definition table for a contract's `objectives` list.

Ess.Contract.Verify.doc: Builds an "inspect or secure this target" objective. t.target or t.spawn names the subject, and t.capture with t.captureHealth turns it into a take-it-alive goal instead of a look-at-it one; t.radius sets the approach distance.
Ess.Contract.Verify.ret: An objective definition table for a contract's `objectives` list.

Ess.Contract.Extract.doc: Builds an exfiltration objective: reach t.at within t.radius (default 15) and stay aboard for t.boardTime, with optional t.heli for the pickup craft and t.victoryLap for the flight out.
Ess.Contract.Extract.ret: An objective definition table for a contract's `objectives` list.

Ess.Contract.Race.doc: Builds a checkpoint race objective: t.checkpoints is the ordered list of points, t.radius how close each one counts, and t.time the limit.
Ess.Contract.Race.ret: An objective definition table for a contract's `objectives` list.

Ess.Contract.Survive.doc: Builds a "stay alive for t.time seconds" objective, with t.target naming who must survive.
Ess.Contract.Survive.ret: An objective definition table for a contract's `objectives` list.

Ess.Contract.Chase.doc: Builds a "run this target down before it escapes" objective. t.spawns/t.objects/t.where describe the quarry, t.escapeAt plus t.escapeRadius mark the zone that loses it, and t.time and t.haste tune the pursuit.
Ess.Contract.Chase.ret: An objective definition table for a contract's `objectives` list.

Ess.Contract.StayInArea.doc: Builds a mission-wide leash: a zone (t.at with t.radius, default 100) the player has to remain inside for the duration of the contract.
Ess.Contract.StayInArea.gotcha: The one builder that does NOT go through the shared wrapper the others use, so it ignores t.optional, t.bonus and t.msg - it is a constraint on the whole contract, not a listed objective.

Ess.Contract.List.doc: Every contract definition registered during this level load, in registration order - what a contract-board UI iterates to build its rows.
Ess.Contract.List.ret: The registry array of definition tables.
Ess.Contract.List.gotcha: Hands back the internal array by reference, not a copy, so mutating what you get corrupts the registry.

Ess.Contract._restoreRelations.doc: Internal: puts back the faction stances a contract changed and drops the handle so the restore cannot run twice. Called from Ess.Contract._finish on every ending, win or lose.

natives.Ai.AddInfraction: Ai.AddInfraction(uCharacterGuid, uFactionGuid, nAmount) adds to a running "infraction" tally a character has against a faction, presumably feeding into relation decay.
natives.Ai.AddSubject: Ai.AddSubject(uGuid) registers an object with the AI subject-tracking system. Confirmed called when a player's character joins the game (resident/mrxplayer.lua).
natives.Ai.Anchor: Ai.Anchor({AIGuid = uGuid, AnchorRadius = n, ...}) pins a subject to its current position/area; AnchorRadius = 0 appears to mean it won't wander at all.
natives.Ai.DefaultGoal: Ai.DefaultGoal(tParameters) has no direct confirmed call sites, but resident/mrxai.lua wraps it 1:1 with Ai.Goal's calling convention (same table shape, same hibernation-gating), so it's inferred-by-analogy to share Goal's table shape rather than independently confirmed.
natives.Ai.Deliver: Ai.Deliver(uDriverGuid, nX, nY, nZ, nDropHeight, bCareless) commands a helicopter's AI driver to cargo-drop at a coordinate; nDropHeight sets drop altitude and bCareless likely relaxes precision/safety checks.

Ai.Deploy.doc: Ai.Deploy({Vehicle = uGuid, Role = sRole, Force = bForce, ...}) deploys/ejects occupants from a vehicle under AI control, e.g. Role = "Passenger", Force = true, MaintainRotorSpeed = true. Wrapped by resident/mrxai.lua with the same hibernation-gating as Goal.
Ai.Deploy.gotcha: Takes {Vehicle=, Role="Passenger", Force=} -- its argument table is not interchangeable with Ai.Goal's or Ai.Role's, and passing the wrong shape fails without an error.

natives.Ai.Enable: Ai.Enable(uGuid, bEnabled) toggles whether the AI system drives a given object at all. Confirmed in resident/mrxactionhijack.lua and resident/mrxutil.lua.
natives.Ai.GetFactionGuid: Ai.GetFactionGuid(uGuid) resolves an individual subject's owning faction guid, for use with GetRelation/SetRelation/etc.
natives.Ai.GetFeeling: Ai.GetFeeling(uGuidA, uGuidB) returns a numeric per-pair "feeling" value between two subjects, distinct from faction-level GetRelation (appears to be per-individual). At least one caller (resident/mrxfollow.lua) treats negative values as hostile.
natives.Ai.GetRelation: Ai.GetRelation(uGuidA, uGuidB) returns a numeric faction relation value (roughly -100 to 100) between two faction/subject guids. This is the literal primitive underneath MrxFactionManager's GetRelation wrapper; calling it directly bypasses that manager's HUD-meter and net-sync bookkeeping.
natives.Ai.GetState: Ai.GetState({AIGuid = uGuid, State = sStateName}) reads a named AI state flag for a subject (e.g. "NoCapture"). Table-shaped call, mirrors SetState's argument shape.

Ai.Goal.doc: Ai.Goal({AIGuid = uGuid, Goal = sGoalName, Target = ..., Priority = sPriority, ...}) issues a one-shot AI task (e.g. "PathMove") to a subject. Confirmed table keys: AIGuid, Goal, Target, Priority ("lowPri"/"hiPri"), Mode ("Oneway"), Start ("Nearest"), Haste, Callback, CallbackData. Returns a handle that can later be passed to RemoveGoal; the full set of valid Goal names/keys isn't enumerated anywhere in the corpus.
Ai.Goal.gotcha: A raw XYZ destination goes in `Location` (a plain {x,y,z} table), not `Position` and not `Target` (which takes a guid) -- and `Role` is NOT an Ai.Goal key at all. Worse, Goal="MoveToPos" with a Location silently returns nil for any ON-FOOT HUMAN regardless of distance (confirmed live; the corpus only ever uses it on a vehicle driver) -- use Goal="MoveTo" against a real object guid, spawning a TinyGeometry anchor at the destination if you need one.

natives.Ai.LivingWorld: Ai.LivingWorld({AIGuid = uGuid, Attrib = sAttribName, State = ...}) enables/disables the ambient "living world" behavior layer for a subject, typically disabled (State = false) before scripting custom behavior like Follow on top.
natives.Ai.RemoveExclusionZone: Ai.RemoveExclusionZone() clears whatever AI exclusion zone is currently active; confirmed called with zero arguments. The counterpart SetExclusionZone has no confirmed call sites.
natives.Ai.RemoveGoal: Cancels a goal by handle. Confirmed in two shapes: Ai.RemoveGoal({AIGuid = uGuid, Handle = hHandle}) and positional Ai.RemoveGoal(uGuid, hHandle); both forms coexist in shipped scripts and which one a given engine build expects isn't resolvable from source alone.
natives.Ai.RemoveSubject: Ai.RemoveSubject(uGuid) unregisters a subject from the AI system; the confirmed counterpart to AddSubject, called on character teardown (resident/mrxplayer.lua).

Ai.Role.doc: Ai.Role({AIGuid = uGuid, Role = sRoleName, ...}) assigns a standing behavioral role (e.g. "Follow", "Idle") to a subject, as opposed to Goal's one-shot tasks; returns a handle. Follow example includes Target, MinDistance, MaxDistance, MoveDistance, Priority, HardPriority, Callback, CallbackData.
Ai.Role.gotcha: "Follow" is a ROLE, not a Goal -- Ai.Goal{Goal="Follow"} is wrong and the confirmed recipe is Ai.Role{Role="Follow", Target=...}. Ai.Goal / Ai.Role / Ai.Deploy argument tables are not interchangeable; mixing them is the most common way AI code fails silently.

natives.Ai.SetFeeling: Ai.SetFeeling(uGuidA, uGuidB, nValue) sets the per-pair feeling value; confirmed used to neutralize hostility (set to 100) before starting a scripted "Follow" role.
natives.Ai.SetHaste: Ai.SetHaste(uGuid, nHaste) is a numeric multiplier controlling how urgently/fast a driven subject moves; 1 appears to be normal/default speed.
natives.Ai.SetInfractionMultiplier: Ai.SetInfractionMultiplier(uFactionGuid, nMultiplier) scales infraction accrual for a faction: 0 suppresses it, 1 is normal, fractional values (e.g. 0.2) soften it during scripted sequences.
natives.Ai.SetLaneActive: Ai.SetLaneActive(uRoadGuid, nLaneIndex, bActive) enables/disables a specific numbered lane on a road object for traffic spawning/routing.
natives.Ai.SetPriorityTarget: Ai.SetPriorityTarget(uGuid) marks a subject as the priority target for hostile AI.
natives.Ai.SetRelation: Ai.SetRelation(uGuidA, uGuidB, nRelation) sets the numeric faction relation between two guids, e.g. Ai.SetRelation(uFactionA, uFactionB, -100). Literal primitive underneath MrxFactionManager's SetRelation; direct calls skip its mutability checks and HUD/net-sync side effects.
natives.Ai.SetState: Ai.SetState({AIGuid = uGuid, State = sStateName, Value = ...}) sets a named AI state flag on a subject, e.g. State = "Pacifist", Value = true. Confirmed across several resident/ and vz/ scripts.
natives.Ai.Squad: Ai.Squad({SquadGuid = uSquad, Action = sAction, ...}) performs squad-level operations. Confirmed Action "GetUnits" returns a table of unit guids belonging to the squad; other actions build squads from scratch but their keys are unconfirmed.
natives.Ai.TestDropZone: Ai.TestDropZone({Callback = fCallback, Location = {x,y,z}, InnerRadius, InnerHeightTolerance, OuterRadius, OuterHeightTolerance, HeightMax, SearchRadius, Water = bAllowWater}) tests for a valid helicopter landing/drop spot. Returns a boolean; false means no valid spot found, and callers respond with fCallback(false, "noland"). The best-documented table-shaped call in the namespace, used identically across mrxgunship, mrxsupportdesignator, mrxtankbuster, and pursuitcopter.
natives.Ai.TweakAttachedSpawners: Ai.TweakAttachedSpawners(uBuildingGuid, {SpawnerState = "on"/"off", SecondsPerCycle = n, SpawnList = sList, ...}) adjusts all AI spawners attached to a building/object. Very common in resident/dangerousbuilding.lua, resident/outpost.lua, and vz/ mission scripts.
natives.Ai.TweakAttachedSpawnersInGroup: Ai.TweakAttachedSpawnersInGroup(uBuildingGuid, sGroupName, {SpawnerState = ..., ...}) is the same as TweakAttachedSpawners but scoped to spawners tagged with a group name ("Ground", "Balcony", "Rooftop") instead of all spawners on the object.
natives.Airstrike.ConeSpawn: Spawns nCount ordnance objects of vTemplate in a cone of half-angle nConeAngleDeg degrees around a direction vector, used for cluster/shrapnel spread patterns. Modules commonly stack multiple calls with widening angles and counts (e.g. a 15deg/10 ring then a 30deg/20 ring) for a denser pattern; no return value is used.
natives.Airstrike.EquipDesignator: Equips a target-designator "weapon" on uOwner — the tool a player aims to call in a strike (laser/smoke/flare/satellite/beacon). sDesignationType is a per-instance string; fCallback/tCallbackArgs fire when designation completes (nil means fire-and-forget); bFireImmediately skips the aim step. Returns the equipped weapon's guid.
natives.Airstrike.Flyby: Spawns a delivery aircraft (vDeliveryVehicle template string or instance field) that flies from a start point to an end point and invokes fDropCallback at the drop point, where the caller then spawns the actual ordnance. Argument order is two XZ pairs then Y — (startX, startZ, endX, endZ, Y, speed), not XYZ triples; callback/args are optional and speeds seen range 50-200. Returns the spawned jet's guid; this is the most-used call in the namespace after the two spawners.
natives.Airstrike.SpawnCarpetBombLine: Drops one row of a carpet-bomb pattern along nHeading and returns the next row's start XZ coordinates so the caller can loop to place successive rows. Only one confirmed call site exists, so the exact tail arguments (a nil 6th arg, then spacing and per-row count) are less certain than for higher-traffic calls.
natives.Airstrike.SpawnDirectedObject: Spawns a directed effect/particle object (not ordnance), oriented along the given direction vector, used for oriented explosion/fireball FX. vTemplate here is a global_particle_* name rather than an ordnance-template string. Returns the spawned object's guid.
natives.Airstrike.SpawnOrdnance: Spawns a single ordnance object (bomb/missile/shell) at a position with a velocity; vTemplate is a named engine-side ordnance template string (e.g. "Gunship Shell"), not a Lua data structure. The tail of the argument list is inconsistent across real call sites (some pass "impact"/a distance as arg 8, others insert a target uGuid first), so match the specific call site you're modeling rather than assuming one fixed signature. Returns the spawned ordnance guid.
natives.Airstrike.SpawnTargettedOrdnance: Same shape as SpawnOrdnance but always takes an explicit uTarget guid, used for homing/guided ordnance (e.g. missiles) rather than ballistic ordnance (bombs/shells). Confirmed usage: Airstrike.SpawnTargettedOrdnance("Vehicle AT Missile", nSpawnX, nSpawnY, nSpawnZ, nVectorX*nSpeedScale, nSpeedScale, nVectorZ*nSpeedScale, uTarget, "impact", 1, nil, BombExplodes, {uBomb}).
natives.Atmosphere.Begin: Graphics.Atmosphere.Begin() opens a scoped atmosphere-override block with no arguments, paired with one or more SetValue(sKey, nValue) calls and closed by End(). Confirmed used identically in every resident/airstrike_atomsphere_*.lua script to start a temporary bloom/lighting override for an airstrike effect.
natives.Atmosphere.ChangeLineRegionSetting: Graphics.Atmosphere.ChangeLineRegionSetting(uRegionGuid, sSettingName) applies a named weather/atmosphere preset to a specific map region. Confirmed example: applying the "warzone" preset to region "rgn_atmo_caracas".
natives.Atmosphere.End: Graphics.Atmosphere.End() closes the scoped atmosphere override opened by Begin(), restoring the prior values. Confirmed called with no arguments in every resident/airstrike_atomsphere_*.lua script.
natives.Atmosphere.SetValue: Graphics.Atmosphere.SetValue(sKey, nValue) sets a named atmosphere/bloom/lighting parameter by string key inside a Begin()/End() scope, e.g. SetValue("fBloomAmount", 0.75) or SetValue("fLightIntensity", 1.55). Confirmed keys include fAtmosphereForce, fAtmosphereLimit, several fBloom* keys, fLightIntensity, and fTimeRestore.
natives.Bloom.SetBlurRadius: Graphics.Bloom.SetBlurRadius(n) sets the bloom blur radius. Confirmed called once at boot with 0.5 in resident/mrxbootstrap.lua alongside the other post-process defaults.
natives.Bloom.SetMultiplier: Graphics.Bloom.SetMultiplier(n) sets the bloom intensity multiplier. Confirmed called at boot with 0 in resident/mrxbootstrap.lua.
natives.Bloom.SetThreshold: Graphics.Bloom.SetThreshold(n) sets the bloom brightness threshold. Confirmed called at boot with 0.775 in resident/mrxbootstrap.lua.
natives.Camera.Blend: Starts a timed blend into a new camera state: `Camera.Blend(uCameraGuid, nBlendTime [, bFlag])`. Confirmed in real scripts, used immediately before setting position/look-at/shot to transition smoothly into a new cinematic camera state.
natives.Camera.GetYaw: Returns the yaw of the camera at uCameraGuid. Confirmed in real scripts, e.g. `self.nHeading = Camera.GetYaw(Player.GetCamera(self:GetOwner()))`; the camera guid must first be obtained via Player.GetCamera.
natives.Camera.Hold: Holds the camera in place: `Camera.Hold(uCameraGuid, bHold, bFlag2 [, bFlag3])`. Confirmed in real scripts with two or three booleans, typically called right after SetLookAt/Blend during cinematics; the exact per-argument meaning beyond "hold in place" is unconfirmed.
natives.Camera.RestoreFocusParams: Graphics.Camera.RestoreFocusParams(nCameraIndex, nDuration) reverts a SetFocusParams depth-of-field override back to normal over the given duration. Confirmed calls always use camera index 0.
natives.Camera.RestoreFovParams: Graphics.Camera.RestoreFovParams(nCameraIndex, nDuration) reverts a SetFovParams field-of-view override. Confirmed calls always use camera index 0.
natives.Camera.RestoreNearFar: Graphics.Camera.RestoreNearFar(nCameraIndex) reverts a SetNearFar clip-plane override. Confirmed calls always use camera index 0.
natives.Camera.SetFocusParams: Graphics.Camera.SetFocusParams(nCameraIndex, nStartNear, nEndNear, nStartFar, nEndFar, nBlur, nDuration) blends a depth-of-field focus transition (near/far planes and blur) over a duration; used during hijack and turret-mount cinematics. This is Graphics.Camera, distinct from the top-level Camera namespace, and the camera index is confirmed as 0 at every call site.
natives.Camera.SetFovParams: Graphics.Camera.SetFovParams(nCameraIndex, nAngle, nDuration) blends the field-of-view angle to a new value over a duration. Confirmed used in hijack and briefing cinematics with camera index 0.

Camera.SetLookAt.doc: Aims the camera at a target, either raw coordinates `Camera.SetLookAt(uCameraGuid, nX, nY, nZ, bLookAtDirection [, bFlag])` or an object+hardpoint pair `Camera.SetLookAt(uCameraGuid, uObjectGuid, sHardpoint, bLookAtDirection [, bFlag])`. Confirmed with both forms in `resident/mrxbriefing.lua`, and with a simpler object+hardpoint call in `resident/mrxactionhijack.lua` (e.g. aiming at bone_chest during a hijack-fail cinematic).
Camera.SetLookAt.gotcha: This is the call that ENABLES Camera.SetPosition -- with no SetLookAt target ever set, SetPosition is a silent no-op. Even a static target that is never repositioned is enough to unblock it.

natives.Camera.SetNearFar: Graphics.Camera.SetNearFar(nCameraIndex, nNear, nFar, nUnknown) directly sets the near/far clip planes, as opposed to SetFocusParams' blended depth-of-field near/far. The trailing 4th argument is 0 at every confirmed call site; its meaning is unconfirmed.
natives.Camera.SetPitch: Sets the camera's pitch to a numeric value: `Camera.SetPitch(uCameraGuid, nPitch)`. Confirmed in real scripts, e.g. `Camera.SetPitch(uCamera, 0.302)` paired right after `Camera.SetYaw(uCamera, 0)` during a teleport-recovery sequence.

Camera.SetPosition.doc: Positions the camera, in either a plain-coordinates form `Camera.SetPosition(uCameraGuid, nX, nY, nZ [, bFlag])` or an object+hardpoint form `Camera.SetPosition(uCameraGuid, uObjectGuid, sHardpoint [, bFlag])`. Both forms are confirmed side-by-side in `resident/mrxbriefing.lua` for cinematic camera setup; the trailing boolean's exact meaning is unconfirmed.
Camera.SetPosition.gotcha: Silently does NOTHING until an active Camera.SetLookAt binding exists -- not even a hardcoded, oversized test teleport moves the camera. Spawn a small anchor prop, SetLookAt the camera at it once, and SetPosition starts working immediately.

natives.Camera.SetShot: Selects a named scripted camera "shot" between two actors: `Camera.SetShot(uCameraGuid, sShotName, uBaseActor, uTargetActor [, bFlag])`. Confirmed in the cinematic-briefing system (`resident/mrxbriefing.lua`), used alongside Blend and Hold to frame e.g. an over-the-shoulder or two-shot between a base actor and a target actor.
natives.Camera.SetYaw: Sets the camera's yaw to a numeric value: `Camera.SetYaw(uCamera, nYaw)`. Confirmed with literal values like 0 and 80 in real scripts (e.g. teleport-recovery and player-camera reset code).
natives.Camera.Shake: Triggers a named screen-shake effect: `Camera.Shake(uCameraGuid, sShakeName, uSourceGuid, nAmplitude, nDuration)`. Confirmed with presets `"ShakeCameraMedium"`, `"ShakeCameraConstantlyRandom"`, and a matching stop call using `"StopShakeCameraConstantly"`; the shake name selects an engine-defined preset not present in the decompiled Lua corpus. The camera guid is usually from Player.GetCamera(...), but one script instead passes StringToGuid("0x1") (possibly a fixed/broadcast camera handle, unconfirmed).
natives.Camera.StopBlending: Stops an in-progress camera blend: `Camera.StopBlending(uCameraGuid)`. Confirmed at one call site (`vz/vzacon001.lua`), notably guarded with an existence check (`if uCam and Camera.StopBlending then`) before calling.
natives.Contrast.SetLimit: Graphics.Contrast.SetLimit(n) sets the contrast limit for post-processing. Confirmed called at boot with 0.1 in resident/mrxbootstrap.lua.
natives.Contrast.SetMultiplier: Graphics.Contrast.SetMultiplier(n) sets the contrast multiplier for post-processing. Confirmed called at boot with 1.5 in resident/mrxbootstrap.lua.
natives.Effect.CameraFade: Graphics.Effect.CameraFade(nAmount) triggers a full-screen fade-to-black/fade-in effect keyed by a 0/1 amount, not tied to a specific camera guid. Confirmed called with 0 and 1 at the start/end of a hijack cinematic.

Event.Create.doc: Registers `callback` to run once when an event of `eventType` occurs, with a filter/parameter table whose shape depends entirely on the event type (e.g. ObjectDeath wants {targetGuid}, ObjectProximity wants {guidA, guidB, cmp, distance, bool, bool}). Returns a handle usable with Event.Delete to unregister. By far the most common event call in the codebase, used hundreds of times.
Event.Create.gotcha: Event.Create(Event.TimerRelative, {sec}, fn) fires exactly ONCE -- fn must re-arm its own next call, and that re-arm must be the FIRST line of the callback: put it after the per-tick work and one uncaught error permanently kills the whole timer chain (the confirmed root cause of a tool that "never turned on"). The timer is also gated on SIMULATION time, so it stops firing entirely while the world is paused, e.g. whenever the PDA is open.

natives.Event.CreatePersistent: Same call shape as Event.Create (eventType, {args}, callback, {callbackArgs}) plus an optional 5th boolean argument (bImmortalEvents). Used for events that should keep listening across multiple occurrences (e.g. repeated health-drop tracking, driver enter/exit) rather than a single fire-and-forget; the exact semantic difference from Create (repeat-fire vs. surviving something Create doesn't) is not confirmed from source.

Event.Delete.doc: Unregisters an event previously registered via Event.Create or Event.CreatePersistent, given the handle it returned. Used pervasively for cleanup/teardown — store the handle and delete it when the listening context goes away to avoid stale callbacks firing later.
Event.Delete.gotcha: The only way to unregister an Event.Create handle -- there is no clear-all native, so an event handle you drop on the floor stays live for the rest of the session. A self-rescheduling loop started from a re-run OnKey script leaks a whole extra loop per keypress unless you supersede it deliberately.

natives.Event.Post: Broadcasts a custom named event: takes a string name (not a numeric Event.* constant) plus a data table, e.g. Event.Post("SurvivalMode", {uGuid}). Appears to be a separate custom-broadcast mechanism from the numeric Event.ScriptEvent ID; no confirmed call site shows Event.ScriptEvent listeners receiving Post-ed names, so the exact delivery relationship between the two is unconfirmed.
natives.Graphics.GetShadowBaseDistance: Graphics.GetShadowBaseDistance() returns the current shadow draw distance with no arguments. Used to save off the current value before temporarily overriding it with SetShadowBaseDistance, then restoring it afterward.
natives.Graphics.InitTinyGeometry: Graphics.InitTinyGeometry() takes no arguments; confirmed called once in resident/mrxtaskmission.lua. Presumably initializes a small/LOD geometry render pass, though exact behavior beyond the call site is unconfirmed.
natives.Graphics.SetBoundaryEffect: Graphics.SetBoundaryEffect(nOpacity) controls the visual "boundary" (map edge / no-go zone) overlay effect opacity. Confirmed called with values like 0 and 0.25.
natives.Graphics.SetGamma: Graphics.SetGamma(nMin, nMax, nGamma) sets the screen gamma range. Confirmed called identically at boot in shell/shellbootstrap.lua and resident/gamebootstrap.lua as Graphics.SetGamma(0, 0.8, 1).
natives.Graphics.SetShadowBaseDistance: Graphics.SetShadowBaseDistance(nDistance) sets the shadow draw distance. Confirmed set to small values (2 during cinematic briefings, 10 elsewhere) and restored afterward, suggesting nDistance is a multiplier/scale rather than raw world units.
natives.Gui.ControllerInUse: Returns whether a controller (vs mouse/keyboard) is currently in use, no arguments. Guard-checked like IsXboxController; confirmed used to branch tutorial prompt phrasing between mouse/keyboard and controller in vzacon001.lua and wift tutorial scripts.
natives.Gui.DoSigninCheck: Runs the platform sign-in check with no arguments; confirmed called as part of the shell/platform-signin flow in mrxguishell.lua.
natives.Gui.EnablePlayerMarkers: Toggles rendering of player markers on screen (bEnabled boolean). Confirmed used as Gui.EnablePlayerMarkers(false)/(true) in mrxbriefing.lua to hide/show player markers during cutscenes and briefings.
natives.Gui.FindGuiLocation: Gui.FindGuiLocation(uOwnerOrPlayerGuid, uTargetGuid) returns nX1, nY1, nX2, nY2 — a screen-space bounding box (two corner points) for a world object, confirmed used to anchor UI overlays/tutorial callouts (mrxguisatellite.lua, mrxguitutorial.lua).
natives.Gui.GetLanguageName: Returns the current localization language name as a string, no arguments. Confirmed used in mrxsoundbanks.lua (local sLanguage = Gui.GetLanguageName()) to pick the correct localized sound bank.
natives.Gui.GetReticlePosition: Gui.GetReticlePosition(uOwnerGuid) returns nX, nY: 2D screen-space coordinates of the reticle for the given owner (e.g. oWidget:GetOwner()), confirmed with 5 call sites in mrxguihudreticle.lua. Distinct from Player.GetTargetUnderReticle, which returns the 3D world position/guid of whatever the reticle is aimed at; the two are complementary, not duplicates.
natives.Gui.IsPdaOnSelect: Returns a boolean with no arguments; confirmed guard-checked before use (if Gui.IsPdaOnSelect and Gui.IsPdaOnSelect() then) in mrxguipda.lua.
natives.Gui.IsXboxController: Returns whether an Xbox controller is in use, no arguments. Always guard-checked in real scripts (if Gui.IsXboxController and Gui.IsXboxController() then), suggesting it may not exist on all platform builds.
natives.Gui.LoadFont: Loads a font by name for HUD use, taking a single font-name string. Confirmed e.g. Gui.LoadFont("fanfare_36") in mrxguihudmessage.lua.
natives.Gui.LoadTexture: Loads a texture by name for HUD use (sTextureName [, sType]). Confirmed extensively, often with an explicit "texture" type string as the 2nd arg (e.g. 24 consecutive HUD-icon preload calls in mrxguihudactionhijack.lua), but also called with just the name elsewhere, so the 2nd argument is optional.
natives.Gui.OnGlobalExit: Called with no arguments as part of global game-exit teardown; confirmed in mrxstate.lua.
natives.Gui.OnShellLoaded: Called with no arguments as part of the shell-load lifecycle; confirmed guard-checked (if Gui.OnShellLoaded then Gui.OnShellLoaded() end) in mrxguishell.lua.
natives.Gui.SetPickupMarkerSize: Sets the on-screen size of pickup markers (nSize, bFlag). Confirmed real usage passes the same numeric size with the boolean flag flipped back-to-back (e.g. SetPickupMarkerSize(18, false) then (18, true) in hero.lua); the exact meaning of the flag is unconfirmed, possibly a near/far or friendly/enemy marker-set selector.
natives.Gui.SetPickupMarkerVisibleDistance: Sets the visible distance for pickup markers (nDistance, bFlag). Confirmed as Gui.SetPickupMarkerVisibleDistance(20, false) in hero.lua, at the same call site as SetPickupMarkerSize, run inside a 3-second delayed Event.TimerRelative block during survival-mode setup.
natives.Gui.ShowLoadingHints: Toggles the loading-screen hint text on/off (bShow boolean). Confirmed always guard-checked first in real scripts, e.g. if Gui.ShowLoadingHints then Gui.ShowLoadingHints(false) end in mrxgui.lua.
natives.Human.DisableWeapons: Disables a character's weapons, given a character uGuid. Extremely common, always paired with EnableWeapons elsewhere in the same module.
natives.Human.DoAction: Plays a named scripted action/pose on a character: Human.DoAction(uGuid, sActionName). Observed action names include "Cower", "Stand", "VerifyCamera", "shieldface", and "Proximity".
natives.Human.Drop: Makes a character drop whatever it's carrying: Human.Drop(uGuid [, bFlag]). Always called right after Human.IsCarrying returns true; the optional second boolean argument's exact effect isn't confirmed.
natives.Human.EnableWeapons: Re-enables a character's weapons, given a character uGuid. Counterpart to DisableWeapons.
natives.Human.ForceExitSeatNoSnap: Forces a character out of a vehicle seat without the normal snap-to-ground/exit animation, given a character uGuid.
natives.Human.IsCarrying: Returns whether a character is currently carrying something, given a character uGuid. Always checked immediately before a paired Human.Drop call in real scripts.
natives.Human.IsGrappling: Returns whether a character is currently grappling, given a character uGuid. Always checked immediately before a paired Human.StopGrappling call in real scripts.
natives.Human.IsSwimming: Returns whether a character is currently swimming, given a character uGuid. Used e.g. to decide whether a support drop should be treated as a water pickup; one call site guards the call defensively (if Human.IsSwimming and ...), suggesting the function's presence was historically treated as uncertain.
natives.Human.Knockdown: Knocks a character down for a given numeric duration: Human.Knockdown(uGuid, nDuration), e.g. Human.Knockdown(uCharacter, 0.5).
natives.Human.PersistTransform: Persists a character's current transform, given a character uGuid. Confirmed call sites but exact effect beyond the name isn't detailed.
natives.Human.PlayRawAnimation: Plays a raw named animation on a character with loop and blend-related flags: Human.PlayRawAnimation(uGuid, sAnimName, bLoop, bFlag2, nBlendTime, bFlag4 [, bFlag5]), optionally returning a success boolean. Exact meaning of the flags/blend-time beyond the animation name and loop flag is unconfirmed.
natives.Human.Scrub: Called on a character uGuid immediately following a Drop/SetState("Upright","Idle") cleanup sequence; likely resets/clears transient character state, but the exact effect is not confirmed.
natives.Human.SetAllowCorpseCleanup: Enables or disables corpse cleanup for a character: Human.SetAllowCorpseCleanup(uGuid, bAllow). One call site wraps the result in a debug print, implying it returns the previous state, though that's inferred rather than confirmed.
natives.Human.SetFireLock: Locks or unlocks a character's ability to fire their weapon: Human.SetFireLock(uGuid, bLocked). Used to prevent/allow firing during a scripted shooting-gallery sequence.
natives.Human.SetJostleEnabled: Toggles whether a character can be jostled, via a character uGuid and boolean: Human.SetJostleEnabled(uChar, bOn). Only one confirmed call site.
natives.Human.SetPreemptiveRagdoll: Puts a character into a preemptive ragdoll state ahead of some scripted event, given a character uGuid. Used in hijack setup/failure paths alongside Knockdown and ForceExitSeatNoSnap.
natives.Human.SetState: Sets a named state on a character along with a paired string value: Human.SetState(uGuid, sStateName, sAnimOrValue). Observed states: "InVehicle" (paired with an animation name), "Upright" (paired with "Idle"), and "Subdued" (paired with "Idle").
natives.Human.StopGrappling: Stops a character's current grapple, given a character uGuid. Always called right after Human.IsGrappling returns true.
natives.Inventory.DropWeapon: Drops a specific weapon from a character's inventory. Takes a character uGuid and a weapon uGuid: Human.Inventory.DropWeapon(uCharGuid, uWeaponGuid). Very common across mission scripts.
natives.Inventory.EquipWeapon: Equips a previously-fetched weapon uGuid onto a character, swapping out whatever they're currently holding. Confirmed usage: Human.Inventory.EquipWeapon(uPlayer, uWeaponGuid), e.g. paired with GetPrimaryWeapon/GetSecondaryWeapon. This is the actually-used form; the top-level Human.EquipWeapon exists but has zero confirmed call sites.
natives.Inventory.GetAllWeapons: Returns a table of weapon guids held by the given character uGuid. Extremely common; some call sites pass an additional boolean second argument whose effect is unconfirmed.
natives.Inventory.GetPrimaryWeapon: Returns the primary weapon uGuid for a given character uGuid, e.g. Human.Inventory.GetPrimaryWeapon(Player.GetLocalCharacter()).
natives.Inventory.GetSecondaryWeapon: Returns the secondary weapon uGuid for a given character uGuid, e.g. Human.Inventory.GetSecondaryWeapon(uPlayer).
natives.Inventory.ReloadAll: Reloads all of a character's weapons. Confirmed with a character uGuid and a boolean flag in one real call: Human.Inventory.ReloadAll(uCharacter, false); the boolean's exact meaning isn't confirmed.
natives.Inventory.SetAllWeapons: Sets a character's full weapon loadout from an array-style table of weapon uGuids, e.g. Human.Inventory.SetAllWeapons(uCharGuid, {uPrimary, uGrenade, uC4}). Some call sites instead pass a single weapon uGuid in place of the table, so the full accepted argument shapes aren't fully pinned down.
natives.Junk.DrawPath: Junk.DrawPath(uPathGuid) draws/visualizes a path object. Confirmed in vz/meccon001.lua, called with a path GUID (resolved via Pg.GetGuidByName) immediately before passing that same GUID to Ai.Goal({Goal="PathMove", Target=uPath,...}) — reads as a debug/AI-path visualization aid with no mechanical gameplay effect.
natives.Junk.FormatTime: Junk.FormatTime(nTime [, bUseTenths]) formats a numeric time value into a display string. Confirmed used in resident/mrxtimer.lua and resident/mrxstatsmanager.lua feeding a displayed stats string; the optional second boolean argument appears to control whether tenths-of-a-second are included.
natives.Junk.InstallToHDD: Junk.InstallToHDD() takes no arguments. Confirmed in resident/mrxguishell.lua as the callback run when the player picks the "install to HDD" option in the console install-options menu; disc/HDD-install tooling, not gameplay-relevant.
natives.Junk.IsInstallable: Junk.IsInstallable() takes no arguments and returns a value used in a boolean context. Confirmed in mrxguishell.lua, called defensively as `if Junk.IsInstallable and Junk.IsInstallable() then` — part of the console install-menu plumbing.
natives.Junk.UseExistingInstall: Junk.UseExistingInstall() takes no arguments. Confirmed in the same mrxguishell.lua install-menu callback, invoked when the player selects "Use Existing HDD Install"; console install tooling, not gameplay-relevant.
natives.Marker.Add: Creates a marker offset from a target object: Marker.Add(nOffsetX, nOffsetY, nOffsetZ, uGuid, nR, nG, nB, nRadius). Confirmed in real scripts (e.g. mrxtaskobjectivedeliver.lua) — offset vector, target uGuid, RGB color, then a radius-looking value. Returns a marker handle later passed to Marker.Remove.
natives.Marker.Add3D: Attaches a 3D icon marker to an object: Marker.Add3D(uGuid, sIconName, nR, nG, nB [, nWidth]). Confirmed in real scripts (mrxtaskrace.lua) with icon names like "global_tripwirefinish" and "global_airring"; the optional trailing width was only seen paired with "global_airring". Returns a marker handle.

Marker.AddBlip.doc: Adds a minimap/radar blip to a uGuid: Marker.AddBlip(uGuid, sTextureName, nSize, nR, nG, nB, nAlpha, ...). The one function on this namespace confirmed by live in-game testing (see wiki snippets page); real scripts (mrxfactionmanager.lua) pass a longer arg list with nil gaps after texture/size/RGBA, so the full trailing parameter set beyond those is not individually confirmed.
Marker.AddBlip.gotcha: Renders at GROUND LEVEL under the object, not at the object's own height -- a known quirk of the one live-confirmed call. An untested texture name silently fails to load rather than erroring, so reuse a confirmed one instead of guessing.

natives.Marker.AddDisc: Draws a flat colored ring/disc on the ground: Marker.AddDisc(uGuidOrLocation, nRadius, nR, nG, nB, nThickness). Confirmed in real scripts; the first argument accepts either a uGuid or a raw location vector (e.g. mrxtaskobjectivedeliver.lua passes a vDestLoc vector directly instead of a uGuid).
natives.Marker.AddTripwire: Creates a tripwire marker at raw world coordinates: Marker.AddTripwire(nX, nY, nZ, nWidth, nYaw, nR, nG, nB). Confirmed in mrxtaskrace.lua, used for race-gate finish lines and typically paired with Add3D for the visual finish-line icon at the same location.
natives.Marker.HaltPulse: Marker.HaltPulse(uGuid) — stops a previously-started Marker.Pulse effect on the given object's marker. Confirmed in mrxfactionmanager.lua, called when tearing down a reporting-display marker.
natives.Marker.Pulse: Marker.Pulse(uGuid, nR, nG, nB) — flashes/pulses an object's existing marker in the given RGB color. Confirmed in real scripts (mrxfactionmanager.lua, munitions.lua); paired with HaltPulse to stop the effect. Takes a uGuid, not a marker handle.

Marker.Remove.doc: Marker.Remove(uMarker) — removes/cleans up a marker. Extremely common in real scripts; always called with the marker handle previously returned by Add, Add3D, AddBlip, AddDisc, or AddTripwire — not a raw object uGuid.
Marker.Remove.gotcha: The only thing that accepts a Marker.Add*() handle -- there is no clear-all native for markers, so a handle you lose track of leaks for the session. Register it with a tracker at creation time.

natives.Monochrome.SetGradient: Graphics.Monochrome.SetGradient(n1..n10) takes 10 numeric arguments and is confirmed called twice back-to-back at boot (e.g. (0,128,0,0,0,0,0,0.65,0.35,0) then (128,255,0,0.65,0.35,0,1,1,1,0)), presumably defining a two-stop shadow/highlight color-grading curve. Exact per-argument meaning is not confirmed.
natives.Net.AutoClient: Returns whether the game should automatically connect as a client at boot. Used as `if Net.AutoClient() then Net.ConnectToServer() end` in gamebootstrap.lua and shellbootstrap.lua.
natives.Net.AutoLobby: Returns whether the game should automatically enter the lobby at boot, the same boot-time chain as AutoClient/AutoServer: `elseif Net.AutoLobby() then Net.EnterLobby() end`.
natives.Net.AutoServer: Returns whether the game should automatically start as a server at boot, part of the same boot-time branch as AutoClient: `if Net.AutoServer() then Net.StartServer(...) end`.
natives.Net.BeginLayerEventGroup: Begins a bracketed group of layer-related network events. Called with no arguments and guarded by an existence check (`if Net.BeginLayerEventGroup then ... end`), confirmed in xQ!L.lua; paired with EndLayerEventGroup.
natives.Net.ConnectToServer: Connects to a server, optionally with a name and an IP-address-or-mode string (e.g. "online" or an empty string for LAN); called with no arguments at boot to use defaults. Returns a boolean treated as success.
natives.Net.DoneReloadingLayers: Signals that layer reloading has completed. Called with no arguments and consistently guarded by an existence check (`if Net.DoneReloadingLayers then ... end`) across several vz mission scripts and mrxtaskcontract.lua — the recurring guard suggests it may not exist on every engine build.
natives.Net.EndLayerEventGroup: Ends a bracketed group of layer-related network events. Called with no arguments and guarded by an existence check, confirmed in xQ!L.lua; paired with BeginLayerEventGroup.
natives.Net.EnterFriendsLobby: Enters the friends lobby. Called with no arguments in mrxguishell.lua.
natives.Net.EnterLobby: Enters the multiplayer lobby. Called with no arguments at boot time and from shell-menu lobby entry.

Net.GetHostName.doc: Returns the local host's display name. Always used as the first argument to Net.StartServer(Net.GetHostName(), ...).
