Graphics.Camera.SetFovParams.doc: Blends the render camera's field-of-view angle to a new value over a duration. Confirmed in resident/mrxactionhijack.lua and resident/mrxbriefing.lua; pair with RestoreFovParams to undo.

Human.EquipWeapon.gotcha: This top-level form has ZERO real call sites anywhere in the decompiled corpus. The confirmed-working call is Human.Inventory.EquipWeapon(uChar, uWeapon).

Math.randf.gotcha: The ENGINE's own RNG, entirely independent of lua-bridge's polyfilled math.random -- two separate generators side by side, so seeding one has no effect on the other. Pick whichever matches the code you're extending and don't mix them.

MrxFactionManager.SetAttitudeMutable.gotcha: A silent no-op for any faction whose static bDynamic flag is false -- CanAttitudeBeMutable gates the entire function body, so there's no error and nothing looks wrong until you notice that faction never reacts to anything.

MrxGuiTextBuffer.AddMessage.gotcha: The display queue is REAL wall-clock time: each message occupies the box for its full display+fade duration before the next one can even show. A bulk dump that blindly copied a 15-second default across 194 lines queued nearly 50 MINUTES of messages and silently blocked every later update on that box -- pass a short duration (~1s) for anything logged in bulk.

MrxGuiTextBuffer.HandleInstantiationEven.gotcha: The bug-free path around the broken InstantiateTextBuffer -- here `oWidget` really is the function's own first parameter. Hand-build a bare widget and name it exactly "MessageBox": that literal string is what flips on the translucent chat-box backdrop.

MrxGuiTextBuffer.InstantiateTextBuffer.gotcha: SHIPPED ENGINE BUG: the documented constructor references a global `oWidget` that doesn't exist in its own scope (a copy-paste mistake -- the real widget is NewTextBuffer), so calling it throws "attempt to index a nil value (global 'oWidget')" and crashes the caller. Patching it from outside doesn't help either -- the patched copy runs in YOUR environment and strands the module's own private functions; use HandleInstantiationEventForTextBuffer instead.

MrxLayerManager.MarkForAddition.gotcha: Only flips an entry in an internal table -- nothing loads until ProcessMarkedLayers runs, and even then the world isn't visibly re-composited without a WaitForStreaming transition. It's a genuine no-op for a layer that's already loaded, which makes it safe to call unconditionally.

MrxLayerManager.MarkForRemoval.gotcha: Only flips an internal table entry; the actual Pg.UnloadLayer fires later inside ProcessMarkedLayers. Check what a layer really contains first -- a name that reads like a status flag ('pristine' as in not-yet-captured) turned out to be load-bearing geometry, and removing it produced destroyed-and-empty bases.

MrxLayerManager.ProcessMarkedLayers.gotcha: Issues the Pg.LoadLayer/UnloadLayer calls but does NOT composite them -- the world only re-composites during a WaitForStreaming game-state transition, which an OnLoad script runs before. Layer edits made from OnLoad are therefore silently rejected; drive the state transition yourself.

MrxPmc.AddCashQty.gotcha: Needs its own `import("MrxPmc")` line in every file that calls it -- import is FILE-SCOPED, so an OnKey/OnLoad script or a console chunk without it fails with "attempt to index global 'MrxPmc' (a nil value)". This is the HUD-updating path; Player.SetCash changes the value but leaves the on-screen number stale.

MrxPmc.AddFuelQty.gotcha: Fuel has a separate quantity and CAPACITY -- raising the quantity past the current capacity does nothing until you raise the capacity too. Same file-scoped import("MrxPmc") requirement as AddCashQty.

MrxState.Enter.gotcha: Increments a per-state refcount that ONLY an explicit MrxState.Exit decrements -- and STATE_WAITFORSTREAMING's own completion path does not decrement it for you. Enter without pairing an Exit (from the readyToExit callback) and the global fade-in never runs: the player is left faded to black, input-locked and invincible, permanently.

MrxState.Exit.gotcha: Must be called explicitly for every MrxState.Enter, from inside the readyToExit callback -- nothing decrements the refcount on your behalf. A single orphaned refcount makes every later global-exit attempt bail out, which is the black-screen hang.

MrxTransit.SetLocationEnabled.gotcha: The PDA, radar colours and fast-travel menu read MrxTransit, NOT the layer system -- flip layers without stamping ownership here and the world looks captured up close while the map still shows the old owner. An easy bug to not notice until someone opens the map.

MrxTutorialManager.HideMessage.gotcha: Only clears a hint whose sId matches EXACTLY -- a different or missing id silently does nothing and the message stays up forever (confirmed by live testing). Keep the id you showed it with.

MrxTutorialManager.ShowMessage.gotcha: Has NO auto-hide timer -- the hint stays on screen until MrxTutorialManager.HideMessage is called with a matching id. It's a completely generic, reusable popup despite being the tutorial-hint primitive (confirmed live with a screenshot).

MrxUtil.SpawnActor.gotcha: ASYNCHRONOUS, and it returns (and fires its callback) before the spawned object's COLLISION has finished streaming. Teleporting inside the naive version of its own callback drops you through the floor -- confirmed live, the player fell from y~451 through y~340 and kept going; poll until the actor resolves (~1.5s beyond the callback) before teleporting.

MrxUtil.TeleportHeroesToLocations.gotcha: This is the CONFIRMED teleport idiom (not raw Object.SetPosition), but multi-player teleport helpers can crash the game when used inside an interior cell -- treat it as outdoor-only.

Pg.ClearPursuitRestrictions.gotcha: Drops the organic-escalation restrictions only; it has no effect on a pursuit that is already running. Clearing restrictions is not the same as clearing heat.
Pg.ClearPursuitRestrictions.doc: Exists per the live enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus; argument shape and actual restriction-clearing effect are unconfirmed.

Pg.RestrictAllPursuit.gotcha: Does NOT clear an active pursuit despite the name, and does not block a scripted pursuit start -- it only gates ORGANIC, AI-driven heat escalation. The off switch for a live chase is Pg.ClearPursuitLock(true), nothing else.
Pg.RestrictAllPursuit.doc: Takes a boolean and blocks organic pursuit escalation -- the game's own AI-driven pursuit triggers. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22; reach for it to keep the world calm during a scripted sequence.

Pg.RestrictPursuitFaction.gotcha: Gates only ORGANIC AI escalation for that faction -- it does not clear an already-active pursuit and does not block a scripted start. Use Pg.ClearPursuitLock(true) to actually end a chase.
Pg.RestrictPursuitFaction.doc: Takes a faction guid and a boolean, blocking that one faction's organic pursuit escalation. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22.

Pg.SaveGame.gotcha: Two independent pieces of code stashing-and-swapping this function will silently clobber each other -- a confirmed interleaving had one system's restore discard another's freshly installed wrap, leaving that system's save-gate permanently ineffective for the session. Install ONE wrap, never uninstall it, and gate by refcount.

Pg.SetMaxPursuitLevel.gotcha: A ONE-WAY RATCHET DOWN for the rest of the session: nothing raises the ceiling back up. A bigger n, a (faction, n) form, 99, SetPursuitLevelTimes and SetCustomPursuit were all tried and none undo it -- only a save-load or full restart resets it.
Pg.SetMaxPursuitLevel.doc: Caps the pursuit level ceiling: after Pg.SetMaxPursuitLevel(2), a following Pg.SetPursuit(uFaction, 5) only reached Level=2. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22.

Ai.Admire.doc: Live-probed over lua-bridge against a running game (2026-07-22) with a manufactured AI subject: runs with no error and no crash, but produced no observable effect at an isolated test spot. Arguments are unconfirmed.
Ai.Admire.gotcha: A 'doesn't crash' confirmation only -- not a confirmation that it does what the name implies. Likely needs an engaged AI context (traffic, hostiles, other subjects) that the test spot did not provide.

Ai.ChangeRelation.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Ai) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. Given the confirmed Ai.GetRelation/Ai.SetRelation pair it is presumably a relative/delta adjustment rather than an absolute set, but that is a naming-based guess.

Ai.EveryoneOut.doc: Forces all occupants out of a vehicle. Confirmed live (2026-07-22) by reading Vehicle.GetDriver before and after the call: a real pilot guid became nil.
Ai.EveryoneOut.gotcha: Takes the vehicle's own guid, not a rider/pilot guid -- the opposite convention from Ai.HeliLand and Ai.Deliver, which want the pilot.

Ai.GetAttrib.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Ai) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. Presumably the getter counterpart of the Attrib field seen in Ai.LivingWorld, but that pairing is inferred from naming only.

Ai.GetPerceivability.doc: Returns a subject's perceivability as two numbers -- a current value and a floor (e.g. 90, 5) -- read as a stealth/detectability rating and its minimum. Confirmed live (2026-07-22); read-only and safe to probe blind.
Ai.GetPerceivability.gotcha: Returns two values, not one. Unlike Ai.GetSubjectData it does answer for AI-controlled subjects, not just the player character.

Ai.GetSubjectData.doc: Returns the AI system's live threat/awareness tally for a subject as a table of {TotalAware, Attackers, TotalObservers, HostileObservers, HostileAware}. Confirmed live (2026-07-22) on the player character; read-only and safe to probe blind.
Ai.GetSubjectData.gotcha: Only the player character appears to be a tracked awareness subject -- probed against an AI-controlled helicopter pilot it returned nothing, where Ai.GetPerceivability returned real data for the same subject.

Ai.GoIn.doc: Live-probed over lua-bridge against a running game (2026-07-22) with a subject guid and a target guid: executes cleanly, but produced no observable effect at an isolated test spot.
Ai.GoIn.gotcha: A 'doesn't crash' confirmation only -- not a confirmation that it does what the name implies.

Ai.HeliLand.doc: Commands a helicopter's AI pilot to descend and land. Confirmed live (2026-07-22): a test helicopter's Y position went from 7.5 down to ground level (-27.5) over roughly six seconds after the call.
Ai.HeliLand.gotcha: Takes the pilot/driver guid (the same convention as Ai.Deliver), not the vehicle's own guid. The descent takes several seconds -- the call returns long before the helicopter is down.

Ai.HeliTakeoff.doc: Intended counterpart to Ai.HeliLand, taking the pilot guid and optionally a destination coordinate. Live-probed 2026-07-22: executed cleanly but produced no observed ascent.
Ai.HeliTakeoff.gotcha: Inconclusive, not confirmed broken -- it likely needs a different trigger or prior AI state (e.g. already landed/idle) that the test spot did not provide.

Ai.RemoveAllSubjects.doc: Zero-argument call that live-probed cleanly (2026-07-22) but showed no observable effect at an isolated test spot holding only one manufactured subject.
Ai.RemoveAllSubjects.gotcha: A 'doesn't crash' confirmation only -- nothing confirms it actually clears the AI subject list.

Ai.Rest.doc: Live-probed over lua-bridge against a running game (2026-07-22) with a manufactured AI subject: runs with no error, but produced no observable effect at an isolated test spot. Arguments are unconfirmed.
Ai.Rest.gotcha: A 'doesn't crash' confirmation only -- not a confirmation that it does what the name implies.

Ai.SetAttitude.doc: Takes a subject uGuid plus either an attitude string ("Hostile"/"Neutral"/"Friendly") or a raw number. Live-probed 2026-07-22: executes cleanly, but showed no observable effect at an isolated test spot with nothing around to react.
Ai.SetAttitude.gotcha: MrxFactionManager builds its own attitude-label system entirely on Ai.GetRelation numeric thresholds and never calls this anywhere in the corpus -- whether Ai.SetAttitude overlaps with or bypasses that resident-side system is unconfirmed.

Ai.SetDriveThroughMassRatio.doc: Takes a single numeric ratio. Live-probed 2026-07-22: executes cleanly with no observable effect at an isolated test spot, so what the ratio actually controls is unconfirmed.
Ai.SetDriveThroughMassRatio.gotcha: A 'doesn't crash' confirmation only -- likely needs live traffic present to show any effect.

Ai.SetFacing.doc: Turns a subject to face a given heading; the wiki records two candidate shapes, Ai.SetFacing(uGuid, nAngle) and Ai.SetFacing(uGuid, nX, nY, nZ). Live-probed 2026-07-22 against a flying helicopter's pilot and a just-exited pilot on foot: executed without error but produced no yaw change either time.
Ai.SetFacing.gotcha: Most likely only turns an idle, AI-driven ground NPC in place -- a flying helicopter's own flight AI owns its heading, and a just-exited pilot may not be a valid facing target at all.

Ai.SetPerceivability.doc: Sets a subject's perceivability (stealth/detectability) value. Confirmed live (2026-07-22) as a real, reversible state change: driving a subject 90 -> 30 -> 90 and reading it back with Ai.GetPerceivability between steps showed the value actually moves.
Ai.SetPerceivability.gotcha: A third argument exists but its purpose is unconfirmed.

Ai.ShowObjectSpawners.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Ai) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. Presumably a debug-visualization toggle given the name, but that is a guess.

Ai.Temp.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Ai) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. Usage is completely unconfirmed, including argument count.

Airstrike.SpawnPlaneNew.doc: Surfaced from a static luaL_Reg engine-binding dump rather than any call site; disassembly shows it reads only a string plus one number. Live-probed 2026-07-22 with both a Flyby-style 7-argument call and a simple (name, x, y, z) call -- neither spawned anything visible nor returned a guid.
Airstrike.SpawnPlaneNew.gotcha: Not a working plane spawner as currently understood, despite the name. Airstrike.Flyby remains the confirmed, working mechanism for spawning delivery aircraft.

Animation.GetTranslationForStanceAndActi.doc: Name and table membership confirmed by the corpus call-prefix cross-reference; never live-probed and no call site with a concrete argument list was captured. Presumed by name to look up a translation/offset keyed by a stance and an action, but signature and even general behaviour are unconfirmed.

Animation.PlayFaceAnim.doc: Name and table membership confirmed by the corpus call-prefix cross-reference; never live-probed and no call site with a concrete argument list was captured. Presumed by name to play a facial animation on a character; signature unconfirmed.
Animation.PlayFaceAnim.gotcha: Distinct from the already-confirmed animation functions on the Object namespace -- this lives on the separate native Animation table.

Atmosphere.GetValue.doc: Not individually checked against the corpus in the wiki's research pass. Presumed getter counterpart to the confirmed SetValue, using the same string-key convention -- assumed, not confirmed.

Atmosphere.SetColorValue.doc: Not individually checked against the corpus in the wiki's research pass. Presumed the colour-typed variant of Graphics.Atmosphere.SetValue.

Atmosphere.SetHenyeyGreensteinConst.doc: Exists per the live enumeration, name only; not individually traced against the corpus. Henyey-Greenstein is a standard atmospheric-scattering phase function, consistent with the other sky/scattering tuning parameters on this sub-table.

Atmosphere.SetLightIntensity.doc: Exists per the live enumeration, name only; not individually traced against the corpus.
Atmosphere.SetLightIntensity.gotcha: Distinct from the confirmed SetValue("fLightIntensity", n) key -- a same-named setter and a SetValue key are two different routes, and only the SetValue form is confirmed in use.

Camera.Follow.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Camera) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. Arguments beyond the presumed leading camera guid are unconfirmed.

Camera.GetFOV.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Camera) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus; usage unconfirmed. Takes the per-player camera guid from Player.GetCamera(uPlayerGuid), like the rest of this namespace.
Camera.GetFOV.gotcha: Do not confuse with Graphics.Camera.SetFovParams -- that is a different, confirmed-in-use function on the separate Graphics.Camera sub-table, which shares the name Camera and nothing else.

Camera.GetPitch.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Camera) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. Presumed counterpart to the confirmed Camera.SetPitch.

Camera.SetFOV.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Camera) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus; usage unconfirmed. Still flagged as needing a dedicated live-probe pass with an active cinematic mode running, not attempted as of 2026-07-22.
Camera.SetFOV.gotcha: Do not confuse with Graphics.Camera.SetFovParams on the separate Graphics.Camera sub-table -- same-sounding name, different table.

Graphics.ReloadShaders.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Graphics) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. The name strongly suggests a dev/debug shader-hotreload utility.

Graphics.SetNumFrameSync.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Graphics) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. The name suggests a frame-sync/vsync-count control; arguments unconfirmed.

Graphics.SetScreenRatio.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Graphics) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. Presumed counterpart to Graphics.GetScreenRatio.

Graphics.ShowTinyGeometryObject.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Graphics) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. Presumed companion to the confirmed Graphics.InitTinyGeometry.

Graphics.AA.SetThreshold.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Graphics) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. Presumably an anti-aliasing edge-detection threshold.

Graphics.Atmosphere.Begin.doc: Opens a scoped atmosphere-override block, with no arguments. Confirmed in every resident/airstrike_atomsphere_*.lua file as the opener for a Begin() / SetValue(sKey, nValue) / End() sequence that temporarily forces bloom and lighting for the duration of an airstrike effect.
Graphics.Atmosphere.Begin.gotcha: Must be paired with Graphics.Atmosphere.End() -- SetValue calls only apply inside the block.

Graphics.Atmosphere.ChangeLineRegionSett.doc: Applies a named weather/atmosphere preset to a specific map region. Confirmed in vz/allcon003.lua: ChangeLineRegionSetting(Pg.GetGuidByName("rgn_atmo_caracas"), "warzone") -- reach for it to swap a region's mood for a mission beat.

Graphics.Atmosphere.End.doc: Closes the scoped override opened by Graphics.Atmosphere.Begin(), with no arguments. Confirmed in every resident/airstrike_atomsphere_*.lua file.

Graphics.Atmosphere.GetColorValue.doc: Not individually checked against the corpus in the wiki's research pass. Presumed the colour-typed variant of Graphics.Atmosphere.GetValue, same string-key convention.

Graphics.Atmosphere.GetCurrentSetting.doc: Exists per the live enumeration; not individually traced against the decompiled corpus. Presumed getter counterpart to ChangeLineRegionSetting/Change.

Graphics.Atmosphere.GetIntValue.doc: Not individually checked against the corpus in the wiki's research pass. Presumed the integer-typed variant of Graphics.Atmosphere.GetValue.

Graphics.Atmosphere.GetLineRegionSetting.doc: Exists per the live enumeration; not individually traced against the decompiled corpus. Presumed getter counterpart to the confirmed ChangeLineRegionSetting.

Graphics.Atmosphere.GetValue.doc: Not individually checked against the corpus in the wiki's research pass. Presumed getter counterpart to the confirmed SetValue, using the same string-key convention -- assumed, not confirmed.

Graphics.Atmosphere.SetColorValue.doc: Not individually checked against the corpus in the wiki's research pass. Presumed the colour-typed variant of Graphics.Atmosphere.SetValue.

Graphics.Atmosphere.SetHenyeyGreensteinC.doc: Exists per the live enumeration, name only; not individually traced against the corpus. Henyey-Greenstein is a standard atmospheric-scattering phase function, consistent with the other sky/scattering tuning parameters on this sub-table.

Graphics.Atmosphere.SetIntValue.doc: Not individually checked against the corpus in the wiki's research pass. Presumed the integer-typed variant of Graphics.Atmosphere.SetValue.

Graphics.Atmosphere.SetLightIntensity.doc: Exists per the live enumeration, name only; not individually traced against the corpus.
Graphics.Atmosphere.SetLightIntensity.gotcha: Distinct from the confirmed SetValue("fLightIntensity", n) key -- a same-named setter and a SetValue key are two different routes, and only the SetValue form is confirmed in use.

Graphics.Atmosphere.SetValue.doc: Sets one named atmosphere/bloom parameter inside a Begin()/End() block. Confirmed extensively in resident/airstrike_atomsphere_*.lua, e.g. SetValue("fBloomAmount", 0.75), SetValue("fAtmosphereLimit", 200), SetValue("fLightIntensity", 1.55). Confirmed keys: fAtmosphereForce, fAtmosphereLimit, fBloomAdaptiveLuminancePercent, fBloomAdaptiveLuminanceScale, fBloomAmount, fBloomBlurRadius, fBloomContastLimit, fBloomContastMultiplier, fBloomMultiplier, fBloomTargetLuminance, fBloomThreshold, fLightIntensity, fTimeRestore.
Graphics.Atmosphere.SetValue.gotcha: Two confirmed key names are misspelled in the engine and must be passed exactly as-is: fBloomContastLimit and fBloomContastMultiplier (sic -- no 'r' in 'Contrast').

Graphics.Bloom.SetAdaptiveLuminancePerce.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Graphics) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. Corresponds to the fBloomAdaptiveLuminancePercent key that is confirmed in use via Graphics.Atmosphere.SetValue.

Graphics.Bloom.SetAdaptiveLuminanceScale.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Graphics) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. Corresponds to the fBloomAdaptiveLuminanceScale key that is confirmed in use via Graphics.Atmosphere.SetValue.

Graphics.Bloom.SetBlurRadius.doc: Sets the bloom blur radius. Confirmed in resident/mrxbootstrap.lua, called once at boot with 0.5 alongside the other post-process defaults.

Graphics.Bloom.SetMultiplier.doc: Sets the bloom multiplier. Confirmed in resident/mrxbootstrap.lua, called at boot with 0.

Graphics.Bloom.SetTargetLuminance.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Graphics) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. Corresponds to the fBloomTargetLuminance key that is confirmed in use via Graphics.Atmosphere.SetValue.

Graphics.Bloom.SetThreshold.doc: Sets the bloom brightness threshold. Confirmed in resident/mrxbootstrap.lua, called at boot with 0.775.

Graphics.Camera.RestoreFocusParams.doc: Reverts a Graphics.Camera.SetFocusParams depth-of-field override over the given duration. Confirmed in resident/emplaced.lua, resident/mrxactionhijack.lua, resident/mrxbriefing.lua and vz/xQ!L.lua, always with camera index 0.

Graphics.Camera.RestoreFovParams.doc: Reverts a Graphics.Camera.SetFovParams override over the given duration. Confirmed in resident/mrxbriefing.lua and vz/xQ!L.lua, called as RestoreFovParams(0, 1).

Graphics.Camera.RestoreNearFar.doc: Reverts a Graphics.Camera.SetNearFar override. Confirmed in vz/wifpmcinterior.lua, vz/xQ!L.lua and resident/mrxhq.lua, all called as RestoreNearFar(0).

Graphics.Camera.SetFocusParams.doc: Controls the depth-of-field blur transition -- near and far focus planes blending over a duration. Confirmed with 7 arguments during hijack and turret-mount cinematics (resident/mrxactionhijack.lua, resident/emplaced.lua); one call site uses only 6.
Graphics.Camera.SetFocusParams.sig: Graphics.Camera.SetFocusParams(nCameraIndex, nStartNear, nEndNear, nStartFar, nEndFar, nBlur, nDuration)
Graphics.Camera.SetFocusParams.gotcha: The first argument is a numeric camera index (0 at every call site seen), not a uGuid -- Graphics.Camera is a different table from the top-level Camera namespace, which does take a guid.

Graphics.Camera.SetLodParams.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Graphics) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. Presumed to control level-of-detail distance thresholds, by analogy with the sibling near/far/focus/FOV setters.

Graphics.Camera.SetNearFar.doc: Sets the render camera's near/far clip planes directly, as opposed to SetFocusParams' blended depth-of-field planes. Confirmed in vz/wifpmcinterior.lua and resident/mrxhq.lua, e.g. SetNearFar(0, 0.3, 500, 0) -- reach for it when an interior or a custom draw distance needs the far plane pulled in.
Graphics.Camera.SetNearFar.gotcha: The trailing 4th argument is 0 at every call site and its meaning is unconfirmed. First argument is a camera index, not a guid.

Graphics.Contrast.SetLimit.doc: Sets the post-process contrast limit. Confirmed in resident/mrxbootstrap.lua, called at boot with 0.1.

Graphics.Contrast.SetMultiplier.doc: Sets the post-process contrast multiplier. Confirmed in resident/mrxbootstrap.lua, called at boot with 1.5.

Graphics.Effect.AmbientSides.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Graphics) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. Presumed paired with Graphics.Effect.AmbientTop for directional ambient-lighting tuning.

Graphics.Effect.CameraFade.doc: Full-screen fade-to-black/fade-in keyed by a 0/1 amount. Confirmed in resident/mrxactionhijack.lua at the start and end of a hijack cinematic.
Graphics.Effect.CameraFade.gotcha: Not tied to a specific camera guid -- it is a global screen effect, unlike the per-camera calls on the top-level Camera namespace.

Graphics.FuelTrail.Extinguish.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Graphics) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. Presumed counterpart to Graphics.FuelTrail.Ignite.

Graphics.FuelTrail.Ignite.doc: Zero call sites anywhere in the decompiled corpus, including the vehicle fuel-tank damage code in resident/mrxpmc.lua. The name strongly suggests it starts a leaking-fuel particle trail, but no in-repo evidence connects it to that or any other system.
Graphics.FuelTrail.Ignite.gotcha: Argument shapes are completely unknown for the whole Graphics.FuelTrail sub-table -- test carefully in-game before relying on it.

Graphics.Monochrome.SetGradient.doc: Takes 10 numeric arguments; confirmed called twice back-to-back at boot in resident/mrxbootstrap.lua, presumably defining a two-stop colour-grading/tone curve for shadow and highlight ranges.
Graphics.Monochrome.SetGradient.sig: Graphics.Monochrome.SetGradient(n1, n2, n3, n4, n5, n6, n7, n8, n9, n10)
Graphics.Monochrome.SetGradient.gotcha: The exact per-argument meaning is not confirmed -- only that 10 numbers are passed and that the two boot calls cover different input ranges (0-128 and 128-255).

Gui.EnableFactionMarkers.doc: Toggles the faction marker overlay. No call sites in the decompiled corpus -- the boolean signature is inferred only by analogy to the confirmed Gui.EnablePlayerMarkers.

Gui.EnablePickupMarkers.doc: Toggles the pickup marker overlay. No call sites in the decompiled corpus -- the boolean signature is inferred only by analogy to the confirmed Gui.EnablePlayerMarkers.

Gui.EnableVehicleEntranceMarkers.doc: Toggles the vehicle-entrance marker overlay. No call sites in the decompiled corpus -- the boolean signature is inferred only by analogy to the confirmed Gui.EnablePlayerMarkers.

Gui.GetLanguageNum.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Gui) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. Presumed the numeric-ID counterpart to the confirmed Gui.GetLanguageName.

Gui.OutputToPIX.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Gui) enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. The name suggests a PIX (graphics-debugger) event/marker output hook for dev builds.

Gui._MarkerAdd.doc: Internal marker primitive with no call sites; the name corresponds closely to the public Marker.Add.
Gui._MarkerAdd.gotcha: Underscore-prefixed and almost certainly internal -- call the public Marker.Add instead. The 1:1 name correspondence is a well-supported hypothesis from two live pairs() dumps, not a confirmed engine-internals finding.

Gui._MarkerAdd3D.doc: Internal marker primitive with no call sites; the name corresponds closely to the public Marker.Add3D.
Gui._MarkerAdd3D.gotcha: Underscore-prefixed and almost certainly internal -- call the public Marker.Add3D instead.

Gui._MarkerAddDisc.doc: Internal marker primitive with no call sites; the name corresponds closely to the public Marker.AddDisc.
Gui._MarkerAddDisc.gotcha: Underscore-prefixed and almost certainly internal -- call the public Marker.AddDisc instead.

Gui._MarkerAddOld.doc: Internal marker primitive with no call sites. An older/legacy variant of Gui._MarkerAdd, judging by the name.
Gui._MarkerAddOld.gotcha: Flagged as a naming mismatch rather than an assumed pairing: its exact relationship to Marker.AddBlip -- the one public Marker function with no equally-named _Marker* counterpart -- is unconfirmed.

Gui._MarkerAddTripwire.doc: Internal marker primitive with no call sites; the name corresponds closely to the public Marker.AddTripwire.
Gui._MarkerAddTripwire.gotcha: Underscore-prefixed and almost certainly internal -- call the public Marker.AddTripwire instead.

Gui._MarkerHaltPulse.doc: Internal marker primitive with no call sites; the name corresponds closely to the public Marker.HaltPulse.
Gui._MarkerHaltPulse.gotcha: Underscore-prefixed and almost certainly internal -- call the public Marker.HaltPulse instead.

Gui._MarkerPulse.doc: Internal marker primitive with no call sites; the name corresponds closely to the public Marker.Pulse.
Gui._MarkerPulse.gotcha: Underscore-prefixed and almost certainly internal -- call the public Marker.Pulse instead.

Gui._MarkerRemove.doc: Internal marker primitive with no call sites; the name corresponds closely to the public Marker.Remove.
Gui._MarkerRemove.gotcha: Underscore-prefixed and almost certainly internal -- call the public Marker.Remove instead.

Gui._MarkerSetBlipLimit.doc: Internal marker primitive with no call sites; the closest public function by behaviour is Marker.SetGroupedBlipLimit.
Gui._MarkerSetBlipLimit.gotcha: Not an exact name match to any public Marker function -- the pairing with Marker.SetGroupedBlipLimit is by closest function, not by name.

Gui._MarkerSetColor.doc: Internal marker primitive with no call sites; the name corresponds closely to the public Marker.SetColor.
Gui._MarkerSetColor.gotcha: Underscore-prefixed and almost certainly internal -- call the public Marker.SetColor instead.

Gui._MarkerSetFollowGuid.doc: Internal marker primitive with no call sites; the name corresponds closely to the public Marker.SetFollowGuid.
Gui._MarkerSetFollowGuid.gotcha: Underscore-prefixed and almost certainly internal -- call the public Marker.SetFollowGuid instead.

Gui._MarkerSetLocation.doc: Internal marker primitive with no call sites; the name corresponds closely to the public Marker.SetLocation.
Gui._MarkerSetLocation.gotcha: Underscore-prefixed and almost certainly internal -- call the public Marker.SetLocation instead.

Gui._MarkerSetScale.doc: Internal marker primitive with no call sites; the name corresponds closely to the public Marker.SetScale.
Gui._MarkerSetScale.gotcha: Underscore-prefixed and almost certainly internal -- call the public Marker.SetScale instead.

Hud.CardFanfare.Commence.doc: Shows the contact-card fanfare popup -- faction, title, name, job title, two phone fields and an email, with a display time and optional callback. Confirmed in resident/mrxbriefing.lua; the full field list comes from the resident/mrxguiinterface.lua implementation.
Hud.CardFanfare.Commence.sig: Hud.CardFanfare:Commence({sFaction=s, sTitle=s, sName=s, sJobTitle=s, sPhone1=s, sPhone2=s, sEmail=s, nDisplayTime=n, fCallback=fn, tCallbackData=t})

Hud.ContactFanfare.Commence.doc: Shows the new-contact fanfare popup. Confirmed in vz/meccon001.lua; the implementation in resident/mrxguiinterface.lua reads tArgs.fCallback and tArgs.tCallbackData.

Hud.EventFanfare.Commence.doc: Shows the standard event toast, keyed by an sType from the fanfare catalog plus the text to display. Confirmed across resident/mrxpmc.lua, resident/mrxunlockfanfare.lua and resident/mrxtaskjobverifyset.lua, and confirmed working by live testing -- the go-to call for a custom on-screen toast.
Hud.EventFanfare.Commence.gotcha: The text field is vText; the implementation only normalises a legacy sText field into vText when vText is absent.

Hud.Fanfare.AddItem.doc: Adds one ledger item to a fanfare being built. Confirmed in resident/mrxtaskcontract.lua, called repeatedly between Hud.Fanfare:Create and Hud.Fanfare:Commence.

Hud.Fanfare.Commence.doc: Fires the fanfare that was built with Create/AddItem. Confirmed in vz/mecjob.lua as Hud.Fanfare:Commence({}); the implementation reads tArgs.nSlowdownDuration.

Hud.Fanfare.Create.doc: Opens a new ledger-style fanfare. Confirmed in vz/mecjob.lua and resident/mrxtaskcontract.lua as the first step of a Create -> AddItem -> Commence sequence.

Hud.JobFanfare.Complete.doc: Job-completed fanfare. No call site was checked in the wiki's pass -- presumed to take a table argument like its confirmed siblings.

Hud.JobFanfare.Failed.doc: Job-failed fanfare. No call site was checked in the wiki's pass -- presumed to take a table argument like its confirmed siblings.

Hud.MessageBox.AddMessage.doc: Queues an objective-style HUD message and returns a message-id table. Widely confirmed (resident/mrxguiinterface.lua's DisplayObjectiveMessage, resident/mrxsupport.lua, resident/mrxtaskcontract.lua, several vz/ scripts); a minimal {sMessage = "..."} table works too.
Hud.MessageBox.AddMessage.sig: tMsgIds = Hud.MessageBox:AddMessage({sMessage=s, nPriority=n, nDuration=n, bClearBuffer=b, bAllowsAppends=b, fCallback=fn})
Hud.MessageBox.AddMessage.gotcha: Capture the returned id table -- it is what Hud.MessageBox:ModifyPendingMessage and RemovePendingMessage expect.

Hud.MessageBox.Clear.doc: Clears the message box. Confirmed in resident/mrxtaskcontract.lua, called with an empty table.

Hud.MessageBox.ModifyPendingMessage.doc: Rewrites a still-pending message in place, using the id table AddMessage returned, and returns a success boolean. Confirmed in resident/mrxguiinterface.lua.

Hud.MessageBox.RemovePendingMessage.doc: Removes a still-pending message. No call site was checked in the wiki's pass -- presumed to take the same message-id table AddMessage returns, by analogy with ModifyPendingMessage.

Hud.ObjectiveTray.ClearSlot.doc: Clears one numbered objective-tray slot. Extremely common in vz/ mission scripts, both as ClearSlot({vPlayer = nil, nSlot = 1}) and the shorter ClearSlot({nSlot = 1}).
Hud.ObjectiveTray.ClearSlot.gotcha: The vPlayer field appears to be optional -- both forms occur in shipped scripts.

Hud.ObjectiveTray.SetSlotToImage.doc: Puts an image in an objective-tray slot. Confirmed in resident/mrxguiinterface.lua alongside SetSlotToText in the same dispatch function; the exact field list was not fully confirmed.

Hud.ObjectiveTray.SetSlotToText.doc: Sets the text shown in one of the small numbered objective-tray slots. Dozens of confirmed call sites across vz/ mission scripts -- the standard way to drive on-screen objective text.

Hud.ObjectiveTray.SetSlotToWidget.doc: Puts a widget in an objective-tray slot. No call site was checked in the wiki's pass -- presumed similar in shape to SetSlotToText/SetSlotToImage.

Hud.Radar.AddLineRegion.doc: Draws a line region (a boundary outline) on the radar from a pre-built region-parameter table. Confirmed in resident/factionzone.lua, resident/mrxguiinterface.lua and vz/wifvzboundary.lua.

Hud.Radar.AddObjective.doc: Adds a radar blip for an objective, with colour, size, texture, target guid and sort order. Confirmed extensively -- resident/blippable.lua's objective-marker class, mrxfactionmanager, mrxhq, mrxsupport, outpost, mrxtaskobjective and more.
Hud.Radar.AddObjective.sig: Hud.Radar:AddObjective({sName=s, nR=n, nG=n, nB=n, nWidth=n, nHeight=n, sTexture=s, uGuid=u, bSticky=b, bRotate=b, bOriented=b, nSortOrder=n, bDontNetSync=b})

Hud.Radar.AnimateObjectiveAlpha.doc: Animates an existing radar blip's alpha. Confirmed in resident/dangerousbuilding.lua and vz/oilcon002.lua with a table argument; the field list beyond a presumed name key was not pinned down.

Hud.Radar.AnimateObjectiveSize.doc: Pulses/animates an existing radar blip's size, e.g. AnimateObjectiveSize({sName = sBlipName}). Confirmed in resident/dangerousbuilding.lua, mrxparkinglotmanager, mrxtaskobjective and two vz/ scripts.

Hud.Radar.AnimateObjectiveSonar.doc: Plays the sonar-ping animation on a radar blip. Confirmed in resident/mrxfactionmanager.lua with a table argument.

Hud.Radar.RemoveLineRegion.doc: Removes a radar line region, most often as RemoveLineRegion({uGuid = uBoundary}). Confirmed in the same three files as Hud.Radar:AddLineRegion.

Hud.Radar.RemoveObjective.doc: Removes an objective blip by name. Confirmed widely alongside Hud.Radar:AddObjective.
Hud.Radar.RemoveObjective.gotcha: One shipped call site (vz/pmccon001.lua) passes a positional array shape, Hud.Radar:RemoveObjective({uDoor}), so the accepted shapes are not uniform.

Hud.Radar.UnanimateObjective.doc: Stops a blip animation. No call site was checked in the wiki's pass -- presumed counterpart to the Animate* family.

Hud.Radar.UpdateObjective.doc: Updates an existing radar blip from a pre-built config table matching AddObjective's shape. Confirmed in resident/mrxtaskobjective.lua.

Hud.ResourceCounter.Hide.doc: Hides the HUD resource counter. Confirmed in resident/mrxbriefing.lua, called with an empty table.

Hud.ResourceCounter.SetCash.doc: Drives the cash readout in the HUD resource counter, with an optional reason string and increment for the change animation. Confirmed in resident/mrxpmc.lua's DisplayCash/DisplayResources.

Hud.ResourceCounter.SetFuel.doc: Drives the fuel readout, taking the current value, the max, and an optional increment. Confirmed in resident/mrxpmc.lua's DisplayResources.

Hud.ResourceCounter.SetSuppressed.doc: Hides or shows the cash and fuel readouts independently. Confirmed in resident/mrxstate.lua (both directions) and resident/mrxmissionflow.lua.

Hud.ResourceCounter.Show.doc: Shows the HUD resource counter for nDuration. Confirmed in resident/mrxbriefing.lua as Show({nDuration = -1}).

Hud.SupportFanfare.AddItem.doc: Adds an item to the support fanfare. The implementation in resident/mrxguiinterface.lua reads tArgs.sTexture, sItemName, sFaction, sContactName and sBlipName.

Hud.SupportFanfare.Commence.doc: Fires the support fanfare built with Create/AddItem. Implemented in resident/mrxguiinterface.lua.

Hud.SupportFanfare.Create.doc: Opens a support fanfare. The implementation in resident/mrxguiinterface.lua reads tArgs.fCallback and tArgs.tCallbackData.

Hud.TextFanfare.Commence.doc: Shows a two-line text fanfare with entrance, display and fade times plus an optional callback. No direct call site was found, but the field list is confirmed from the resident/mrxguiinterface.lua implementation.
Hud.TextFanfare.Commence.sig: Hud.TextFanfare:Commence({sLine1=s, sLine2=s, nEntranceTime=n, nDisplayTime=n, nFadeTime=n, fCallback=fn, tCallbackData=t})

Hud.Tutorial.SetText.doc: The lowest-level entry point for a tutorial HUD message: SetText({vPlayer = Player.GetLocalPlayer(), sText = sMessage}) shows it, and calling again with sText = nil clears it. Confirmed in resident/mrxtutorialmanager.lua.
Hud.Tutorial.SetText.gotcha: Do not call it directly in a mod -- use MrxTutorialManager.ShowMessage/HideMessage, which additionally handles net-sync, duplicate suppression and identifier-based message ownership that this call bypasses.

Hud.Tutorial.ShowTutorialForObject.doc: Shows a tutorial prompt tied to an object. No call site was checked in the wiki's pass -- presumed a table argument like the confirmed Hud.Tutorial:SetText.

Hud.Tutorial.ShowTutorialOnscreen.doc: Shows an on-screen tutorial prompt. No call site was checked in the wiki's pass -- presumed a table argument like the confirmed Hud.Tutorial:SetText.

Human.Inventory.DropWeapon.doc: Makes a character drop a specific weapon. Very common in real scripts, always with a character uGuid and a weapon uGuid.

Human.Inventory.EquipWeapon.doc: Swaps a character's currently-held weapon for a weapon uGuid previously fetched via GetPrimaryWeapon/GetSecondaryWeapon. Confirmed in resident/mrxshootinggallery.lua.

Human.Inventory.GetAllWeapons.doc: Returns a table of the weapon guids a character is carrying. Extremely common in real scripts (resident/hero.lua, resident/soldier.lua).
Human.Inventory.GetAllWeapons.gotcha: Some call sites pass a second boolean argument (e.g. in resident/mrxplayer.lua); its effect is unconfirmed.

Human.Inventory.GetPrimaryWeapon.doc: Returns the primary weapon uGuid for a character, e.g. Human.Inventory.GetPrimaryWeapon(Player.GetLocalCharacter()). Confirmed in resident/mrxstatsmanager.lua.

Human.Inventory.GetSecondaryWeapon.doc: Returns the secondary weapon uGuid for a character. Confirmed in resident/mrxshootinggallery.lua.

Human.Inventory.ReloadAll.doc: Reloads all of a character's weapons. Confirmed in one real call site with a character uGuid and a boolean, vz/xQ!L.lua.

Human.Inventory.SetAllWeapons.doc: Sets a character's whole loadout from an array-style table of weapon uGuids, e.g. SetAllWeapons(uCharGuid, {uPrimary, uGrenade, uC4}) in resident/mrxplayer.lua.
Human.Inventory.SetAllWeapons.gotcha: Some vz/ scripts pass a single uGuid where the table is expected, so the full set of accepted argument shapes is not pinned down.

Junk.ActivateAlarm.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Junk) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus; independently corroborated 2026-07-22 as a genuine native binding by a static luaL_Reg registration-table dump. Presumed a one-directional counterpart to Junk.ToggleAlarm.
Junk.ActivateAlarm.gotcha: resident/alarm.lua calls its own local AlarmActivated/AlarmDeactivated rather than this, so the relationship is inferred from naming only. The binding audit proves table membership, not argument shape.

Junk.CreateRegion.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Junk) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus; independently corroborated 2026-07-22 as a genuine native binding by the static luaL_Reg registration-table audit -- membership only, no argument shape recovered.

Junk.DescribeGuid.doc: The name strongly suggests a debug helper returning a human-readable description (type/name/state) for a uGuid, which would be directly useful for object-identification work.
Junk.DescribeGuid.gotcha: Unconfirmed and untested -- no call sites anywhere in the corpus. Treat it as a lead to probe live, not a documented API.

Junk.GetModelBBoxExtents.doc: Returns a model's bounding-box extents along each axis as three numbers (a boat measured 19.98, 18.74, 22.71). Confirmed live 2026-07-22 -- the way to size an object before placing or fitting something around it.
Junk.GetModelBBoxExtents.gotcha: Takes a uGuid, NOT a model/template name string -- easy to assume otherwise for a model-lookup function, since Pg.Spawn wants a name. The signature comes entirely from live probing; there are no call sites in the corpus.

Junk.SpawnHomingProjectile.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Junk) enumeration with no call sites; corroborated 2026-07-22 as a genuine native binding by the static luaL_Reg audit. The likeliest candidate for the mechanism behind AntiAir's homing missiles, since resident/antiair.lua never calls Airstrike anywhere.
Junk.SpawnHomingProjectile.gotcha: That AntiAir connection is inference from the name, not a confirmed call chain, and no argument shape was recovered.

Junk.SpawnWithModel.doc: Investigated in full as a possible additive-model-spawning route and confirmed a dead end -- see the wiki's dedicated writeup. No call sites in the corpus.
Junk.SpawnWithModel.gotcha: Not a working spawner as understood; do not build on it.

Junk.ToggleAlarm.doc: Toggles an alarm object -- the function that actually runs when a player interacts with an alarm. Confirmed in resident/alarm.lua, wired as the Event.ContextAction callback for the alarm object.
Junk.ToggleAlarm.gotcha: Genuinely gameplay-relevant despite living on the dev/debug-flavoured Junk namespace.

Marker.SetColor.doc: Recolours an existing marker. No call sites in the corpus -- the RGB signature is inferred only by analogy to the confirmed Marker.Add*/Pulse functions.

Marker.SetFollowGuid.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Marker) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. The name suggests re-attaching an existing marker to follow a different object.

Marker.SetGroupedBlipLimit.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Marker) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. Presumably caps how many blips of a group collapse into a single minimap icon; corresponds by function, not exact name, to Gui._MarkerSetBlipLimit.

Marker.SetLocation.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Marker) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. The name suggests moving an existing marker to new world coordinates.

Math.CrossProduct.doc: Returns the 3-component cross product of two 3D vectors. Live-probed directly against a running game and the only member of this table with a fully live-confirmed argument and return shape.
Math.CrossProduct.sig: cx, cy, cz = Math.CrossProduct(ax, ay, az, bx, by, bz)

Math.PolarToRect.doc: Named as a member of this table by the corpus call-prefix cross-reference; never live-probed. Presumed a polar-to-rectangular coordinate conversion by name, but the argument shape is a guess, not a confirmed signature.

Math.abs.doc: Named as an existing member of this table by the corpus call-prefix cross-reference; never live-probed. Presumed absolute value by name; signature unconfirmed.

Math.deg.doc: Live-probed against a running game; takes and returns a number. Read as radians-to-degrees from the name and from plausible degree-range values in the probe, but the exact conversion was not verified against reference values.
Math.deg.gotcha: Capitalised Math is a native engine table, entirely unrelated to the lowercase Lua math table -- Math.deg and math.deg are not the same function.

Math.exp.doc: Live-probed against a running game; takes and returns a number. Presumed the standard exponential function by name; not independently verified against known values.

Math.round.doc: Live-probed against a running game; takes and returns a number.
Math.round.gotcha: Rounding behaviour (half-up vs half-to-even, and whether a decimal-places argument is accepted) was never tested beyond the plain single-argument call.

MessageBox.AddMessage.doc: Queues an objective-style HUD message and returns a message-id table. Widely confirmed (resident/mrxguiinterface.lua's DisplayObjectiveMessage, resident/mrxsupport.lua, resident/mrxtaskcontract.lua, several vz/ scripts); a minimal {sMessage = "..."} table works too.
MessageBox.AddMessage.sig: tMsgIds = Hud.MessageBox:AddMessage({sMessage=s, nPriority=n, nDuration=n, bClearBuffer=b, bAllowsAppends=b, fCallback=fn})
MessageBox.AddMessage.gotcha: Capture the returned id table -- it is what Hud.MessageBox:ModifyPendingMessage and RemovePendingMessage expect.

MessageBox.ModifyPendingMessage.doc: Rewrites a still-pending message in place, using the id table AddMessage returned, and returns a success boolean. Confirmed in resident/mrxguiinterface.lua.

MessageBox.RemovePendingMessage.doc: Removes a still-pending message. No call site was checked in the wiki's pass -- presumed to take the same message-id table AddMessage returns, by analogy with ModifyPendingMessage.

Net.ExitFriendsLobby.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Net) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. Presumed counterpart to the confirmed Net.EnterFriendsLobby.

Net.SendEvent_AddDangerousBuilding.doc: Part of the Net.SendEvent_* family: a one-way, server-to-client broadcast of one specific named network event, used to keep HUD/UI/world state (fanfare cards, PDA and radar blips, objective markers, messages) identical on every client. Confirmed at resident/dangerousbuilding.lua:134. The wiki groups it with the family rather than giving it its own row, because its argument shape adds nothing beyond the family convention -- arguments match the data being synced.
Net.SendEvent_AddDangerousBuilding.gotcha: Gate it behind Net.IsServer() -- every call site in the corpus does, sometimes with an extra condition such as not Player.IsLocal(uPlayerGuid).

Object.ApplyAngularImpulse.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Object) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus; arguments beyond the presumed leading uGuid are unconfirmed.

Object.AreEqual.doc: Compares two object guids and returns a boolean. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22; still no call sites in the decompiled corpus.

Object.BeginQueuedAcceleration.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Object) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. Presumably pairs with Object.QueueAcceleration, but that pairing is inferred from naming only.

Object.GetHardpointPitch.doc: Returns a named hardpoint's pitch in degrees. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22, settling an earlier by-analogy guess; still no call sites in the corpus.

Object.GetHardpointYaw.doc: Returns a named hardpoint's yaw in degrees. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22, settling an earlier by-analogy guess; still no call sites in the corpus.

Object.GetHeightAboveTerrain.doc: Returns an object's height above ground or seabed, in metres. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22 -- useful for altitude checks on aircraft or dropped cargo.
Object.GetHeightAboveTerrain.gotcha: The return meaning comes from the live probe, not from source: there are no call sites anywhere in the corpus.

Object.GetInvincible.doc: Returns whether an object is currently invincible, as a boolean. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22; still no call sites in the corpus.

Object.GetModelName.doc: Returns an object's model name-hash handle. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22.
Object.GetModelName.gotcha: Returns userdata, NOT a string, despite the name. String concatenation and string.* calls will not work on the result without conversion -- treat it as an opaque handle.

Object.GetVelocitySquared.doc: Returns speed squared -- the squared magnitude of the object's velocity. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22; handy for distance/speed comparisons without a square root.
Object.GetVelocitySquared.gotcha: Squared, not raw speed: compare against a squared threshold, or take the square root before treating it as a speed.

Object.GetVelocityVector.doc: Returns the object's velocity as three components, vx, vy, vz. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22.
Object.GetVelocityVector.gotcha: Returns three values where the similarly-named Object.GetVelocity returns a single scalar.

Object.GetWinchState.doc: Reads a winch's state. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22 only on a non-winch object, where it returns nil.
Object.GetWinchState.gotcha: nil on a non-winch object is expected behaviour, not a bug. What it returns on an object that does have a winch was never exercised -- the setter uses string states like "deployed", so a string return is inferred, not confirmed.

Object.HasWinch.doc: Returns whether an object has a winch, as a boolean. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22 -- the safe guard to call before the rest of the winch family.

Object.IsWinching.doc: Reports whether a winch is currently winching. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22 only on a non-winch object, where it returns nil.
Object.IsWinching.gotcha: nil on a non-winch object is expected behaviour, not evidence of a broken call -- gate on Object.HasWinch first.

Object.RemoveFromDisposer.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Object) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. Presumed counterpart to the confirmed Object.AddToDisposer.

Object.SetHibernationDistance.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Object) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. Presumed to pair with the confirmed Object.GetHibernationDistance / Object.RevertHibernationDistance.

Object.SetPositionToObject.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Object) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus.
Object.SetPositionToObject.gotcha: The signature is inferred only by analogy to the confirmed Object.SetTransformToObject -- treat with caution.

Object.TransformLocalToWorld.doc: Converts a point from an object's local space to world space, returning x, y, z. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22 -- reach for it to place something at an offset from a moving or rotated object.
Object.TransformLocalToWorld.sig: x, y, z = Object.TransformLocalToWorld(uGuid, lx, ly, lz)
Object.TransformLocalToWorld.gotcha: The signature comes from the live probe, not source: there are no call sites anywhere in the corpus.

ObjectFilter.AddObject.doc: Name and table membership confirmed by the corpus call-prefix cross-reference; never live-probed. Presumed by naming to add a specific object guid into a filter's candidate set; signature unconfirmed.

ObjectFilter.Create.doc: Name and table membership confirmed by the corpus call-prefix cross-reference; never live-probed. Presumed by naming to construct a new filter handle -- the first step of an inferred Create/AddObject/SetFilter/SetRelation/Eval builder pattern.
ObjectFilter.Create.gotcha: The builder-pattern reading of this namespace is inference from names alone; no signature is confirmed for any member.

ObjectFilter.Eval.doc: Name and table membership confirmed by the corpus call-prefix cross-reference; never live-probed. Presumed by naming to evaluate a configured filter and return its matches; signature unconfirmed.

ObjectFilter.GetCoopPlayerGuid.doc: Name and table membership confirmed by the corpus call-prefix cross-reference; never live-probed.
ObjectFilter.GetCoopPlayerGuid.gotcha: Does not obviously fit the Create/AddObject/SetFilter/SetRelation/Eval builder reading -- plausibly a convenience getter feeding a co-op player's guid into a filter, but its relationship to the other five is not confirmed.

ObjectFilter.SetFilter.doc: Name and table membership confirmed by the corpus call-prefix cross-reference; never live-probed. Presumed by naming to set a filter predicate on a filter handle; signature unconfirmed.

ObjectFilter.SetRelation.doc: Name and table membership confirmed by the corpus call-prefix cross-reference; never live-probed. Presumed by naming to set a relational condition (combining criteria, or a spatial/faction relation) on a filter handle; signature unconfirmed.

ObjectState.SendMessage.doc: Name and table membership confirmed by the corpus call-prefix cross-reference; never live-probed and no call site with a concrete argument list was captured. Presumed by naming to send a message/signal to an object.
ObjectState.SendMessage.gotcha: A leading-uGuid argument shape is a guess by analogy with other namespaces, not a confirmed signature.

ObjectState.StartEmitter.doc: Name and table membership confirmed by the corpus call-prefix cross-reference; never live-probed. Presumed by naming to start a particle emitter attached to an object, but the argument shape is a guess from the name only.

ObjectiveTray.ClearSlot.doc: Clears one numbered objective-tray slot. Extremely common in vz/ mission scripts, both as ClearSlot({vPlayer = nil, nSlot = 1}) and the shorter ClearSlot({nSlot = 1}).
ObjectiveTray.ClearSlot.gotcha: The vPlayer field appears to be optional -- both forms occur in shipped scripts.

ObjectiveTray.SetSlotToImage.doc: Puts an image in an objective-tray slot. Confirmed in resident/mrxguiinterface.lua alongside SetSlotToText in the same dispatch function; the exact field list was not fully confirmed.

ObjectiveTray.SetSlotToText.doc: Sets the text shown in one of the small numbered objective-tray slots. Dozens of confirmed call sites across vz/ mission scripts -- the standard way to drive on-screen objective text.

ObjectiveTray.SetSlotToWidget.doc: Puts a widget in an objective-tray slot. No call site was checked in the wiki's pass -- presumed similar in shape to SetSlotToText/SetSlotToImage.

Pg.AddSkirmishTemplate.doc: Part of the pursuit/skirmish director. Live-probed 2026-07-22: executes without error or crash, but no visible effect was observable from an isolated test spot and the exact argument shape was not pinned down.

Pg.AdjustPursuitLevel.doc: Live-probed 2026-07-22: executes without error or crash. No visible effect from an isolated test spot -- it needs an actively engaged pursuit with faction units present to show what it adjusts.
Pg.AdjustPursuitLevel.gotcha: A live lead, not a settled signature: the exact argument shape was never pinned down.

Pg.AdjustPursuitTimer.doc: Live-probed 2026-07-22, same story as Pg.AdjustPursuitLevel: executes without error or crash, no visible effect observable in isolation, exact argument shape not pinned down.

Pg.ClearCustomPursuit.doc: Exists per the live enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. Presumed the inverse of Pg.SetCustomPursuit by naming, unconfirmed.

Pg.FastCollectBoats.doc: Returns a table of boat guids within fRadius of (x, y, z). Live-confirmed 2026-07-22, matching the rest of the FastCollect* family shape.
Pg.FastCollectBoats.gotcha: The optional trailing filter argument seen on FastCollectHumans/FastCollectGroundVehicles was not exercised for this member -- presumed present by family pattern, not confirmed.

Pg.FastCollectCars.doc: Returns a table of car guids within fRadius of (x, y, z). Live-confirmed 2026-07-22 in the same probe as Pg.FastCollectBoats.
Pg.FastCollectCars.gotcha: The optional trailing filter argument seen on other FastCollect* members was not confirmed for this one.

Pg.FastCollectGroundVehiclesExceptTanks.doc: Returns a table of ground-vehicle guids within fRadius of (x, y, z), excluding tanks -- the filtered sibling of Pg.FastCollectGroundVehicles. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22.
Pg.FastCollectGroundVehiclesExceptTanks.gotcha: The optional trailing filter argument seen on other FastCollect* members was not confirmed for this one.

Pg.FastCollectJets.doc: Returns a table of jet guids within fRadius of (x, y, z). Live-confirmed 2026-07-22.
Pg.FastCollectJets.gotcha: The optional trailing filter argument seen on other FastCollect* members was not confirmed for this one.

Pg.FastCollectProps.doc: Returns a table of prop guids within fRadius of (x, y, z). Live-confirmed 2026-07-22.
Pg.FastCollectProps.gotcha: The optional trailing filter argument seen on other FastCollect* members was not confirmed for this one.

Pg.FastCollectUsables.doc: Returns a table of usable-object guids within fRadius of (x, y, z). Live-confirmed 2026-07-22.
Pg.FastCollectUsables.gotcha: The optional trailing filter argument seen on other FastCollect* members was not confirmed for this one.

Pg.GetAllGuidsByName.doc: Returns a table of every guid matching a designer-assigned name, e.g. Pg.GetAllGuidsByName('L300') returned {800075FD}. Reach for it instead of Pg.GetGuidByName when several objects share one name. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22.
Pg.GetAllGuidsByName.gotcha: Returns a table, where the near-identically-named Pg.GetGuidByName returns a single guid. Zero call sites anywhere in the corpus -- the signature comes from the live probe, not from source.

Pg.GetBoundaryRadius.doc: Takes a guid and returns a number. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22.
Pg.GetBoundaryRadius.gotcha: Despite the naming symmetry it is not confirmed as the getter for the global Pg.SetBoundaryRadius(fRadius) setter -- it takes a guid where that setter takes none, so it is more likely a per-object/per-boundary query. Treat the pairing as naming-only.

Pg.GetTetherDiameterEnd.doc: Takes a guid and returns a number. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22; its sibling Pg.GetTetherDiameterStart was not part of that probe batch and remains unconfirmed.

Pg.GetWarningRadius.doc: Takes a guid and returns a number. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22.

Pg.ReloadAsset.doc: Exists per the live enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. Presumed to combine unload and load by naming, unconfirmed.

Pg.SetGlobalSkirmishState.doc: Part of the pursuit/skirmish director rather than asset streaming, despite where it originally appeared in the dump. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22: accepted both a boolean and an integer without erroring, but showed no visible effect from an isolated test spot -- it needs an actively engaged skirmish to observe.

Pg.SetSkirmishTable.doc: Part of the pursuit/skirmish director. Live-probed 2026-07-22: executes without error or crash, but no visible effect was observable from an isolated test spot and the exact argument shape was not pinned down.

Pg.SpawnPlayerAdvanced.doc: Exists per the live enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus and no confirmed usage. Explicitly flagged as still unmapped after the 2026-07-22 live-confirmation pass -- a known gap needing a dedicated probing pass.

Pg.SpawnRelative.doc: Exists per the live enumeration with no call sites in the decompiled corpus. Presumed to spawn relative to an anchor object by naming symmetry with Pg.SpawnFromCamera, but that is inference, not evidence; still unmapped after the 2026-07-22 pass.

Player.GetCurrentLocalPlayers.doc: Returns the number of local players currently joined, with no arguments. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22 (returned 1 at test time) -- the local-only counterpart to Player.GetCurrentPlayers.

Player.GetLocalId.doc: Takes a local-player-slot index and returns that slot's id as a number. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22, correcting an earlier no-argument guess.
Player.GetLocalId.gotcha: The argument is a slot index, not a uGuid, and 0-based vs 1-based indexing is unconfirmed -- test both 0 and 1 as the first slot. A bad index returns nil silently rather than erroring, as everywhere in this engine.

Player.GetMaximumLocalPlayers.doc: Returns how many local/split-screen player slots this build supports, with no arguments. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22 (returned 2).

Player.GetOutBoundary.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Player) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. Presumed getter counterpart to Player.SetOutBoundary.

Player.GetProfileCharacter.doc: Returns the profile's selected character index for a local-player slot. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22, correcting an earlier no-argument guess.
Player.GetProfileCharacter.gotcha: Takes the same local-player-slot idx as Player.GetLocalId/IsJoined, not a uGuid. Distinct from the no-argument Player.GetProfileCostume.

Player.GetProfileUpgrade.doc: Returns a number for a local-player slot's profile upgrade state. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22, correcting an earlier bare-placeholder signature.
Player.GetProfileUpgrade.gotcha: Takes the same local-player-slot idx as Player.GetLocalId/GetProfileCharacter, not a uGuid.

Player.GetSeat.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Player) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. Vehicle.GetSeatFromRider and Vehicle.GetFromRider cover similar ground from the vehicle side and do have real call sites -- prefer those.

Player.GetViewport.doc: Returns 5 values for a local-player slot: width, height, x, y, and a fifth value of unconfirmed meaning (live example: 2560, 1440, 0, 0, 0). Live-confirmed 2026-07-22 -- reach for it when positioning HUD elements against the real viewport.
Player.GetViewport.gotcha: The argument is a local-player-slot index, not a uPlayerGuid as earlier guessed.

Player.IsJoined.doc: Returns whether a local player is joined in a given slot, as a boolean. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22.
Player.IsJoined.gotcha: The argument is the local-player-slot idx shared with Player.GetLocalId, not a uPlayerGuid as previously guessed.

Player.SetPlayerStart.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Player) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. Presumed setter counterpart to Player.GetPlayerStart.

Sound.IsActionLevelLockedMusic.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Sound) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. Presumed the getter counterpart to Sound.LockActionLevelMusic, by naming only.
