Sound.TestCueSound.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Sound) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. The Test prefix suggests a debug/dev-console variant of Sound.CueSound.

Sound.TestPauseSound.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Sound) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. Presumed a debug/dev-console variant of Sound.PauseSound, by naming only.

Sound.TestStopSound.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Sound) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. Presumed a debug/dev-console variant of Sound.StopSound, by naming only.

Sound.UnloadBank.doc: Unloads a sound bank by name and type. No call sites in the corpus -- presumed the synchronous counterpart to Sound.LoadBank, by naming only.

Sound._SummonEd.doc: Exists per the live pairs(Sound) enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. The leading underscore matches this codebase's private/internal convention; "Ed" plausibly names an internal editor or debug-visualisation hook, but the name is the only clue available.

Sys.Clock.doc: Callable with no arguments and returns a plain number. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22.
Sys.Clock.gotcha: What the number means is still unconfirmed -- raw tick count versus clock-seconds was never settled.

Sys.Date.doc: Returns the current date and time as a string in MM/DD/YY HH:MM:SS format, with no arguments. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22.
Sys.Date.gotcha: Unlike its numeric Time & Clock siblings, this one returns a formatted string, not a number.

Sys.DiffTime.doc: Exists per the live enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. Presumed to compute a difference between two time values by naming, unconfirmed.

Sys.IsAutosaveEnabled.doc: Exists per the live enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. Presumed getter counterpart to Sys.SetAutosaveEnabled, unconfirmed.

Sys.MemUsage.doc: Callable with no arguments and returns a plain number, confirming the presumed memory-diagnostics role. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22.

Sys.RealTime.doc: Callable with no arguments and returns a plain number. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22; consistent with the presumed real-world-clock counterpart to Sys.MainTime, paired with Sys.RealTimeStamp.
Sys.RealTime.gotcha: The unit and epoch are unconfirmed -- only that a number comes back.

Sys.Time.doc: Callable with no arguments and returns a plain number. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22; the probe found Sys.Time, Sys.RealTime and Sys.Clock all returning the same number shape, with no way yet to tell them apart.

Sys.ToStringL.doc: Exists per the live enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. Presumed a localised/long string conversion by naming, unconfirmed.

Sys.WriteToConsole.doc: Exists per the live enumeration with no call sites in the corpus. Presumed a debug-console print by naming, unconfirmed.

Vehicle.GetFromSeat.doc: Takes a vehicle guid and a seat identifier. Live-probed 2026-07-22 and inconclusive: neither 'd' (string) nor 0 (number) as the seat argument returned anything but nil.
Vehicle.GetFromSeat.gotcha: Not a working call yet -- the correct seat-id shape is unconfirmed. Try a seat guid from Vehicle.GetSeatByType/GetSeatToSeat rather than a guessed literal.

Vehicle.GetRiderFromSeat.doc: Takes a vehicle guid and a seat identifier; presumed the inverse of Vehicle.GetSeatFromRider by naming symmetry. Live-probed 2026-07-22 with the same inconclusive result as Vehicle.GetFromSeat.
Vehicle.GetRiderFromSeat.gotcha: Neither 'd' nor 0 as the seat argument returned anything but nil -- the correct seat-id shape is still unconfirmed.

Vehicle.IsFlipped.doc: Returns whether a vehicle is flipped over, as a boolean. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22; still no call sites in the corpus.

Vehicle.IsHijackBad.doc: Returns a boolean about hijack viability. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22.
Vehicle.IsHijackBad.gotcha: The probe did not disambiguate which guid it expects -- hijacker character or vehicle. Naming symmetry with the adjacent uHijacker-taking hijack functions makes the hijacker likelier, but that is inference.

Vehicle.RestoreAmmo.doc: Refills a vehicle's ammo. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22 as a write with no return value; still no call sites in the corpus.

Vehicle.RestoreHealth.doc: Heals a vehicle to full health -- confirmed live 2026-07-22 (98.9 to 100 in the probe). A write with no return value.

Vehicle.SetTurretYaw.doc: Sets a vehicle turret's yaw from a numeric angle. Live-confirmed 2026-07-22 as a write with no return value.
Vehicle.SetTurretYaw.gotcha: Presumed analogous to the confirmed Vehicle.SetTurretPitch by naming only -- including whether it is orientation-only, which this probe did not re-verify.

math.doc: Standard Lua 5.1 math functions that this game's stripped runtime was missing, patched back in by lua-bridge. ADDITIVE -- the engine's own math.floor/abs/max/min and its separate math.randf() are untouched, so this list is not the whole of math.

TCP.doc: A tiny outbound TCP helper added by lua-bridge. Loopback destinations only, by design.

Loader.doc: The lua-bridge mod's own API -- printing to its log, reading the keyboard, persisting a variable across a level load, and pushing a line to a connected WebSocket. Not part of the game: these exist only because the .asi is loaded, which is why nothing in the decompiled base-game scripts calls them.

assert.doc: Raises an error when v is false or nil, otherwise returns everything it was given. Added by lua-bridge as a Lua polyfill over the engine's existing error() -- stock Lua 5.1 has it, this game's stripped runtime did not. Idempotent and re-applied on every pump batch, so a _G wipe across a level transition cannot strand it. Use it to fail loudly and early on a bad guid or a missing module rather than letting a nil propagate somewhere confusing.

MrxFactionManager.doc: Manages faction relations, attitudes, the attitude meter, reporting/pursuit (civilians calling you in) and civilian-casualty charges. It is always resident and importable from anywhere, which is why the networking and co-op-chat deep dives hijack its NetEventCallback to carry their own custom net events. Like every resident module it must be pulled in with import("MrxFactionManager") before use; calling it cold fails with "attempt to index global 'MrxFactionManager' (a nil value)".

Init.doc: Initializes attitude level mappings and faction template to abbreviation mappings. It populates _tAttitudeLevelsToLabels and _tAttitudeLabelsToLevels based on _tAttitudes, and assigns unique GUIDs to each faction in _tFactions.

Reset.doc: Resets the report system by initializing it with default parameters.

Setup.doc: Sets up the report system, initializes pursuit level times, and configures various aspects of faction management. It also sets up next flybys, achievements, disguise handling, faction zone handling, and HUD faction display thresholds.

SendPlayerJoinEvents.doc: Sends network events to synchronize mutable factions and civilian casualties when a player joins the game.

GetFactionStringIndex.doc: Retrieves the faction abbreviation based on a string hash. Returns "NO NAME" if no matching faction is found.

NetEventCallback.doc: Handles network events related to faction management. It processes mutable factions and civilian casualties based on the event ID.

NetInitializeClientFactionRelations.doc: Initializes client-side faction relations in a staggered manner to avoid performance issues.

SetAttitudeMutable.doc: Marks a faction's attitude as mutable, adds it to the HUD attitude meter and initialises its relation with PMC, sending a net event when done on the server. Call this before trying to change a faction's standing.
SetAttitudeMutable.gotcha: This is the fix for SetRelation silently doing nothing on a faction that is not yet mutable.

IsAttitudeMutable.doc: Checks if a faction's attitude is mutable by returning the boolean value stored in _tFactions.

CanAttitudeBeMutable.doc: Checks if the attitude of a faction with the given abbreviation (sAbbrev) can be dynamically changed. Returns boolean: True if the attitude is mutable, false otherwise.

GetRelation.doc: Retrieves the relation value between two factions based on their abbreviations. Returns number: The relation value between the two factions.

TestAttitude.doc: Tests if the attitude between two factions meets a specified comparison condition against a given attitude label. Returns boolean: True if the condition is met, false otherwise.

GetAttitudeLevel.doc: Retrieves the attitude level between two factions based on their abbreviations. Returns number: The attitude level between the two factions.

GetAttitudeLabel.doc: Retrieves the attitude label between two factions based on their abbreviations. Returns string: The attitude label between the two factions.

GetMeterValue.doc: Retrieves the meter value representing the attitude between two factions based on their abbreviations. Returns number: The meter value representing the attitude.

GetPriceScale.doc: Retrieves the price scale factor based on the attitude between two factions. Returns number: The price scale factor.

SetRelation.doc: Sets the relation value between two factions and updates related UI elements and events.
SetRelation.gotcha: Confirmed working by live testing — with a real gotcha: silently no-ops toward "Pmc" if the subject faction isn't currently mutable.

ChangeRelation.doc: Changes the relation value between two factions by a specified amount.

CreateAttitudeChangeEvent.doc: Creates a non-persistent attitude change event with specified parameters and callback.

CreatePersistentAttitudeChangeEvent.doc: Creates a persistent attitude change event with specified parameters and callback.

_CreateAttitudeChangeEvent.doc: Internal function to create an attitude change event, either persistent or non-persistent.

ConvertRelationToMeterValue.doc: Converts a relation value to a meter value representing attitude. Returns number: The converted meter value.

ConvertRelationToAttitudeLevel.doc: Converts a relation value to an attitude level based on defined ranges. Returns number: The corresponding attitude level.

GetAttitudeFromLevel.doc: Retrieves the attitude label from a given attitude level. Returns string: The corresponding attitude label.

GetFactionAbbrevs.doc: Retrieves a sorted list of all faction abbreviations. Returns table: A table containing the sorted faction abbreviations.

GetFactionAbbrev.doc: Converts a faction template name into its short abbreviation ("All", "Chi", "Gur", ...), which is the form the rest of this module's API expects. Commonly fed the full-name string returned by MrxUtil.GetFaction.

GetFactionAbbrevFromFactionGuid.doc: Retrieves the abbreviation for a faction based on its GUID. Returns string: The corresponding faction abbreviation.

GetFactionTemplateName.doc: Retrieves the template name for a given faction abbreviation. Returns string: The corresponding faction template name.

GetBribableFactions.doc: Retrieves a list of factions that can be bribed based on their attitude towards the PMC and mutability. Returns table: A table containing the abbreviations of bribe-able factions.

GetAttitudes.doc: Retrieves a table mapping attitude labels to their median values. Returns table: A table where keys are attitude labels and values are their median values.

GetAttitudeMedianValue.doc: Retrieves the median value for a given attitude label. Returns number: The median value of the attitude.

GetRgbColor.doc: Retrieves the RGB color associated with the attitude between two factions. Returns table: A table containing the RGB color values.

SaveSingleton.doc: Saves the current state of faction relations and mutable factions for persistence. Returns table: A table containing saved data including relations, mutable factions, civilian casualties, and penalties.

LoadSingleton.doc: Loads the saved state of faction relations and mutable factions from provided save data.

GetPlayerVisibleName.doc: Retrieves the player-visible name for a given faction abbreviation. Returns string: The player-visible name of the faction.

GetShortPlayerVisibleName.doc: Retrieves the short player-visible name for a given faction abbreviation. Returns string: The short player-visible name of the faction.

GetAdjective.doc: Retrieves the adjective associated with a given faction abbreviation. Returns string: The adjective for the faction.

GetInlineIcon.doc: Retrieves the inline icon texture for a given faction abbreviation. Returns string: The inline icon texture name.

GetMarkerTexture.doc: Retrieves the marker texture for a given faction abbreviation. Returns string: The marker texture name.

CivCasualtySetup.doc: Sets up event handling for civilian casualties, initializing a persistent event to resolve civilian deaths.

ResolveCivCasualty.doc: Resolves the consequences of a civilian death, including determining if it was caused by the player and charging penalties.

ChargeCivCasualty.doc: Charges penalties for civilian casualties, updates player statistics, and triggers related events and voice cues.

GetFactionStringAbbrev.doc: Retrieves the faction abbreviation string for a given GUID and optional hash. If uAbbrev is provided, it searches _tFactions for a matching hash; otherwise, it calls GetFactionAbbrev(GetFaction(uGuid)).

NetSafeRemoveReportingDisplay.doc: Safely removes the reporting display by calling GetFactionStringAbbrev to get the faction abbreviation and then invoking RemoveReportingDisplay.

NetSafeHandleReporter0.doc: Handles reporter state 0 by getting the faction abbreviation and calling HandleReporter0.

NetSafeHandleReporter1.doc: Handles reporter state 1 by getting the faction abbreviation and calling HandleReporter1.

NetSafeHandleReporter2.doc: Handles reporter state 2 by getting the faction abbreviation and calling HandleReporter2.

NetSafeFinishedReporting.doc: Safely finishes reporting by getting the faction abbreviation and calling FinishedReporting.

RemoveReportingDisplay.doc: Removes the reporting display for a given GUID and faction abbreviation. It removes markers, halts pulses, deletes minimap objectives, and cancels timers if specified.

HandleReporter0.doc: Handles reporter state 0 by setting up markers, radar objectives, and voice sequences based on the faction data. It also starts a timer if necessary and sends a network message if on the server.

HandleTressPasser.doc: Handles tresspassers by playing voice-over messages and setting timers. It checks if a VO has already been played to avoid repetition.

HandleReporter1.doc: Handles reporter state 1 by checking for jamming conditions, starting timers, and playing voice sequences based on faction data. It also updates the network state if on the server.

HandleReporter2.doc: Handles reporter state 2 by removing reporting displays, updating active reporters, and setting report delays. It also updates the network state if on the server.

AmIBeingJammed.doc: Checks if a given GUID is being jammed by comparing factions of drivers in vehicles with AA levels.

HandleReporter.doc: Handles different reporter states (0, 1, 2) by calling appropriate functions based on the current state.

ValidateReporter.doc: Validates a reporter by checking faction mutability, disabled reporters, and other conditions. Logs reasons for cancellation if validation fails.

FinishedReporting.doc: Handles the completion of reporting by adjusting relations, setting delays, incrementing pursuits if necessary, playing voice sequences, posting events, and updating network states.

expand.doc: Expands a table by printing each entry's index and values. This function is defined twice in this part.

SetReportDelay.doc: Sets the report delay for various factions based on the provided delay value.

GetFaction.doc: Retrieves the faction label for a given GUID from a predefined list of factions. Logs an error if no faction label is found.

GetPerceivedFaction.doc: Gets the perceived faction by checking if the object is disguised and retrieving the faction accordingly.

DisableReporter.doc: Disables a reporter by setting its GUID in tDisabledReporters and handling active reporters.

EnableReporter.doc: Enables a reporter by removing its GUID from tDisabledReporters.

DisableReporting.doc: Disables or enables reporting based on the input boolean bDisable. If reporting is disabled, it logs "Reporting DISABLED" and handles any active reporter.

SetFactionReporting.doc: Sets the reporting status for a specific faction (sFaction). Logs whether the faction was found and updates its bCanReport field in _tFactions.

IncrementPursuit.doc: Increments the pursuit level for a given faction abbreviation. It retrieves the faction's GUID, adjusts the pursuit level to a maximum of 3, sets the pursuit duration, starts the pursuit on the HUD, and optionally plays a voice-over cue if available.

LockPursuit.doc: Locks the pursuit for a specific faction identified by uGuid at a given nLevel. It updates the pursuit state in Pg, starts the pursuit display on the HUD, and hides any meters for factions.

ClearPursuitLock.doc: Clears all pursuit locks. It hides meters for all factions and clears the pursuit lock in Pg.

SetCustomPursuit.doc: Sets a custom pursuit for a specific faction with a given duration and settings. It updates the pursuit state in Pg, starts the pursuit display on the HUD, and hides any meters for factions.

ClearCustomPursuit.doc: Clears all custom pursuits. It hides meters for all factions and clears the custom pursuit in Pg.

RandomFlyby.doc: Generates a random flyby based on faction configurations defined in tFlybys. It selects a random faction, template, and number of aircraft to spawn, calculates positions, and triggers the flyby using Airstrike.Flyby.

SetupNextFlyby.doc: Sets up a timer for the next random flyby. It creates an event that triggers RandomFlyby after a random interval between 19 and 90 seconds.

GetPdaFactionIdFromFactionId.doc: Retrieves the PDA faction ID from a given faction ID by looking up _tFactions.

GetFactionIdFromIndex.doc: Retrieves the faction ID at a specific index in _tFactions.

GetIndexFromFactionId.doc: Retrieves the index of a specific faction ID in _tFactions.

MrxGui.doc: Top-level GUI facade. Its Init() copies the widget classes and widget-management functions out of MrxGuiBase (plus the dialog- and numeric-box entry points) into the MrxGui namespace, which is why HUD code everywhere calls MrxGui.ImageWidget:new() / MrxGui.AddWidget(...). On top of that aliasing it natively implements global screen fades, HUD messages, the objective-description callback and the E3 demo-mode toggle. Like every resident module it must be pulled in with import("MrxGui") before use; calling it cold fails with "attempt to index global 'MrxGui' (a nil value)".

Init.doc: Init() binds these MrxGui.* names to their real implementations: - Widget classes (call :new() on these): Widget, ImageWidget, TextWidget, FlashWidget, SpriteWidget, MovieWidget, MinimapWidget ← MrxGuiBase.*. - Widget management: AddWidget, AddWidgetWithChildren, RemoveWidget, RemoveWidgetWithChildren, RemoveEverySingleWidget (← MrxGuiBase.WidgetManager.RemoveAll), PushWidgetToFront/PushWidgetToBack, PushAllTextToFront. - Lookup: GetWidgetByName, GetAllWidgetsByName, GetWidgetByNameAndOwner ← MrxGuiBase.*. - Layout: LoadGuiFile/LoadGUIFile (← MrxGuiBase.LoadGUIFile), UnloadGuiFile, RemoveAllWidgets/RemoveAllWidgetsInLayout, DeleteTransientWidgets, ReAddAllWidgets, HideAllWidgets, ShowAllWidgets, SetAllWidgetsSleep, AssignLayoutToPlayer, DuplicateLayout. - Dialog/numeric: DisplayDialogBox ← MrxGuiDialogBox.DisplayDialogBox, CloseDialogBox ← MrxGuiDialogBox.Close, DisplayNumericBox ← MrxGuiNumericBox.DisplayNumericBox. - Input constants: Joystick ← MrxGuiBase.Joystick (the button-id table other modules read). - Event dispatch: SendEvent ← MrxGuiBase.SentEvent (note the source's SentEvent spelling).

GetObjectiveDescription.doc: Retrieves the description of an objective using a callback function if available. Returns nil if no callback is set or if the input is invalid.

SetObjectiveInformationCallback.doc: Sets a callback function to provide objective information. The callback data can be a table that will be stored and passed back when the callback is invoked.

RemoveObjectiveInformation.doc: Removes an objective from the list of tracked objectives in the callback data.

GlobalFadeToBlack.doc: Initiates a global fade to black effect. If multiple fades are requested simultaneously, they are queued and executed sequentially.

GlobalFadeFromBlack.doc: Completes the global fade from black effect by cleaning up resources and resetting internal state.
GlobalFadeFromBlack.gotcha: Confirmed in source: this function guards if _oTimerEvent then Event.Delete(_oTimerEvent) ... end, but _oTimerEvent is declared nil at module scope (line 84 of source) and is never assigned anywhere else in the file — no Event.Create call in this module ever sets it.

HandleLoadingHint.doc: Handles the display of loading hints during the fade effect by updating the text in the flash widget.

_FinishFadeToBlack.doc: Finishes the fade to black process by setting up event handlers and preparing for the next phase of the fade effect.

_FinishFadeFromBlack.doc: Finishes the fade from black process by pausing the animation, hiding the widget, and cleaning up resources.

_InitFadeFlash.doc: Initializes the flash widget used for global fades. Sets up event handlers and adds the widget to the GUI system.

CleanupFadeFlash.doc: Cleans up the fade flash widget by deleting it and resetting related state.

_CompleteFadeFlashLoad.doc: Completes the loading of the fade flash SWF file, sets up necessary event handlers, and starts the fade effect if queued.

_FadeUpdate.doc: Processes any queued callbacks after a fade update event.

SetGlobalFadeVisible.doc: Sets the visibility of the global fade widget.

FadeToColor.doc: Initiates a color-based fade effect for either the global screen or a specific player's screen. The function handles setting up the animation points and starting the fade process.
FadeToColor.sig: MrxGui.FadeToColor(nTime, uPlayerGuid, nRed, nGreen, nBlue, nAlpha)

FadeFromColor.doc: Completes a color-based fade effect by animating the widget back to full transparency and hiding it when done.

SetFadeEnabled.doc: Enables or disables the global screen fade widget based on the provided boolean flag.

_HideWhenDone.doc: Hides the widget after an animation completes.

AddMessage.doc: Adds a message to the HUD. The function accepts various parameters such as text, priority, duration, and type of message.

ClearMessages.doc: Clears all messages from the HUD.

SetE3HudMode.doc: Toggles the E3/HUD mode on or off. This mode is used for demonstration purposes and can affect how certain UI elements are displayed.

IsE3HudModeActive.doc: Returns a boolean indicating whether the E3/HUD mode is currently active.

FindShellWidget.doc: Finds and returns the ID of the shell widget, which is often used as a base for other GUI elements.

GetReticleSize.doc: Retrieves the size of the reticle image for a given player. If the reticle widget is not found, it defaults to a size of 48.

_fObjectiveInformationCallback.doc: Module-level storage slot (initialised to false), not a function you call: SetObjectiveInformationCallback writes the caller's provider function here and GetObjectiveDescription invokes it as _fObjectiveInformationCallback(_tObjectiveInformationCallbackData, uGuid).
_fObjectiveInformationCallback.gotcha: While it is false, GetObjectiveDescription returns nil for every GUID.

MrxGuiBase.doc: Foundational GUI layer: the Widget/ImageWidget/TextWidget/FlashWidget/SpriteWidget/MovieWidget/MinimapWidget classes plus the WidgetManager that adds, removes, hides, layers and re-adds them, and the control-focus, layout-file and screen-resolution machinery. Most mods reach it indirectly through the MrxGui facade, which re-exports these same functions. Like every resident module it must be pulled in with import("MrxGuiBase") before use; calling it cold fails with "attempt to index global 'MrxGuiBase' (a nil value)".

GetControlFocus.doc: Manages the focus queue for a given widget. If bPause is true, it sets the dialog box mode; otherwise, it sets the support menu mode.

ReleaseControlFocus.doc: Removes a widget from the control focus queue and updates the control mode accordingly. Called by MrxGuiDialogBox.Close/_CloseAndCallCallback to hand control back when a dialog closes.

GetCurrentControlHolder.doc: Returns the current widget holding control for a given owner GUID or "global".

InformControlOwnerChanged.doc: Placeholder function that currently does nothing.

IsPlayerLocal.doc: Checks if a player is local. Returns true if the player GUID is nil, not in multiplayer, or if the viewport ID is 1.

IsViewportLocal.doc: Checks if a viewport is local. Returns true if the viewport ID is nil, not in multiplayer, or if the viewport ID is 1.

SentEvent.doc: Sends an event to the EventManager.

ProcessEventImmediate.doc: Processes an event immediately based on its type.

AddWidget.doc: Adds a widget to the WidgetManager so it actually renders - the call that makes a hand-built ImageWidget/TextWidget appear on screen.
AddWidget.gotcha: It is declared as a literal = 0 in the decompiled source and never visibly reassigned, which makes it look uncallable; it demonstrably works at runtime, and is normally reached through the MrxGui facade rather than this module directly.

AddWidgetWithChildren.doc: Adds a widget and all its children to the WidgetManager.

RemoveWidget.doc: Removes a widget from the WidgetManager.

RemoveWidgetWithChildren.doc: Removes a widget and all its children from the WidgetManager.

PushAllTextToFront.doc: Pushes all text widgets to the front.

PushWidgetToFront.doc: Pushes a specific widget to the front.

PushWidgetToBack.doc: Pushes a specific widget to the back.

GetWidgetByName.doc: Retrieves a widget by its name.

GetAllWidgetsByName.doc: Retrieves all widgets with a given name.

GetWidgetByNameAndOwner.doc: Retrieves a widget by its name and owner GUID.

DeleteTransientWidgets.doc: Deletes all transient widgets owned by a specific player.

_HandleAnimationComplete.doc: Handles the completion of an animation by calling the completion callback, managing the animation queue, and initiating the next animation point.

_FlashCallback.doc: A helper function that processes callbacks from the flash widget. It unpacks callback data and calls the provided function with the appropriate arguments.

_HandleInputForFlashWidget.doc: Handles input events for Flash widgets. It iterates through the event table and sends corresponding input to the widget based on whether the key contains "ButtonPress" or "ButtonReleased".

MinimapDataUpdateHandler.doc: Handles data updates for the minimap. It updates the minimap's position and rotation, adjusts the range based on player velocity, and corrects widget resolution.

MinimapHandleE3HudModeEvent.doc: Handles E3 HUD mode events by setting the visibility of the minimap based on whether the event is "on" or "off".

LoadGUIFile.doc: Loads a GUI file dynamically. It sets up a callback that calls GUIFileLoadedCallback and an optional finished loading callback.

RemoveAllWidgetsInLayout.doc: Removes all widgets in a given module by iterating through the AddedWidgetList and calling RemoveWidgetWithChildren.

ReAddAllWidgets.doc: Re-adds all widgets in a given module by iterating through the AddedWidgetList and calling AddWidgetWithChildren.

HideAllWidgets.doc: Hides all widgets in a given module by setting their visibility to false.

ShowAllWidgets.doc: Shows all widgets in a given module by setting their visibility to true.

SetAllWidgetsSleep.doc: Sets the sleeping state for all widgets in a given module.

AssignLayoutToPlayer.doc: Assigns a layout to a player by setting the owner GUID for each widget in the module's AddedWidgetList.

DuplicateLayout.doc: Duplicates a GUI layout by creating a new module with a copy of the original's LocalWidgetList. It calls GUIFileLoadedCallback to initialize the new module.

GUIFileLoadedCallback.doc: Handles the loading of a GUI file. It initializes the AddedWidgetList, loads and adds widgets from the LocalWidgetList, triggers any initialization events, and corrects widget resolution for each widget.

LoadAndAddWidgetFromLayoutFileData.doc: This function creates and adds a new widget to the GUI based on the provided layout data. It handles different types of widgets such as images, text, minimaps, flash, and sprite widgets.

UnloadGUIFile.doc: This function unloads a GUI file by calling dynamic_remove with the provided file.

ChangeScreenResolution.doc: This function changes the screen resolution and updates the screen dimensions and scale factor accordingly. It also marks all widgets as needing correction for the new resolution.
ChangeScreenResolution.sig: MrxGuiBase.ChangeScreenResolution(nWidth, nHeight, nNewPixelWidth, nNewPixelHeight, nX, nY)

ChangeScreenPixelSize.doc: This function changes the pixel size of the screen and updates the pixel width and height accordingly.

ValidateParameter.doc: This function validates a parameter against a specified type. If the parameter matches the type, it returns the parameter; otherwise, it returns a default value.

Run.doc: This function processes events using EventManager.ProcessEvents.

GetEventListTable.doc: This function returns the event list table from EventManager.EventList.

SetDialogBoxMode.doc: This function sets the dialog box mode for a player. It checks if the provided parameters are of the correct types and then calls _SetDialogBoxMode with the player GUID and activation status.

SetSupportMenuMode.doc: This function sets the support menu mode for a player. It checks if the provided parameters are of the correct types and then calls _SetSupportMenuMode with the player GUID and activation status.

Init.doc: This function initializes various widget types (TextWidget, ImageWidget, FlashWidget, MinimapWidget, SpriteWidget, MovieWidget) and sets their transient properties to nil. It also adjusts joystick button mappings if necessary.

ReInit.doc: This function is intended for reinitializing the GUI but currently does nothing.

DeInit.doc: This function is intended for deinitializing the GUI but currently does nothing.

_SetDialogBoxMode.doc: Captured reference to the engine global GuiSetDialogBoxMode, stashed at module load (the global is then cleared out of _G). The public SetDialogBoxMode type-checks its arguments and delegates here.
_SetDialogBoxMode.gotcha: Call the public SetDialogBoxMode instead; it returns false rather than erroring if the engine never provided GuiSetDialogBoxMode or if the arguments are the wrong types.

_SetSupportMenuMode.doc: Captured reference to the engine global GuiSetSupportMenuMode, stashed at module load (the global is then cleared out of _G). The public SetSupportMenuMode type-checks its arguments and delegates here.
_SetSupportMenuMode.gotcha: Call the public SetSupportMenuMode instead; it returns false rather than erroring if the engine never provided GuiSetSupportMenuMode or if the arguments are the wrong types.

MrxGuiHudMessage.doc: Drives on-screen messages and fanfares: full-screen contract/mission/wager payout fanfares, 'new contact / new shop item / new landing zone' unlock pop-ups, business-card reveals, COMPLETED/FAILED stamps, sliding text fanfares and the 'classy text' effect. Fanfares are mostly Scaleform FlashWidgets driven through ActionScript callbacks. Like every resident module it must be pulled in with import("MrxGuiHudMessage") before use; calling it cold fails with "attempt to index global 'MrxGuiHudMessage' (a nil value)".

CreateFanfare.doc: Creates a new fanfare widget based on the specified type (contract, mission, wager, support, contact, or card) and faction. It initializes the widget with necessary properties and sets up event handlers for input and loading completion.

SetFanfareCompleteCallback.doc: Sets a callback function that will be called when the fanfare completes. The callback can include additional data passed through tCallbackData.

SupportFanfareAddItem.doc: Adds an item to the support fanfare widget with specified texture and details. This function is used to populate the items in a support-related fanfare.

SupportFanfareCommence.doc: Starts the support fanfare if it is ready to begin. It checks if the loading is complete before starting the fanfare.

_SupportLoadCompleteCallback.doc: Internal callback function that marks the support widget as loaded and starts the fanfare if it is ready.

_BeginSupportFanfare.doc: Begins playing the support fanfare by setting its visibility and triggering a scroll-out effect after 3 seconds.

_ScrollOutFanfare.doc: Handles the scroll-out effect of the fanfare, calling an action script callback and scheduling the widget's deletion.

ContactFanfareCommence.doc: Starts the contact fanfare with specified texture and details. It checks if the loading is complete before starting the fanfare.

_ContactLoadCompleteCallback.doc: Internal callback function that marks the contact widget as loaded and starts the fanfare if it is ready.

_BeginContactFanfare.doc: Begins playing the contact fanfare by setting its visibility and triggering a scroll-out effect after 3 seconds.

CardFanfareSetParameters.doc: Sets parameters for the business card fanfare, including title, name, job title, contact information, and display time. It marks the card as ready if all required fields are provided.
CardFanfareSetParameters.sig: MrxGuiHudMessage.CardFanfareSetParameters(sTitle, sName, sJobTitle, sPhone1, sPhone2, sEmail, nDisplayTime)

CardFanfareCommence.doc: Starts the business card fanfare if it is ready to begin. It checks if the loading is complete before starting the fanfare and sends network events if applicable.

_CardLoadCompleteCallback.doc: Internal callback function that marks the card widget as loaded and starts the fanfare if it is ready.

_BeginCardFanfare.doc: Begins playing the business card fanfare by setting its visibility, calling an action script callback to start the fanfare, and scheduling cleanup events.

_ContinueCardFanfare.doc: Continues the business card fanfare by calling an action script callback and scheduling the end of the fanfare based on the display time.

_EndCardFanfare.doc: Ends the business card fanfare by calling an action script callback to conclude the fanfare.

_CleanupCardFanfare.doc: Cleans up the business card fanfare by scheduling its deletion after a short delay.

SetFanfareParameters.doc: Sets parameters for contract or mission fanfares, including profile names, cancel message, and retry option. It ensures that only valid types are set.

AddFanfareLineItem.doc: Adds a line item to the contract or wager fanfare with specified description, value, type, and player index. It checks for valid input and ensures that the cancel message is not set.

CommenceFanfare.doc: Starts the fanfare by locking HQ, sending network events if applicable, setting up time dilation effects, and preparing the fanfare widget for display. It also handles UI state changes like disabling the HUD and PDA.

NetClientCloseFanfare.doc: Closes the fanfare on the client side by stopping sound callbacks, closing the fanfare, and ending it.

_SlowdownUpdate.doc: Handles the time dilation effect during the fanfare, updating the time scale and fade widget's alpha value accordingly. It triggers the beginning of the fanfare when the time scale reaches zero.

_LoadCompleteCallback.doc: Internal callback function that marks the main widget as loaded and starts the fanfare if it is ready.

_BeginFanfareFlash.doc: This function initializes the fanfare flash sequence for a given widget. It checks if the loading is complete and proceeds to close any pause screens, set invincibility for the local player, initialize the fanfare, create a timer event for an initial delay, and get control focus.

_InitializeFanfareFlash.doc: This function initializes the fanfare flash by setting up various properties of the widget. It changes the shell state, sets visibility and pauses the widget, calls action script callbacks to initialize the fanfare with player data, and sets up event handlers for closing, retrying, and continuing the fanfare.

_ContinueFanfare.doc: This function handles the continuation of the fanfare by calling an action script callback to make the fanfare buttons appear.

_InitialDelay.doc: This function makes the widget visible and plays it after a short delay.

_SkipFanfare.doc: This function sets up event listeners for skipping the fanfare based on player input. It creates events for button presses that trigger the _EndFanfare function.

_RetryEvents.doc: This function sets up persistent event listeners for retrying the fanfare using left stick inputs and selection buttons. It sends flash inputs to handle these actions.

OnPlayerJoined.doc: This function handles the event when a player joins the game. If there is an active fanfare flash widget, it sends a specific input to the widget.

_DeleteFanfareEvents.doc: This function deletes various persistent events related to the fanfare flash sequence.

_EndFanfare.doc: This function ends the fanfare flash by handling cleanup tasks such as deleting events, releasing control focus, and calling callbacks. It also unlocks all HQs if necessary.

_DeleteFanfareWidget.doc: This function deletes the fanfare widget, removes it from the GUI, and calls any callback functions associated with it. It also handles restoring certain game states like PDA suppression and scope enabling.

_HandleFanfareInput.doc: This function handles input events for the fanfare flash by calling a custom handler defined in the widget's custom data.

ShowTextFanfare.doc: This function creates and displays a text-based fanfare with two lines of text. It sets up animations for entering, displaying, and fading out the text, and calls a callback function when the fanfare is done.
ShowTextFanfare.sig: MrxGuiHudMessage.ShowTextFanfare(uPlayerGuid, sLine1, sLine2, nEnterTime, nDisplayTime, nFadeTime, fCallback, tCallbackData)

_TextFanfareDone.doc: This function handles the completion of a text fanfare by calling the provided callback function and cleaning up the widget.

_TextDelay.doc: This function sets up a delay before fading out the text in a text fanfare.

_TextFadeout.doc: This function handles the fade-out animation of the text in a text fanfare.

_TextDelete.doc: This function removes and deletes the animated widget from the text fanfare.

ShowEventFanfare.doc: Displays an event fanfare message on the HUD.

_EventFanfareFinishAppear.doc: Handles the appearance animation completion of an event fanfare.

_EventFanfareProcessTextQueue.doc: Processes the text queue for sequential display in the event fanfare.

_EventFanfareContinueTextFade.doc: Continues the fade animation for the next text in the queue.

_EventFanfareFinishDisplay.doc: Handles the display animation completion of an event fanfare.

_EventFanfareComplete.doc: Completes the event fanfare by removing the widget and executing the callback.

GetEventFanfareTitle.doc: Retrieves the title for a given event type.

HandleInitialization.doc: Handles initialization of a widget by setting its translucency and scheduling removal.

ShowCompletedMessage.doc: Displays a completed message on the HUD.

ShowFailedMessage.doc: Displays a failed message on the HUD.

ShowMessage.doc: Displays a message on the HUD with specified parameters.
ShowMessage.sig: MrxGuiHudMessage.ShowMessage(uPlayerGuid, sTextureName, fZoomCompleteCallback, fFadeCompleteCallback, nXLocation, nYLocation, sHorizontalAnchor, sVerticalAnchor, nMessageWidth, nMessageHeight, nMessageDisplayTime, vSoundEffect)

AnimationFinishCallback.doc: Handles the completion of an animation for a widget.

HandleUpdateEvent.doc: Updates the display time remaining for a widget and handles removal if necessary.

RemovalCallback.doc: Handles the removal of a widget after its fade animation completes.

Init.doc: Initializes the module by loading necessary fonts.

HandleClassyTextInit.doc: Initializes a widget for displaying classy text.

DisplayClassyText.doc: Displays classy text on the HUD with specified parameters.
DisplayClassyText.sig: MrxGuiHudMessage.DisplayClassyText(oWidget, sText, nX, nY, nDuration, nScale, sHorizAnchor, sVertAnchor, sJustification, bExpand)

_ClassyTextLoadCompleteCallback.doc: Handles the completion of loading a classy text widget.

_HandleClassyTextEnd.doc: Handles the end of a classy text widget by scheduling its deletion.

_DeleteClassyText.doc: Deletes a classy text widget from the HUD.

MrxGuiManager.doc: Loads the master HUD, binoculars, satellite and PDA layouts, duplicates them per player, and owns the HUD's sleep/visibility stack. Use it to add or remove your own widget from a player's HUD and to toggle the HUD or satellite overlay. Like every resident module it must be pulled in with import("MrxGuiManager") before use; calling it cold fails with "attempt to index global 'MrxGuiManager' (a nil value)".

Init.doc: Resets the module's four tracking tables (_tPlayerGuiList, _tPendingList, _tHudStates, _tPendingHudWidgets) to empty. Standard lifecycle reset, not something a mod would normally call directly.

CreateGui.doc: Called when a new player's GUI needs to be created. Loads master copies of GUI layouts if they haven't been loaded yet, then duplicates these layouts for the given player.

ToggleHud.doc: Toggles the visibility state of the HUD for a given player. Uses a refcounted sleep/visibility stack (nHudState) to manage when widgets should be shown or hidden.

_DetoggleWidget.doc: Private function that wakes up a single widget by name and owner.

_DetoggleWidgetRecursive.doc: Private function that recursively wakes up a widget and all its children by name and owner.

_RecursiveWakeup.doc: Private recursive function that sets a widget and all its children to be awake (not sleeping).

GetHudState.doc: Returns the current visibility state of the HUD for a given player.

AddWidgetToHud.doc: Adds a widget to a specific player's HUD, recursing into its children when bIncludeChildren is true. Use it instead of a bare AddWidget when the widget should belong to one player's HUD layout.

RemoveWidgetFromHud.doc: Removes a widget from the HUD for a given player. If the widget has children and bRemoveChildren is true, it recursively removes all children as well.

ToggleSatellite.doc: Toggles the satellite overlay state for a given player. Sets up callbacks for map mode changes and sends events to update the satellite progress and state.

ApplySatelliteUpdateEvent.doc: Private function that sends an event with updated satellite progress information.

DoNothing.doc: A no-op function used as a placeholder callback.

SetSatelliteSuccessCallback.doc: Sets the success callback for the satellite minigame. This callback is triggered when the satellite designation is successful.

SetSatelliteMinigameData.doc: Sets the data for the satellite minigame sectors.

SetSatelliteCost.doc: Sets the cost of the satellite minigame.

DeleteGui.doc: Deletes the GUI for a given player by removing and deleting all widgets associated with that player's layouts.

DeleteAllGuis.doc: Deletes the GUI for all players by calling DeleteGui for each player in the list.

SetLoadingCompleteCallback.doc: Sets a callback function to be called when all GUIs have been loaded. If there are already loaded GUIs, it calls the function immediately; otherwise, it stores the callback and data for later use.

HudLoaded.doc: Called when the HUD layout is loaded. Sets up the master HUD layout.

ScopeLoaded.doc: Called when the binoculars (scope) layout is loaded. Sets up the master scope layout.

SatelliteLoaded.doc: Called when the satellite layout is loaded. Sets up the master satellite layout.

PdaLoaded.doc: Called when the PDA layout is loaded. Sets up the master PDA layout.

_SetupMasterLayouts.doc: Private function that sets up the master copies of GUI layouts once they are all loaded.

_AllRequiredModulesLoaded.doc: Private function that checks if all required GUI modules have been loaded.

_RemoveAndDeleteWidgets.doc: Private function that removes and deletes all widgets in a given layout.

MrxGuiTextBuffer.doc: The engine's scrolling message-log widget: message arrays, text wrapping, priority queuing, fade in/out and append-vs-evict rules. It is the right tool whenever you need more than one line of HUD text stacked over time (chat window, kill feed, debug console). Like every resident module it must be pulled in with import("MrxGuiTextBuffer") before use; calling it cold fails with "attempt to index global 'MrxGuiTextBuffer' (a nil value)".

HandleInstantiationEventForTextBuffer.doc: The working constructor for a text buffer: sets up font/scale, scroll direction, backdrop and border sizing, and attaches AddMessage/ClearMessages/ClearVisibleMessages/RemovePendingMessage/ModifyPendingMessage/SetLocation onto the widget you pass in. Build a bare widget by hand, name it "MessageBox" if you want the translucent backdrop, then call this on it.
HandleInstantiationEventForTextBuffer.gotcha: Use this rather than the module's own InstantiateTextBuffer constructor, which crashes the game - that function writes to an oWidget that does not exist in its scope.

InstantiateTextBuffer.doc: The module's own documented constructor for a text buffer - broken in the shipped game, do not call it. Use HandleInstantiationEventForTextBuffer on a hand-built widget instead.
InstantiateTextBuffer.gotcha: It builds its widget into a global named NewTextBuffer but then writes to an oWidget that does not exist in its scope, so it throws "attempt to index a nil value (global 'oWidget')" and crashes the caller. Patching the typo does not help either.

AddMessage.doc: Defaults if omitted: nPriority=5, nDisplayDuration=2, nFadeDuration=0.25, bClearBuffer=false, bAllowsAppends=true. nPriority is clamped to 0-5; 0 is special — it forcibly evicts however many current messages are needed to make room rather than queuing behind them, for anything urgent enough to jump the line. A negative nDisplayDuration makes the message persistent (bPersistent=true, internally set to display for 10000 "seconds" instead) — it stays until something else clears it rather than fading out on its own. bAllowsAppends=false prevents the *next* message from sharing the buffer's remaining space alongside this one.
AddMessage.sig: MrxGuiTextBuffer.AddMessage(oTextBuffer, sMessage, nPriority, nDisplayDuration, nFadeDuration, bClearBuffer, bAllowsAppends, fCallback, tCallbackData)

SetLocation.doc: Moves the widget and recalculates the border-adjusted internal bounds (x1/y1/x2/y2) other functions read from.

ClearMessages.doc: ClearMessages wipes everything — current and pending — and hides the widget.

ClearVisibleMessages.doc: ClearVisibleMessages only clears what's currently on-screen; pass bAdvance=true to immediately pull the next pending message(s) in to fill the freed space rather than leaving it empty.

ModifyPendingMessage.doc: Edit or cancel a message that's still queued (by the ID AddMessage returned) before it's actually displayed. Both return false if the ID doesn't correspond to a still-pending message — e.g. it already scrolled onto screen, or never existed.
ModifyPendingMessage.sig: MrxGuiTextBuffer.ModifyPendingMessage(oTextBuffer, nMessageId, sMessage, nDisplayDuration, nFadeDuration, bClearBuffer, bAllowsAppends, fCallback, tCallbackData)

RemovePendingMessage.doc: Edit or cancel a message that's still queued (by the ID AddMessage returned) before it's actually displayed. Both return false if the ID doesn't correspond to a still-pending message — e.g. it already scrolled onto screen, or never existed.

AdvanceMessages.doc: Zeroes out the currently-showing message's remaining display duration, forcing it to advance/dismiss on the very next update tick instead of waiting out its normal timer.

CallCallback.doc: The actual mechanism that fires the fCallback/tCallbackData a message was created with via AddMessage. Called as oMessage:CallCallback() when a message finishes displaying; defensively coerces tCallbackData to {} if it isn't a table, calls fCallback(unpack(tCallbackData)), then clears fCallback so it can't fire twice.

GetCurrentMessageId.doc: Returns an array of the numeric IDs of every message currently visible (not pending).

HandleAddMessageEvent.doc: HandleAddMessageEvent adds a message from an event payload: oWidget:AddMessage(tEvent.sMessage, nil, tEvent.nDuration).

HandleE3HudModeEvent.doc: HandleE3HudModeEvent hides/shows the buffer's first child and its current messages when tEvent.bOn toggles — a demo/screenshot "clean HUD" mode.

HandleTextBufferUpdateEvent.doc: Per-frame update driver for a text buffer: fades the exiting message out, removes and deletes it when fully transparent, and scrolls/advances the remaining messages. Wired to the widget's "GuiUpdate" event by HandleInstantiationEventForTextBuffer, so you never call it yourself.

PushMessageIntoTextBuffer.doc: Internal plumbing that moves a queued message into the visible list. This is where an over-tall message gets :SplitIntoLines() into multiple queued messages so it can scroll through a short buffer.

GetMessageHeight.doc: Internal helper: returns oTextWidget:GetHeight() for a message widget, used when working out how much vertical space a message needs in the buffer.

WrapText.doc: Internal helper: calls oTextWidget:Wrap() to re-flow a message's text to the buffer width.

IsEmpty.doc: Internal helper: returns true when the given table has no array entries, nil if the argument is not a table. Used to test whether the message lists are empty.

MboxAbs.doc: Internal helper: the module's own absolute-value function, returning nNumber when positive and nNumber * -1 otherwise.

ValidateParameter.doc: Internal helper: returns Parameter if its type() matches sType, otherwise DefaultValue. This is how the module applies its defaults for omitted arguments.

DrawDebugRectangle.doc: Debug-only helper that draws a fixed red rectangle (10,10 to 400,300) onto the target widget. Useful for eyeballing where a buffer actually sits on screen.

MrxHqManager.doc: Tracks the game's HQs - locking and unlocking them, registering their starters, setting respawn behaviour, recording whether the player is inside, and reacting to HQ death/hibernation. Use it to gate or open up HQ access. Like every resident module it must be pulled in with import("MrxHqManager") before use; calling it cold fails with "attempt to index global 'MrxHqManager' (a nil value)".

GetHq.doc: Retrieves an HQ instance by its name. Logs a debug message if the HQ cannot be retrieved and returns nil.

AddStarter.doc: Adds a starter to an HQ. If the HQ does not exist, it attempts to unlock it first.

RemoveStarter.doc: Removes a starter from an HQ.

UnlockHq.doc: Unlocks an HQ by loading its data (via WifHqData.GetHqConfigFromId) and setting up its properties on first unlock (creates MrxHq:Create(tHqData), sets its name), then clears its lock flag, refreshes its UI, and enables respawn by default (SetHqRespawn(sHqName, true)) if no respawn state is set yet. Logs debug messages for each step.
UnlockHq.gotcha: Likely bug: line 37's failure message reads Debug.Printf("Failed to find data for HQ " .. sName) — sName is not this function's parameter (which is sHqName) and is never assigned anywhere in this file, so it's an always-nil global.

LockHq.doc: Locks an HQ by setting its lock state to true and refreshing the UI display. Deletes any associated events.

LockAllHq.doc: Globally locks all HQs that are not already locked.

UnlockAllHq.doc: Globally unlocks every HQ that had been globally locked. The bulk counterpart to UnlockHq.

_CreateDeathEvent.doc: Creates a death event for an HQ. Depending on the HQ's configuration, it listens for either object health or object death events.

_SetupRespawn.doc: Sets up respawn behavior for an HQ. If bEnable and the HQ object is alive, calls _CreateDeathEvent; if bEnable and the object is already dead, calls _OnHqDeath directly.
_SetupRespawn.gotcha: Confirmed bug: line 117 does _tHqEvents[uHqGuid] = _CreateDeathEvent(sHqName, uHqGuid). _CreateDeathEvent has no return statement in either of its branches — it always implicitly returns nil. _CreateDeathEvent itself already correctly writes the real Event.Create(...) handle into _tHqEvents[uHqGuid] internally; _SetupRespawn then immediately clobbers that with nil by reassigning the call's (nonexistent) return value on top of it.

SetHqRespawn.doc: Enables or disables respawn behavior for an HQ. Updates the HQ's respawn state and sets up or removes the appropriate events based on the new state.

_SetHq.doc: Sets the lock state of an HQ and refreshes its UI display.

_OnHqDeath.doc: Handles the death event for an HQ. Logs a debug message, clears _tHqEvents[uHqGuid], locks the HQ via _SetHq(sHqName, false).

_OnHqHibernation.doc: Handles the hibernation event for an HQ by reviving it, updating its lock state, and setting up death events again.

IsInside.doc: Returns whether the player is inside an HQ.

SetInside.doc: Sets whether the player is inside an HQ.

SetUnloadCallback.doc: Sets a callback function and arguments to be called when the module unloads.

GetUnloadCallback.doc: Retrieves the unload callback function and its arguments.

MrxLayerManager.doc: Loads and unloads named layers of level geometry - the mechanism behind every 'the world changed because of something you did' moment (a base destroyed, an outpost captured, a story chapter swapping a region's geometry). Missions and WifMissionFlow simply tell this module which named layers should exist right now. Like every resident module it must be pulled in with import("MrxLayerManager") before use; calling it cold fails with "attempt to index global 'MrxLayerManager' (a nil value)".

Init.doc: Stores Sys.GetAssetRequestMax() at startup (_knOrigAssetRequestMax) so it can be restored later once the operation queue drains.

Add.doc: The immediate "load this layer now" entry point - a thin wrapper over _AddRequest(_knRequestTypeAdd, ...). vLayers accepts either a single layer-name string or a table of them.
Add.sig: MrxLayerManager.Add(vLayers, fCallback, tCallbackArgs, bCullDupes, bStatic, bClientNeedsLoadingScreen)
Add.gotcha: Use this, not MarkForAddition, when you want the layer to load right now - MarkForAddition only stages the change until ProcessMarkedLayers runs.

Remove.doc: The immediate "unload this layer now" entry point. vLayers accepts either a single layer-name string or a table of them.
Remove.gotcha: Confirmed bug: it forwards only four arguments to _AddRequest, so bClientNeedsLoadingScreen lands in the bCullDupes slot - Remove can never show a client loading screen no matter what you pass.

RemoveDynamicLayers.doc: Convenience wrapper that removes every currently-loaded dynamic layer by walking _tLoadedLayers.

RemoveAllLayers.doc: Removes every currently-loaded dynamic layer and, alongside them, a caller-supplied list of static layers. The bulk teardown counterpart to RemoveDynamicLayers.
RemoveAllLayers.gotcha: It does local tLayers = tStaticLayers and then table.inserts every loaded dynamic layer into that same table, mutating your argument in place - copy it first (MrxUtil.CopyTable) if you intend to reuse it.

MarkForRemoval.doc: Stages a layer (or table of layers) for unloading, lowercasing every name first, and cancels any previously-staged addition of the same name. Nothing unloads until ProcessMarkedLayers runs.
MarkForRemoval.gotcha: It does not unload anything by itself - the change only takes effect when ProcessMarkedLayers() is separately called. Use Remove for an immediate unload.

MarkForAddition.doc: Stages a layer (or table of layers) for loading, lowercasing every name first, and cancels any previously-staged removal of the same name. Nothing loads until ProcessMarkedLayers runs.
MarkForAddition.gotcha: It does not load anything by itself - calling MarkForAddition({"my_layer"}) alone changes nothing visible until ProcessMarkedLayers() is separately called. Use Add for an immediate load.

RemoveMarkedLayers.doc: Collects every layer name currently flagged true in _tLoadedLayers (i.e. marked for removal) and calls the real Remove() on all of them at once.

ProcessMarkedLayers.doc: Commits everything staged by MarkForRemoval/MarkForAddition. Two-phase and strictly sequential - removals first, then additions, never both at once.
ProcessMarkedLayers.gotcha: If you want a layer to appear or disappear immediately and reliably from your own script, call Add/Remove directly rather than relying on MarkForAddition/MarkForRemoval plus this.

_AddRequest.doc: The real entry point behind both Add and Remove. For every requested layer name (lowercased first): - Culls it if Sys.GetIgnoreLayers() exists and lists that name (logged, not an error). - Checks Pg.AssetExists(sLayerName, "layer") — a nonexistent layer name is silently culled and logged, never an error or crash.
_AddRequest.sig: MrxLayerManager._AddRequest(nRequestType, vLayers, fCallback, tCallbackArgs, bCullDupes, bStatic, bClientNeedsLoadingScreen)

_ProcessOpQueue.doc: The throttled worker loop. Only _knLayersToProcessCap (10) layer load/unload operations run concurrently — once that many are in flight, this function just returns early on each call and relies on _LayerStatusChange (below) to re-invoke it as operations complete, until the queue drains.

_LayerStatusChange.doc: The native completion callback. Updates _tLoadedLayers (adds get false — loaded, not marked for removal; removes get cleared to nil), decrements the in-flight counter, tallies completion against every tRequest that included this layer, and — only once a request's nDone reaches its nQuota (every layer in that original Add/Remove call has finished) — queues that request's callback to fire.

SaveSingleton.doc: Returns the save payload for this subsystem: every currently-loaded dynamic layer not marked for removal, plus anything staged-but-not-yet-loaded in _tLayersToBeAdded.

LoadSingleton.doc: Restores the saved layer set: diffs it against whatever is actually loaded via FindLayerIntersection, then reconciles with a single Remove(toRemove, ...) followed by Add(toAdd, ...).
LoadSingleton.gotcha: A layer your mod force-adds live does not persist across a save/reload by itself - nothing here writes that choice into tSaveData, so re-apply it on every load.

ResetState.doc: Wipes all four tracking tables to empty — presumably called on a fresh game/level start.

FindLayerIntersection.doc: A classic sorted two-pointer merge-diff between two layer-name lists (tR = currently loaded, tA = saved target state): returns (tRemoveList, tAddList) — layers only in tR need removing, layers only in tA need adding, layers in both stay untouched. Generic enough to reuse for any two layer-name-list reconciliation, not SaveSingleton/LoadSingleton-specific.

MrxMusic.doc: Owns dynamic music state: faction and freeplay music cue tables, action-level transitions, special music (fanfares, hijack stings, misc cues) and multiplayer sync of the music context via custom net events. It drives the engine Sound music API; the higher-level MrxSound facade is what normally calls into it. Like every resident module it must be pulled in with import("MrxMusic") before use; calling it cold fails with "attempt to index global 'MrxMusic' (a nil value)".

_DisableDynamicMusic.doc: Saves Sound.IsDynamicMusic() into _bPrevDynamic, then disables dynamic music.

_RestoreDynamicMusic.doc: Restores dynamic music to whatever _bPrevDynamic holds.

SetMusicActionInterval.doc: Sets _fActionInterval if fActionInterval >= 0; otherwise logs a Debug.Printf warning and leaves the existing value unchanged.

BindMusicCue.doc: Requires 0 < iCueIndex < 4. Searches all of _tMusicCues (both factions and freeplay categories) for a matching faction/state pair and overwrites cueTable[iCueIndex] = sCue.

_InitializeMusic.doc: Top-level setup, expected to run once. For every faction in _tMusicCues.factions, calls _InitializeFaction then _BindMusicStateCues.

SendPlayerJoinEvents.doc: Sends catch-up net events to a newly joined player: NETEVENT_ENTERCONTRACT with {sFaction} if the bare global sFaction is truthy, else NETEVENT_ENTERFREEPLAY. Then NETEVENT_PLAYSPECIALMUSIC with {_sCurrentMusicCue} if _sCurrentMusicCue is set, else NETEVENT_STOPSPECIALMUSIC with {_sStopSpecialMusicCue or "silence", 0}.
SendPlayerJoinEvents.gotcha: Likely bug: the sFaction checked at the top of this function (no leading underscore) is never assigned anywhere in this file — _sCurrentContractFaction is the variable actually set by EnterContractMusic/EnterFreeplayMusic. As written, sFaction reads as an always-nil global, so the NETEVENT_ENTERCONTRACT branch is dead code and this function always tells a joining player they're in freeplay, even mid-contract.

_InitializeFaction.doc: Registers a full faction music state machine via Sound.AddFactionMusic/AddMusicState/SetActionThresholdsMusic/AddMusicTransition calls: states none, explore, action, mission_success, mission_failure, hijack, hijack_success, hijack_success_resume, source, shell, misc1, misc2, pause, silence, plus transitions between them (none↔explore, explore→action, hijack_success→explore/hijack_success_resume, etc.).

_InitializeFreeplay.doc: Same as _InitializeFaction but also registers a high_action state and its transitions (none/explore/source/action ↔ high_action) — the escalation level that factions don't have.

_BindMusicStateCues.doc: Calls Sound.SetFactionMusic(sFaction), then for every state/cue-list pair in tCues, calls Sound.BindMusicCue(cue, state) for each cue in the list.

Reset.doc: Re-enables dynamic music (Sound.SetDynamicMusic(true), resets _bPrevDynamic to true), calls _CleanupSpecialMusic(), clears faction lock (_bPrevFactionLock = false, Sound.LockFactionMusic(false)), and resets action-level music (Sound.SetActionLevelsMusic(0,0,0,0), Sound.LockActionLevelMusic(false)).

EnterFreeplayMusic.doc: Logs via Debug.Printf, calls Reset(), activates faction-region music, transitions to "explore". If server: clears _sCurrentContractFaction and sends NETEVENT_ENTERFREEPLAY.

EnterContractMusic.doc: Logs via Debug.Printf, sets/locks faction music to sFaction, transitions to "explore". If server: sets _sCurrentContractFaction = sFaction and sends NETEVENT_ENTERCONTRACT with {sFaction}.

PlayFanfare.doc: Cleans up any special music, then force-transitions the music state to "mission_success" or "mission_failure" depending on bMissionSuccess. Use it for the sting at the end of a mission.

PlaySpecialMusic.doc: Locks out the dynamic faction music and plays a one-off cue: it saves the current faction-lock state, advances the misc-music slot, rebinds that slot to sMusicCue and transitions to it. On the server it also records the cue and broadcasts NETEVENT_PLAYSPECIALMUSIC so clients follow.
PlaySpecialMusic.gotcha: Pair it with StopSpecialMusic - until you do, dynamic faction music stays locked out.

_SetMiscMusicIndex.doc: Toggles _iCurrentMiscMusicIndex between the two _tMiscMusicStates slots: if currently > 1 (i.e. 2), decrements to 1; otherwise increments (covers both the initial 0 and the 1 case, both becoming/staying 1 then 2 on alternating calls — net effect is it alternates 1, 2, 1, 2, ... once started from 0).

_ResumeSpecialMusic.doc: If _bPlayingSpecialMusic, re-transitions to the current misc music slot (_tMiscMusicStates[_iCurrentMiscMusicIndex]).

StopSpecialMusic.doc: Ends the special-music mode started by PlaySpecialMusic, transitioning to sNewState if given and "none" otherwise, and broadcasting NETEVENT_STOPSPECIALMUSIC from the server so clients follow.
StopSpecialMusic.gotcha: Does nothing at all unless special music is actually playing (_bPlayingSpecialMusic).

_CleanupSpecialMusic.doc: If _bPlayingSpecialMusic: restores faction lock to _bPrevFactionLock, resets _iCurrentMiscMusicIndex to 0, sets _bPlayingSpecialMusic = false. If server: clears _sCurrentMusicCue, sends NETEVENT_STOPSPECIALMUSIC with {sNewState or "none", 1}.
_CleanupSpecialMusic.gotcha: Likely bug: _CleanupSpecialMusic takes no parameters and has no local sNewState. It references a bare global sNewState that is never assigned anywhere in this file — StopSpecialMusic's parameter of the same name is a *different*, function-local variable and isn't visible here (this codebase's Lua has no closures capturing sibling-call locals that way).

GetFactionByStringHash.doc: Searches every category/faction key in _tMusicCues for one whose String.GetHash(faction) matches. Returns the faction name string, or nil if none match.

GetStateByStringHash.doc: Searches every category/faction/state key in _tMusicCues for one whose String.GetHash(state) matches. Returns the state name string, or "silence" if none match (unlike GetFactionByStringHash, which returns nil on no match — different fallback conventions between the two).

NetEventCallback.doc: Dispatches on nEventType (one of the four NETEVENT_* constants): calls EnterFreeplayMusic(); or resolves tArgs[1] via GetFactionByStringHash and calls EnterContractMusic(sFaction) (asserting via ASSERT(0, ...) if the hash doesn't resolve); or calls PlaySpecialMusic(tArgs[1]); or resolves tArgs[1] via GetStateByStringHash and calls either _CleanupSpecialMusic() (if tArgs[2] == 1) or StopSpecialMusic(sNewState).

MrxPmc.doc: Owns the player's PMC economy - cash, fuel and fuel capacity, support-item stockpile, freebies and equipment - and keeps the HUD in sync when any of it changes. This is the module to use for giving/taking resources, because the lower-level Player.* calls change the value without refreshing the on-screen number. Like every resident module it must be pulled in with import("MrxPmc") before use; calling it cold fails with "attempt to index global 'MrxPmc' (a nil value)".

Init.doc: Initializes the player's economy by setting the initial fuel capacity to _knMinFuelCapacity and creating a high-score event.

AddCashQty.doc: Adds cash to the player's total and refreshes the HUD, posts the CashAdded event and reports the delta to MrxStatsManager. Both the per-call amount and the resulting total are clamped to a 1,000,000,000 ceiling and floored at 0, so you cannot go negative through this call.
AddCashQty.gotcha: Prefer this over the lower-level Player.AddCash, which changes the real value but skips the HUD-refresh trigger, so the on-screen number will not visibly update.

GetCashQty.doc: Returns the player's current cash total. The read counterpart to AddCashQty.

GetFuelQty.doc: Returns the current fuel amount — a thin wrapper over Player.GetFuel(). Confirmed working by live testing (see Snippets).

AddFuelQty.doc: Adds fuel to the player's total, clamped between zero and the current fuel capacity, and triggers the low-fuel / no-fuel tutorials as appropriate. Confirmed working with the HUD updating.
AddFuelQty.gotcha: The amount is capped at the current capacity - if you want more than the default maximum, raise the ceiling first with SetFuelCapacity.

SetFuelCapacity.doc: Sets the player's fuel capacity to a specified value, ensuring it is within the allowed range (_knMinFuelCapacity to _knMaxFuelCapacity). If bDoNotSyncFuel is false and the current fuel exceeds the new capacity, it adjusts the fuel accordingly.

AddFuelCapacity.doc: Adds a specified amount to the player's fuel capacity. If the resulting capacity exceeds the maximum or falls below the minimum, it sets the capacity to the respective limit.

GetFuelCapacity.doc: Returns the current fuel capacity of the player.

AddSupportQty.doc: Adds a quantity of a support item to the stockpile, updating client-side spending data, firing the unlock fanfare if asked, checking support thresholds and refreshing mission details. sName keys come from MrxSupportData.tSupportData.

SetSupportQty.doc: Sets the quantity of a specific support item in the stockpile.

GetSupportQty.doc: Returns the quantity of a specific support item in the stockpile. Used alongside AddSupportQty and tData.nMaxStock (from MrxSupportData) to compute "how much more to add to max this item out" — see the "The Works!" snippet linked above.

SetSupportNew.doc: Marks a specific support item as new or viewed.

SetAllSupportViewed.doc: Marks all support items as viewed.

IsSupportNew.doc: Checks if a specific support item is marked as new.

CheckSupportThreshold.doc: Checks if the quantity of a specific support item meets any set thresholds and triggers callbacks accordingly.

SetStockpileChangeCallback.doc: Sets a callback function to be triggered when the quantity of a specific support item meets a specified threshold.

DeleteStockpileChangeCallback.doc: Deletes a previously set stockpile change callback by its ID.

AddFreebieQty.doc: Adds a specified amount of freebies to the player's inventory.

SetFreebieQty.doc: Sets the quantity of a specific freebie in the player's inventory.

GetFreebieQty.doc: Returns the quantity of a specific freebie in the player's inventory.

AddEquipment.doc: Adds an equipment item to the player's inventory. If the item is a fuel tank it may also raise the fuel capacity and spawn the corresponding world object, unless bDoNotAddCapacity is set.

RemoveEquipment.doc: Removes a specified equipment item from the player's inventory. If it is a fuel tank, it adjusts the fuel capacity and removes the corresponding object from the world.

HasEquipment.doc: Checks if the player has a specific equipment item in their inventory.

DisplayCash.doc: Updates the HUD to display the current cash amount, the reason for the change, and the change itself.

MapPluralReasonToSingular.doc: Maps a plural reason to its singular form using the _tPluralReasonToSingular table.

DisplayResources.doc: Updates the HUD to display both the current cash and fuel amounts, as well as any changes.

AddFuelTank.doc: Adds a fuel tank to the player's inventory. If bModifyCapacity is true, it adjusts the fuel capacity accordingly.

RemoveFuelTank.doc: Removes a fuel tank from the player's inventory, adjusting the fuel capacity and removing the corresponding object from the world.

_OnFuelTankDeath.doc: Handles the death of a fuel tank by adjusting the fuel capacity and updating internal state.

GetClientReimburseAmount.doc: Calculates the amount to reimburse the client based on their support spendings and remaining stockpile items.

NetClientReimburse.doc: Reimburses the client with the calculated amount and displays a message in the HUD.

_CreateHiScoreEvent.doc: Creates a dummy widget to handle high-score events and updates the leaderboard accordingly.

_HiScoreUpdated.doc: Handles the update of the leaderboard by displaying a fanfare event.

SaveSingleton.doc: This function saves the current state of the player's PMC resources and equipment. It retrieves the player's cash, fuel, and equipment status, then constructs a table containing this information.

LoadSingleton.doc: This function loads the player's PMC resources and equipment from a previously saved state. It takes a table tSaveData as an argument, which should contain the saved game state.

MrxRewardData.doc: Holds the reward tables for missions, contracts and milestones and dispenses them - cash, fuel, faction mood, support items, equipment and stockpile - plus custom rewards and wager data. It also formats human-readable reward strings for the UI. Like every resident module it must be pulled in with import("MrxRewardData") before use; calling it cold fails with "attempt to index global 'MrxRewardData' (a nil value)".

Init.doc: Initializes the reward data by iterating through each reward entry in _tRewards. For each reward, it sets the mission ID and faction ID based on the reward key.

GetRewards.doc: Retrieves the reward data associated with the given sRewardKey from _tRewards.

GetAllPotentialShopItems.doc: Generates lists of potential support and equipment items that can be sold in shops for a specific faction. It caches these lists in gtAllSupport and gtAllEquipment to avoid redundant calculations.

DispenseRewards.doc: Dispenses the rewards specified in tRewards. This includes adding cash and fuel to the player's PMC account, changing faction attitudes, unlocking support and equipment items, and updating stockpile quantities.

DispenseAllRewards.doc: Walks every entry in _tRewards and dispenses it with fanfares disabled - in practice a mass grant of cash, fuel, faction reputation and shop-item unlocks in one call. Confirmed working by live testing.

GetRewardKeyFromHash.doc: Retrieves the reward key associated with a given hash value from _tRewards.

NetEventCallback.doc: Handles network events. If the event ID matches EVENT_GRANTREWARDKEY, it retrieves the reward key and calls GrantRewardKey to grant the reward.

GrantRewardKey.doc: Grants the reward associated with sRewardKey. On the server, it sends a custom network event to clients.

EnableCashRewardHalving.doc: Enables or disables halving of cash rewards based on the boolean value bEnable.

SaveSingleton.doc: Saves the wager data for each reward in _tRewards to a table tSaveData. Only rewards with a wager are saved.

LoadSingleton.doc: Loads the wager data from tSaveData into _tRewards, updating the corresponding entries.

GetWagerData.doc: Calculates and returns the wager data for the given reward. It computes the wager amount based on the player's current cash, the reward's percentage-based wager, and any minimum or maximum wager constraints.

GenerateRewardString.doc: Generates a string representation of the rewards associated with a specific mission ID. This includes cash, fuel, support items, equipment items, stockpile quantities, and custom rewards.

AddCustomReward.doc: Adds a custom reward to the list of rewards for a specific mission ID.

_GenerateStringFromRewardData.doc: Generates a string representation of the reward data. It formats each type of reward (cash, fuel, support, equipment, stockpile) into a readable string and appends any custom strings provided.

_GetPrintableSupportString.doc: This function takes a support ID (sSupportId) and returns a printable string representation of the support. It retrieves the support data from MrxSupportData.tSupportData using the provided ID.

_GetPrintableEquipmentString.doc: This function takes an equipment ID (sEquipId) and returns a printable string representation of the equipment. It retrieves the equipment data using WifEquipmentData.GetEquipmentData(sEquipId).

_FormatMilestoneString.doc: This function formats a milestone string based on the provided milestone data (tMilestoneData). It extracts the milestone number and key from tMilestoneData, retrieves the corresponding reward data using GetRewards(sMilestoneKey).

_FormatMilestoneSuffix.doc: This function formats a milestone suffix by appending a number to a given suffix. It checks if both sSuffix is a string and nNumber is a number.

_FormatLevelMilestoneString.doc: This function formats a level milestone string based on the provided milestone data (tMilestoneData). It extracts the milestone key from tMilestoneData, retrieves the corresponding reward data using GetRewards(sMilestoneKey).

MrxState.doc: Manages global game-state transitions and their lifecycle - fades, player-input suppression and the coordination of states such as cinematic, streaming, tethering and game-ready. States are reference-counted, so every Enter needs a matching Exit. Like every resident module it must be pulled in with import("MrxState") before use; calling it cold fails with "attempt to index global 'MrxState' (a nil value)".

_GlobalEnter.doc: Handles the global enter transition by fading out, ducking audio, suppressing player input, and setting characters invincible. Logs ###!

_GlobalExit.doc: Handles the global exit transition by fading in, restoring player input, and running global-exit callbacks. Logs ###!

Reset.doc: Resets various internal flags and callback tables to their initial states.

_StateComplete.doc: Completes a state transition by calling the state's exit function and attempting a global exit if all states are exited. Logs detailed debug information about the state completion process.

Enter.doc: Increments _States[nState].nRefCount and enters/re-enters the state. Returns false for an unknown nState.
Enter.gotcha: Worth knowing before wrapping this function heavily or calling it in a tight loop — it's a real, if minor, per-call cost, and it's the highest-frequency function in this file to log through if you're also bracketing it with your own diagnostic wrapper for an unrelated investigation (stacking enough hooks near Enter/Exit was one contributing factor in a real crash encountered while debugging a separate briefing-flow issue — see the Custom Contract deep dive).

_CompleteEnter.doc: Completes the enter transition by calling the state's enter function and processing any queued enter callbacks. Logs ###!

Exit.doc: Decrements _States[nState].nRefCount. Unpaired-exit guard: if the refcount is already <= 0, it logs "UNPAIRED EXIT to state <NAME>", calls fCallback immediately, and returns false without decrementing — so an over-Exit is a no-op with a warning, not an underflow.
Exit.gotcha: Confirmed: also calls Debug.Printf(Debug.GetCallstack()) unconditionally on every call, both the normal case and the "unpaired exit" warning case — same caution as Enter above.

_AttemptGlobalExit.doc: Attempts to perform a global exit if no states are active and the game is not globally locked. Logs detailed debug information about the attempt.

_GetTotalRefCount.doc: Returns the total reference count across all states.

IsLocked.doc: Checks if the game is globally locked.

SetQuickFade.doc: Enables or disables quick fading effects.

EnableFade.doc: Enables or disables global fade effects.

PrintStatus.doc: Logs the current status of all states, indicating which are active.

GetStateName.doc: Returns the name of a specified state.

SafeEnter.doc: Deferred-exit wrapper around Enter for the case where an Exit might arrive before its matching Enter has finished: calls Enter(nState, SafeEnterCallback, {nState}). Use SafeEnter/SafeExit instead of raw Enter/Exit when the ordering is not guaranteed.

SafeEnterCallback.doc: The completion callback SafeEnter hands to Enter: it increments the state's safeEnterCount and pays down any forceExitCount that SafeExit accrued while the enter was still in flight.

SafeExit.doc: Either consumes one pending safe-enter (decrement safeEnterCount plus a real Exit) or, if none is pending yet, increments forceExitCount - a "you owe me an exit" tally that SafeEnterCallback pays down as safe-enters complete.

AddGlobalExitCallback.doc: Registers a callback to fire on the next global exit. If the game is not currently _bGloballyLocked, it runs the callback immediately instead of queuing it — confirmed used by MrxTaskContract.AssetsLoaded to run a contract's Activated right after its assets finish loading, whether or not a load transition is in flight.

MrxSupportData.doc: Owns the catalog of every purchasable support item in the game (supply drops, vehicles, airstrikes) plus per-faction unlock, freebie and recruit-requirement tracking. Its tSupportData table is what cheat/shop code iterates over to enumerate support items. Like every resident module it must be pulled in with import("MrxSupportData") before use; calling it cold fails with "attempt to index global 'MrxSupportData' (a nil value)".

IsSupportEquippable.doc: Checks if a support item is equippable based on its key (sKey). Considers whether the recruit requirement has been met and any additional optional requirements.
